IFSP – Programa de Intervención Temprana para Infantes y Niños Pequeños de NC (NC ITP)
Revisión de IFSP – Informe de progreso trimestral – Formato SOAP

CDSA de la Región Piedmont
210 Avenida Mills, Burlington, Condado de Alamance, 27215
Tel. (336) 555-0142 | Fax (336) 555-0199

Fecha de la revisión: 12 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 3 de marzo de 2026
Próxima revisión programada: 12 de abril de 2027

Niño: Mateo Isaías Hernández Rodríguez (apodo "Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de enero de 2024
Edad cronológica: 2;9
Edad gestacional al nacer: 38 semanas
Peso al nacer: 3,100 gramos
ID del niño (CDSA): AT-884512
ID de Medicaid: 934217865B

Madre/Guardiana: Lucía Rodríguez
Padre/Guardián: Jorge Hernández
Domicilio: 742 Calle Roble, Burlington, Condado de Alamance, 27215
Tel. madre: (336) 555-0187 | Tel. padre: (336) 555-0233
Correo de contacto: lucia.rodriguez84@gmail.com

Coordinadora de servicios: Alicia Fernández, CDSA de la Región Piedmont
Patóloga del habla-lenguaje: Marisol Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP — Pediatric Therapy Partners, LLC
Pediatra remitente: Dr. Kevin Walsh
Hospital de nacimiento: Hospital Regional de Alamance

S:
Mamá, Lucía Rodríguez, refiere en sus propias palabras: "Teo entiende casi todo lo que le decimos pero no nos dice lo que quiere, solo señala y hace sonidos como 'eh-eh'." Agrega: "En la casa le hablamos mitad en español mitad en inglés, y a veces se frustra porque no le entendemos." Papá, Jorge Hernández, comenta: "Cuando quiere algo jala la ropa y grita, no usa palabras." Ambos padres reportan que Teo dice aprox. 8 palabras funcionales ("mamá", "papá", "agua", "más", "no", "pan", "oso", "arriba") y no combina palabras.

Hx fam/social: la familia vive con la abuela materna, a quien Teo llama "abuela Lupe" (doña Lupe), quien cuida a Teo y a su hermana mayor, Valentina Hernández Rodríguez ("Vale", 4;6), tres días a la semana mientras los padres trabajan. Mamá trabaja de lunes a viernes en el turno de la mañana en Smithfield Packing Plant, una planta empacadora; papá trabaja de lunes a sábado en Construcciones Rivera, una compañía de construcción. Tía materna, Rosa Gómez, trabaja de noche en El Jardín Restaurant y ayuda algunos fines de semana. Doña Lupe también cuidó antes en una granja familiar en Mebane antes de mudarse con la familia.

Rutina diaria: Teo se despierta aprox. a las 6:30 a.m., desayuna con la abuela, y es llevado a la guardería Centro de Cuidado Pequeños Pasos de 8:00 a.m. a 3:00 p.m. los días que mamá y papá trabajan. Ahí su maestra es la maestra Carmen y el asistente es Mr. Tom. Teo juega con sus compañeros Emma y Liam, y le gusta imitar a su primo Pepe y a su primo Juanito cuando visitan los domingos. La niñera ocasional, Miss Ana, lo cuida algunos sábados cuando doña Lupe no puede. La familia tiene un perrito llamado Rocky, y mamá dice que Teo se emociona mucho y grita "¡guau, guau!" cuando ve a Rocky.

Mamá refiere que la familia recibe apoyo de WIC para nutrición y está inscrita en Smart Start del condado para actividades de alfabetización familiar. También tienen un caso abierto con DSS del Condado de Alamance por servicios de vivienda, no relacionado con seguridad.

Preocupaciones y prioridades de la familia: 1) que Teo pueda decir lo que quiere sin frustrarse; 2) que entienda instrucciones de dos pasos en ambos idiomas; 3) que se pueda comunicar con su hermana Vale y con sus primos Pepe y Juanito durante el juego; 4) preparación para ingresar a preescolar el próximo año.

O:
Horario de sesiones (terapia de habla-lenguaje, EI a domicilio y en guardería):

| Día | Hora inicio | Hora fin | Lugar |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lunes | 9:00 a.m. | 9:45 a.m. | Centro de Cuidado Pequeños Pasos |
| Miércoles | 4:00 p.m. | 4:45 p.m. | domicilio, 742 Calle Roble |
| Viernes | 9:00 a.m. | 9:45 a.m. | Centro de Cuidado Pequeños Pasos |

Evaluación formal administrada 28 de septiembre de 2026 por Marisol Ortiz con intérprete Daniela Soto presente para verificación con la familia.

Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5) — Spanish/English bilingual norms:
- Auditory Comprehension: puntaje estándar 76 (percentil 5), IC 90%: 70-82
- Expressive Communication: puntaje estándar 68 (percentil 2), IC 90%: 62-74
- Edad equivalente expresiva: 14 meses

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale: rango global de edad equivalente 16-18 meses en todos los dominios excepto interacción-apego, que fue de 24 meses.

Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (15 min, guardería): Teo produjo 8 palabras diferentes en la sesión, 0 combinaciones de dos palabras. Produjo "más" y "pan" espontáneamente cuando vio a Liam comer galletas. Imitó "arriba" con mod cues (modelo + gesto).

Fonética/fonología: inventario consonántico limitado a /m, p, b, n, t/. Omite consonantes finales y sustituye velares por alveolares, ej. "dato" por "gato". No se observan distorsiones de /ɾ/ ni de [w] por ser aún muy temprano para esos sonidos a su edad.

Comprensión de instrucciones: siguió 3 de 5 instrucciones de un paso con min cues (gesto); 0 de 5 instrucciones de dos pasos incluso con max cues.

Juego e interacción social: inicia juego funcional simple (empujar carrito, dar de comer a muñeco). Observado compartir juguete con Emma sin indicación verbal, solo gesto. Protodeclarativos presentes; protoimperativos predominan.

Pragmática/interacción: contacto visual adecuado, toma turnos en juego motor con adulto 8/10 oportunidades. Rechaza actividad no deseada empujando el objeto o llorando, sin señalar aún de forma consistente.

Audición y estructura oral: cribado auditivo pasado 10 de marzo de 2026. Estructura oral dentro de límites normales; sin hallazgos de hipotonía orofacial. Apgar 8/9 al nacer, sin complicaciones perinatales reportadas.

A:
Teo presenta un retraso significativo del lenguaje expresivo y receptivo en ambos idiomas (español e inglés), consistente con retraso global de la comunicación más que con un perfil específico de un solo idioma; no hay evidencia de que la exposición bilingüe sea la causa del retraso. El perfil fonológico es consistente con la edad de desarrollo observada, con procesos típicos de simplificación (omisión final, frontalización velar) que se espera resuelvan con intervención dirigida y no indican un trastorno motor del habla.

Diagnóstico de trabajo: Trastorno del Lenguaje, de inicio en la niñez temprana (ICD-10 F80.9). Código de servicio facturado: CPT 92523, modificador GN.

Resultados del IFSP (continuación y actualización):

Resultado 1 (continuado): Teo usará al menos 25 palabras nuevas de forma espontánea en ambos idiomas para pedir objetos y actividades preferidas. Estrategia: modelado expansivo bilingüe, tiempo de espera de 5 segundos, uso de PECS como apoyo visual transicional durante rutinas de guardería y domicilio. Progreso: parcial; aumentó de 3 a 8 palabras desde la revisión anterior.

Resultado 2 (nuevo): Teo seguirá instrucciones de un paso familiares sin apoyo gestual en el 80% de las oportunidades en ambos idiomas. Estrategia: enfoque Hanen (It Takes Two to Talk) para entrenamiento de los padres y la abuela Lupe en estrategias de seguimiento del niño ("follow the child's lead") durante rutinas de comida y baño.

Resultado 3 (continuado): Teo iniciará interacción comunicativa con compañeros (ej. Emma, Liam) usando un gesto convencional (señalar, dar) en lugar de empujar o llorar, en el 70% de las oportunidades observadas en guardería. Estrategia: Marisol Ortiz entrenará a la maestra Carmen y a Mr. Tom en estrategias de espera estructurada y refuerzo de gestos comunicativos durante el juego libre.

Resultado 4 (nuevo, familia): la familia reportará mayor confianza al apoyar el desarrollo del lenguaje de Teo en casa, incluyendo a doña Lupe, usando estrategias de lenguaje dual sin eliminar ninguno de los dos idiomas. Estrategia: sesiones de coaching domiciliario mensual con materiales bilingües; se incluirá a Vale como modelo de lenguaje entre hermanos durante el juego dirigido.

Factores contextuales considerados: exposición bilingüe en casa (español predominante con abuela, mixto con padres), participación irregular de doña Lupe los fines de semana cuando trabaja la tía Rosa Gómez, y variabilidad en el horario laboral de los padres en Smithfield Packing Plant y Construcciones Rivera, que pueden afectar la consistencia de la práctica en casa.

P:
1. Continuar terapia de habla-lenguaje bilingüe directa, 2x/semana, 45 min por sesión, según el horario indicado arriba, iniciando 19 de octubre de 2026.
2. Añadir coaching domiciliario mensual (60 min) con la familia y doña Lupe, primera sesión 26 de octubre de 2026.
3. Consulta de colaboración con la maestra Carmen y Mr. Tom en Centro de Cuidado Pequeños Pasos, programada para 2 de noviembre de 2026.
4. Referido a evaluación de audición completa con audiólogo si no hay progreso en resultado 2 para 12 de abril de 2027.
5. Coordinación continua con Alicia Fernández (CDSA de la Región Piedmont) para seguimiento de elegibilidad y revisión del IFSP cada seis meses.
6. Próxima revisión formal del IFSP: 12 de abril de 2027. Revisión de progreso intermedia por teléfono: 15 de enero de 2027, tel. madre (336) 555-0187.
7. Autorización de servicios válida hasta 30 de septiembre de 2027 bajo ID de Medicaid 934217865B.

Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Center, PLLC
2214 Chapel Hill Road, Mebane, NC 27302
Phone: (919) 555-0148 | Fax: (919) 555-0149
Email: intake@carolinabilingualslp.com

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez (called Teo by family)
Date of Birth: August 2, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Date of Evaluation: October 2, 2026
Date of Report: October 9, 2026
Record/Case ID: LD-2026-00482
Medicaid ID: 487205613A
Primary Language of Home: Spanish and English
Address: 1428 Willow Bend Lane, Mebane, NC 27302
Home Phone: (919) 555-0231
Mother's Cell: (919) 555-0294
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Rodríguez (madre) and Diego Flores (padre)
Referral Source: Dr. James Whitfield, pediatrician, Alamance Pediatric Associates
Evaluator: Mariana Castillo-Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist
Interpreter Present: Carmen Ibarra, Spanish-English medical interpreter
Service Coordinator: Brenda Walsh, Alamance-Caswell Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA)

2. REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred by Dr. Whitfield after his eighteen-month and three-year well-child checks flagged limited expressive vocabulary and unclear speech in both English and Spanish. His mother, Lucía, reports, "no entendemos casi nada de lo que dice en casa" ("we understand almost nothing he says at home"), and his teacher, Ms. Lopez, noted similar concerns at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. The family was connected to this clinic through CDSA following an initial screening coordinated by Brenda Walsh. This comprehensive bilingual evaluation was requested to determine eligibility for ongoing speech-language intervention and to inform his upcoming IFSP review.

3. BACKGROUND INFORMATION / HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO

Background information was gathered through parent interview, conducted in Spanish with support from interpreter Carmen Ibarra, review of records from UNC Health Alamance, and a questionnaire completed by Lucía Rodríguez and Diego Flores.

3.1 Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 39 weeks gestational age via scheduled cesarean section at UNC Health Alamance on August 2, 2022. Birth weight was 7 lbs 4 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. No complications were reported during pregnancy or delivery. Lucía reported that Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening and has had no ear infections requiring tubes, though he had two episodes of otitis media treated with amoxicillin around 18 months and 22 months of age. A hearing re-screening completed by audiologist Dr. Sandra Kim on September 18, 2026 showed results within normal limits bilaterally. Mateo's developmental milestones were reported as follows: sat independently at 6 months, walked at 13 months, and first words ("mamá," "agua") emerged around 14 months. His parents note that word combinations did not appear until closer to 3;0, considerably later than his older sister, Sol, who they describe as "muy habladora desde chiquita" (very talkative from a young age).

Mateo's medical history is otherwise unremarkable. He is up to date on immunizations per his pediatrician, Dr. Whitfield, and has no diagnosed genetic syndromes, seizure history, or significant illnesses. He takes no current medications. The family dog, Max, is frequently mentioned by Mateo in session, and he often says "[EW] Max afuera" when requesting to let the dog outside, a phrase his mother confirmed is a stable routine request at home.

3.2 Family and Language History

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Diego Flores; his older sister, Sol, age 7; and his maternal aunt, Rosa Hernández, who provides childcare three days a week while Lucía works. Lucía is employed part-time at Food Lion on Trollinger Road, and Diego works full-time as a foreman for Pinnacle Construction Group. The family's maternal grandmother, Esperanza Rodríguez, visits frequently from out of state and speaks only Spanish with Mateo.

The home language environment is predominantly Spanish, with Lucía and Rosa estimated at roughly 80% Spanish input, while Diego and Sol code-switch more frequently, estimated at closer to 50% Spanish and 50% English. Lucía described Mateo's early language exposure: "en casa hablamos puro español, pero con su hermana Sol él escucha mucho inglés de la tele y de la escuela." Diego added, "yo le hablo en los dos, a veces se me sale el inglés sin querer." Both parents report that Mateo understands routine directions better in Spanish but has begun producing more English vocabulary since starting at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center in January 2026.

Lucía described her concern plainly: "lo que más me preocupa es que ni su maestra ni su prima lo entienden cuando habla" (what worries me most is that neither his teacher nor his cousin understand him when he talks). His cousin, Will Hernández, son of Rosa, is close in age and the two play together most weekends, but Lucía reports Will frequently asks her to "translate" what Mateo is trying to say.

3.3 Educational History

Mateo has attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, located at 905 Spring Garden Court, Mebane, since January 2026, five days a week from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.. He is enrolled in Ms. Lopez's room, the "Sunflower Room," alongside sixteen other children. Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo is social and eager to participate but is frequently misunderstood by peers, including his best friend at school, Noah, and classmate Jazmín. The assistant teacher, Mr. Daniels, echoed similar concerns in a brief phone consultation on September 25, 2026. Prior to Little Sprouts, Mateo attended a part-time Early Head Start classroom through Alamance County from August 2023 to December 2025, where he was first flagged for a speech-language referral.

4. AGENCIES AND SERVICES INVOLVED

The family has been connected with multiple community agencies to support Mateo's development and the family's broader needs. The Alamance-Caswell Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA) office, through service coordinator Brenda Walsh, manages Mateo's IFSP and coordinates referrals. The family also receives support from Alamance County DSS for supplemental nutrition benefits, and Lucía has participated in WIC appointments monthly since Mateo's infancy. Smart Start of Alamance County provided a home-visiting parent coach, Teresa Owens, who visited biweekly from March 2024 to June 2025 to support early literacy routines.

Additionally, the family was connected by Teresa Owens to the Asociación de Padres Hispanos para el Desarrollo Infantil (APHDI), a community organization serving Spanish-speaking families of children with developmental delays across the Piedmont region. APHDI has provided Lucía with a Spanish-language parent support group that meets monthly, and staff at APHDI helped the family understand their rights under Part C of IDEA during the initial IFSP process. Lucía stated, "sin APHDI no hubiera entendido nada del proceso, todo estaba en inglés al principio."

Mateo's current IFSP, developed on April 14, 2026 and most recently reviewed on August 11, 2026, includes Outcome #2 targeting expressive vocabulary growth and Outcome #3 targeting intelligibility in connected speech. The next scheduled IFSP review is February 9, 2027.

5. SESSION SCHEDULE

Mateo has received speech-language intervention twice weekly since May 2026. The current schedule is below.

| Day | Start Time | End Time | Location |
|-----|-----------|----------|----------|
| Tuesday | 9:00 a.m. | 9:45 a.m. | Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, 905 Spring Garden Court |
| Thursday | 3:30 p.m. | 4:15 p.m. | Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Center, PLLC, 2214 Chapel Hill Road |
| Monthly consult | 11:00 a.m. | 11:30 a.m. | CDSA office, 308 Court Square, Graham |

Sessions at Little Sprouts occur in a quiet corner of Ms. Lopez's room, while clinic sessions take place in the therapy suite at Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Center, PLLC. The monthly consult at the CDSA office includes Brenda Walsh and, when available, Diego Flores.

6. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following procedures were completed across two sessions, on September 25, 2026 and October 2, 2026:

- Parent interview (Spanish, with interpreter Carmen Ibarra)
- Review of records from UNC Health Alamance and CDSA
- Classroom observation at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center
- Administration of the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual edition
- Administration of the Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)
- Administration of the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Spontaneous language sample (English and Spanish), analyzed using SALT conventions
- Oral-motor and hearing screening

7. TEST RESULTS

7.1 Standardized Testing

| Test/Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Confidence Interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (Spanish) | 79 | 8th | 73-85 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication (Spanish) | 71 | 3rd | 65-77 |
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension (English) | 82 | 12th | 76-88 |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication (English) | 74 | 4th | 68-80 |
| BESA Morphosyntax Index | 77 | 6th | 70-84 |
| BESA Semantics Index | 81 | 10th | 74-88 |
| GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 68 | 2nd | 62-74 |

Age equivalents derived from the GFTA-3 placed Mateo's articulation skills at approximately 2;6–3;0, well below his chronological age of 4;2.

7.2 Speech Sound Production

Mateo demonstrated the following error patterns in both languages, consistent with a phonological disorder rather than isolated articulation errors:

- Final consonant deletion: "gato" produced as "[ga]" and "dog" produced as "[dɔ]"
- Cluster reduction: "azul" produced as "[asu]"
- Fronting of /k/ to [t], observed consistently across both languages
- Gliding of /ɾ/ to [w] in Spanish, e.g., "para" produced as "[pawa]"
- Stopping of fricatives, e.g., /s/ produced as [t] in word-initial position

Speech intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at 30% for unfamiliar listeners and 65% for familiar listeners such as Lucía and Rosa. With moderate cues, Mateo was able to self-correct 3 of 5 trial productions of target words, improving to 8/10 accuracy on simple CVC targets with minimal cues.

7.3 Language Sample Analysis

A 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was collected in both English and Spanish. Mean length of utterance was 2.4 morphemes in English and 2.1 morphemes in Spanish, both falling below expected ranges for his age. Mateo used primarily single-word and two-word combinations, such as "más agua" and "Max afuera," with limited use of grammatical morphemes in either language. During the sample, he spontaneously requested, "quiero jugo," which was coded as [EW] for an early-emerging want/request form.

8. CLINICAL OBSERVATIONS

During both the classroom observation and clinic sessions, Mateo presented as an engaged, socially motivated child who readily initiated play with the evaluator and interpreter. He was observed attempting to communicate with peer Noah during free play, pointing repeatedly and vocalizing before Noah appeared to lose interest and move to another activity. Ms. Lopez intervened to help translate Mateo's request for a toy, noting this is a frequent occurrence in the classroom.

Mateo transitioned easily between Spanish and English within the same testing session, often translating his own utterances when he perceived he was not understood, a behavior his mother, Lucía, confirmed is common at home with his sister Sol. No significant attention or behavioral concerns were observed. Oral-motor examination was within normal limits, with adequate strength, range of motion, and coordination of the articulators.

9. DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSIONS

Based on results across both languages, Mateo presents with a bilingual speech sound disorder (phonological) and expressive-receptive language delay affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with ICD-10 code F80.9 (developmental disorder of speech and language, unspecified) and F80.1 (expressive language disorder). Because deficits are present and proportionate across both of Mateo's languages, these findings are not attributable to typical second-language acquisition or bilingual language development alone. Mateo continues to meet eligibility criteria for Part C early intervention services under North Carolina's Infant-Toddler Program, pending his transition planning given his age.

10. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Continue individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, provided in both Spanish and English, focusing on phonological process remediation and expressive vocabulary expansion. CPT code 92507 applies to individual sessions; CPT code 92508 applies when co-treatment with a group format is used.
2. Incorporate Cycles phonological approach to target final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and fronting patterns across both languages.
3. Introduce Hanen-based strategies for Lucía and Diego to support language modeling at home in Spanish, with coaching provided through CDSA and APHDI parent groups.
4. Collaborate with Ms. Lopez and Mr. Daniels at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to implement visual supports and peer-modeling strategies during free play, particularly with peers Noah and Jazmín.
5. Refer for a repeat hearing screening with Dr. Sandra Kim in 6 months given history of recurrent otitis media.
6. Update IFSP Outcome #2 and Outcome #3 to reflect current baseline data at the next review on February 9, 2027.
7. Continue family support services through WIC, Smart Start of Alamance County, and APHDI to maintain consistency of care across languages and settings.
8. Begin transition planning discussions with Brenda Walsh at CDSA regarding preschool special education eligibility prior to Mateo's third transition conference.

11. SUMMARY

Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez, age 4;2, presents with a bilingual phonological disorder and expressive-receptive language delay affecting both Spanish and English. These findings are consistent across standardized testing, parent report, and classroom observation, and are not explained by typical bilingual development. Continued intervention, family coaching in the home language, and coordination across CDSA, Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, and community supports including APHDI are recommended to support Mateo's communication development and school readiness.

Report prepared by:

Mariana Castillo-Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Center, PLLC
License No. NC-SLP-48217
Date: October 9, 2026

Clínica de Lenguaje y Habla Piedmont
2210 Kildaire Farm Road, Cary, NC 27518
Teléfono: (919) 555-0199 · Correo electrónico: pnunez@piedmontspeech.com

Fecha del informe: 11 de octubre de 2026

Nombre del niño: Mateo Fernández Ramírez ("Teo")
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de marzo de 2022
Edad en el momento de la evaluación: 4;7
Padres/tutores: Lucía Ramírez y Carlos Fernández
Dirección: 1420 Maple Hollow Drive, Cary, NC 27511
Teléfono de contacto: (919) 555-0148
Número de Medicaid: 584912037A
Número de expediente: 4471-SP
Fuente de referencia: pediatra Dra. Ana María Castillo, a través de Piedmont CDSA
Coordinadora de servicios: Mónica Díaz
Intérprete: Rosa Elena Pérez (español/inglés)
Evaluadora: Patricia Núñez, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingüe español-inglés

Estimados Sr. Fernández y Sra. Ramírez:

Gracias por confiarnos la evaluación de Teo. Fue un placer conocerlo a él y conocerlos a ustedes el 3 de octubre de 2026 en nuestra clínica. Con la ayuda de nuestra intérprete, Rosa Elena Pérez, pudimos conversar con ustedes en español y explicar cada parte de la evaluación mientras la hacíamos. Este informe explica, en lenguaje sencillo, lo que encontramos y lo que recomendamos.

**Motivo de la evaluación**

Teo fue referido para una evaluación completa de habla y lenguaje después de que su maestra en Little Learners Daycare, la Sra. Karen Phillips, notara que a Teo le costaba que sus compañeros lo entendieran durante el juego libre. Según la Sra. Phillips, compañeros como Ava y Noah con frecuencia le pedían que repitiera lo que decía, y Teo a veces dejaba de intentar comunicarse. La Sra. Phillips también observó que Teo usa oraciones más cortas que sus compañeros de la misma edad.

Teo recibió servicios de intervención temprana a través del Little Learners Program desde los 2;6 hasta los 3;6, con sesiones grupales de lenguaje dos veces por semana, de 30 minutos cada una. Esos servicios terminaron cuando cumplió tres años, y la familia no había buscado terapia adicional hasta ahora.

**Historia de nacimiento y médica**

Teo nació el 14 de marzo de 2022 a las 36 semanas de gestación, con un peso de 2,450 gramos. Sus puntajes de Apgar fueron 8 y 9. Pasó cuatro días en la unidad de cuidados especiales para recién nacidos por dificultad leve para respirar, y no tuvo otras complicaciones médicas en ese momento.

Según sus padres, Teo ha tenido seis episodios de infección de oído desde el año de edad, el más reciente en enero de 2026. Fue evaluado por un especialista de oído, nariz y garganta, el Dr. Steven Kim, quien colocó tubos de ventilación en ambos oídos en febrero de 2026. Desde entonces, la familia reporta menos infecciones y la impresión de que Teo escucha mejor. Su pediatra, la Dra. Ana María Castillo, confirmó que su audición actual es normal según una prueba de audiometría reciente.

No hay otros diagnósticos médicos. Teo no toma medicamentos de forma regular y no tiene alergias conocidas.

**Historia familiar y del lenguaje**

En casa, la familia habla principalmente español, con algo de inglés cuando están presentes los hermanos mayores de Teo. Su hermana, Sol Fernández, tiene 7 años y es bilingüe; su hermano, Diego Fernández, tiene 10 años. Durante las tardes, su abuela, Rosa Fernández, cuida a los tres niños mientras los padres trabajan. La Sra. Ramírez trabaja en Carolina Distribution Co. y el Sr. Fernández trabaja en una sucursal de Capital Bank en Raleigh.

Los padres reportan que entienden la mayoría de lo que dice Teo, pero que personas fuera de la familia a menudo le piden que repita las palabras. No hay historia familiar de trastornos del habla, lenguaje o aprendizaje que los padres conozcan.

**Procedimientos de evaluación**

La evaluación incluyó pruebas estandarizadas, observación de juego, una muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, y una entrevista con los padres. Debido a que Teo se comunica en ambos idiomas, administramos partes de la evaluación en español y partes en inglés, según el idioma en el que Teo se sentía más cómodo respondiendo. Usamos también observaciones informales en su ambiente de juego y revisamos un video corto grabado en Little Learners Daycare.

**Resultados de las pruebas**

A continuación se presentan los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas. Los puntajes estándar típicos van de 85 a 115.

Prueba | Área | Puntaje estándar | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza
Escala de Lenguaje Preescolar, Quinta Edición (PLS-5) | Comprensión auditiva | 73 | 4 | 68-78
PLS-5 | Comunicación expresiva | 70 | 2 | 65-75
PLS-5 | Puntaje total de lenguaje | 68 | 2 | 63-73
Evaluación Clínica de Fundamentos del Lenguaje, Preescolar-3 (CELF Preescolar-3) | Núcleo del lenguaje | 71 | 3 | 73-83
Prueba de Articulación Goldman-Fristoe, Tercera Edición (GFTA-3) | Articulación | 75 | 5 | 70-80

El equivalente de edad de Teo en comprensión auditiva en PLS-5 cayó en el rango de 2;6–3;0, aproximadamente dos años por debajo de su edad real. Su equivalente de edad en comunicación expresiva fue similar, en el rango de 2;9–3;3.

En la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, Teo combinó principalmente dos y tres palabras, con pocas oraciones de cuatro palabras. Omitió con frecuencia los artículos y las conjugaciones verbales correctas, tanto en español como en inglés, por ejemplo diciendo "yo quiere agua" en vez de "yo quiero agua".

**Análisis del habla**

En la prueba GFTA-3, Teo mostró varios patrones de simplificación fonológica típicos de niños menores. Usó anteriorización, reemplazando sonidos posteriores como /k/ y /g/ con sonidos anteriores como /t/ y /d/. También mostró reducción de grupos consonánticos, por ejemplo produciendo "pato" en vez de "plato".

Durante la prueba de nombrar imágenes, uno de las palabras meta fue "sol" (la imagen del sol en el cielo). Teo produjo [tol], sustituyendo el sonido /s/ inicial con /t/, un ejemplo claro de anteriorización. En otra palabra meta, "casa", produjo [tata].

Calculamos un porcentaje de consonantes correctas de 80% en habla espontánea, y Teo produjo correctamente 8/10 palabras de una lista de palabras de alta frecuencia cuando se le dieron claves de articulación con nivel de apoyo moderado (mod cues). Sin apoyo, su precisión bajó a 3 de 10.

Su inteligibilidad para oyentes familiares fue calificada como moderadamente reducida; para oyentes que no lo conocen, como severamente reducida.

**Observaciones conductuales**

Teo se mostró sociable y curioso durante toda la sesión. Buscó la aprobación de sus padres con frecuencia y miró a su madre antes de intentar palabras difíciles. En un momento, mientras veía una foto familiar en la sala de espera, señaló la foto y dijo "Sol no está aquí", refiriéndose a que su hermana no estaba presente ese día. Teo se frustró brevemente cuando no pudimos entender una palabra, pero se calmó rápidamente cuando le ofrecimos opciones visuales.

No observamos conductas que sugirieran dificultades de atención, interacción social o juego más allá de lo esperado para su edad. Su juego simbólico y su contacto visual fueron apropiados para su edad.

**Impresiones clínicas**

Según los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la observación clínica, y la información de los padres y de la maestra, Teo cumple con los criterios para un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (CIE-10 F80.2), con un trastorno fonológico concurrente. Sus dificultades están presentes en ambos idiomas, lo cual indica un trastorno del lenguaje real y no simplemente una diferencia esperada por el bilingüismo.

Las dificultades de Teo con el habla y el lenguaje probablemente contribuyen a sus dificultades para comunicarse con compañeros como Ava y Noah en Little Learners Daycare, y pueden afectar su participación en el salón de clases si no se atienden ahora.

**Recomendaciones**

1. Recomendamos terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, dos veces por semana, de 30 minutos cada sesión, facturada bajo el código CPT 92507. Esta evaluación se facturó bajo el código CPT 92523.

2. Recomendamos que la terapia use un enfoque de Cycles para los patrones fonológicos identificados, junto con elementos de PROMPT para apoyar la producción motora del habla.

3. Recomendamos continuar trabajando hacia el Resultado 2 del IFSP de comunicación funcional, y añadir un nuevo Objetivo 3 enfocado en la claridad del habla en ambos idiomas.

4. Recomendamos coordinación continua con la terapeuta ocupacional, Diana López, OTR/L, y con el fisioterapeuta, Jorge Martínez, PT, quienes también atienden a Teo, para asegurar que las metas de todos los proveedores estén alineadas.

5. Recomendamos que el equipo de Little Learners Daycare, incluyendo a la Sra. Karen Phillips, reciba estrategias simples de apoyo de lenguaje para usar durante el juego y las actividades en grupo.

6. Recomendamos una reevaluación en seis meses para medir el progreso y ajustar las metas según sea necesario.

**Cierre**

Entendemos que recibir esta información puede ser difícil. Queremos que sepan que Teo es un niño alegre, curioso y cariñoso, y que con el apoyo correcto puede progresar mucho. Estamos disponibles para responder cualquier pregunta que tengan sobre este informe o sobre los próximos pasos.

Pueden comunicarse con nuestra oficina al (919) 555-0199 o por correo electrónico a pnunez@piedmontspeech.com. También pueden comunicarse con la coordinadora de servicios, Mónica Díaz, en Piedmont CDSA, si tienen preguntas sobre el IFSP o los servicios de intervención temprana.

Gracias nuevamente por su confianza. Esperamos trabajar junto a ustedes y a Teo en este próximo paso.

Atentamente,

Patricia Núñez, MS, CCC-SLP
Patóloga del habla y el lenguaje, bilingüe español-inglés

Intérprete de español: Rosa Elena Vidal
Patóloga del habla-lenguaje bilingüe: Carla M. Benítez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language, PLLC
Participan: madre Lucía Fernández, padre Diego Cruz, hermana Valentina Cruz (5 a.), abuela materna Rosario Cruz

S:
Entrevista con mamá, Lucía, con apoyo de la intérprete Rosa Elena Vidal, ya que mamá prefiere hablar español en reuniones formales aunque entiende algo de inglés. Mamá reporta en sus palabras: "Mateo entiende todo lo que le decimos pero casi no habla. Dice como diez palabras y se frustra mucho, grita y nos jala de la mano." Papá, Diego, añade por teléfono desde el trabajo: "En la guardería dicen que se queda solo, no juega con los demás niños. A veces en la casa se enoja porque su hermana no le entiende y le quita el juguete." Preocupación principal de la familia: lenguaje expresivo muy limitado para la edad; conductas de frustración (gritar, jalar) cuando no se le entiende; aislamiento social frente a otros niños.

Rutina diaria: Mateo se levanta ~7:00 a.m., desayuna con Lucía y Valentina antes de que ella salga para Escuela Primaria Oak Hill. Asiste a Centro Infantil Pequeños Soñadores de 8:30 a.m. a 4:30 p.m., lunes a viernes, mientras Lucía trabaja en Empacadora Reidsville Foods y Diego trabaja turnos rotativos en Transportes Alamance. Abuela Rosario, que vive a dos cuadras, lo recoge los miércoles y lo lleva a la hora del cuento en la Biblioteca Regional del Condado de Guilford, programa Mother Goose, donde según mamá "le gusta mucho, pero no repite las canciones como los otros niños, se queda mirando." Los fines de semana la familia asiste a misa en la Iglesia Católica San José, donde hay grupo de juego para niños pequeños antes del servicio; mamá dice que Mateo se aísla también en ese grupo y prefiere jugar solo con bloques. Por las noches, Diego hace rutina de baño y cuento con ambos niños cuando su turno lo permite.

Familia recibe apoyo nutricional de WIC y está inscrita en clases de crianza de Smart Start de Guilford; mamá menciona interés en Early Head Start para el próximo año si no logra plaza en preescolar público. Pediatra: Dr. Andrés Palacios, Clínica Pediátrica Lindley, refirió a ITP tras notar retraso de lenguaje en el chequeo de los 24 meses. Niño recibe OT con Hannah Griggs, OTR/L, por sensibilidad táctil, y PT con Marcus Dell, DPT, por hipotonía leve de tronco; ambos del mismo contrato CDSA, visitas quincenales.

Prioridades de la familia, en orden: (1) que Mateo use más palabras o señas para pedir lo que quiere; (2) reducir las conductas de frustración en casa y guardería; (3) que juegue con otros niños en la guardería, la biblioteca y la iglesia; (4) entender qué esperar de cara a la transición al preescolar cuando cumpla 3 años.

O:
Sesión de reevaluación realizada 2 de octubre de 2026 en el hogar, 4821 Winding Creek Lane, Greensboro, NC 27410, 10:00 a.m.–11:15 a.m.. Códigos facturados: 92523 (evaluación de habla/lenguaje) y 92507 (tratamiento individual, 30 min posteriores). Presentes: Mateo, Lucía Fernández, intérprete Rosa Elena Vidal.

Administrado Preschool Language Scale, 5.ª ed., versión en español (PLS-5 Spanish): Auditory Comprehension puntaje estándar 68 (percentil 2), Expressive Communication puntaje estándar 62 (percentil 1), Total Language puntaje estándar 64, intervalo de confianza 58-70. Edad equivalente expresiva: 1;2–1;6; edad equivalente receptiva: 1;8–2;0. Subtest de vocabulario receptivo: 11 de 20 ítems (55%), identificó correctamente objetos familiares pero no acciones ni atributos.

Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (15 min, codificada con convenciones SALT): 12 enunciados espontáneos en 15 minutos; vocabulario expresivo observado ~11 palabras aproximantes, principalmente sustantivos ("agua", "mamá", "más"). Longitud media de enunciado 1.1 morfemas. Un enunciado codificado [EW] (error de palabra) al intentar "pelota" → produjo [pe].

Inventario fonético limitado a /m, p, b, a, e, o/; ausencia de /t, d, k, g, s, l/. Praxias orales dentro de lo esperado; no hay hallazgos consistentes con apraxia infantil del habla en este momento.

Imitación de señas/gestos funcionales: 8/10 ensayos correctos (80%) para "más" y "terminado" con modelo + mod cues. Comprensión de instrucciones de un paso: 7 de 10 (70%); de dos pasos: 3 de 10 (30%). Juego simbólico: nivel emergente, secuencias de dos pasos con apoyo mod-máx. Lista informal de hitos pragmáticos (adaptada de Rossetti): 9 de 18 ítems presentes (50%), con déficits en atención conjunta sostenida y turnos de juego.

Observación en guardería (25 de septiembre de 2026, 9:15 a.m.) en Centro Infantil Pequeños Soñadores: Mateo juega paralelo, no inicia interacción con compañeros; se observó breve intercambio con compañera Camila al compartir bloques, pero sin contacto visual sostenido. Maestra Srta. Johana Reyes reporta conductas similares a las de casa y confirma que usa mayormente gestos y señalar.

Informe de OT (Hannah Griggs, 28 de septiembre de 2026): hiporesponsividad táctil moderada, sin cambios significativos desde la última revisión. Informe de PT (Marcus Dell, 30 de septiembre de 2026): tono de tronco mejorando, ahora dentro de límites funcionales para la edad; PT recomienda alta en próxima revisión.

Antecedentes médicos: parto a término (39 semanas), peso al nacer 3,210 g, Apgar 9/9. Sin hospitalizaciones. Audición: pasó cribado neonatal; audiometría conductual de 15 de agosto de 2026 dentro de límites normales bilateral. Sin antecedentes familiares reportados de retraso de lenguaje ni trastorno del espectro autista.

A:
Mateo presenta trastorno mixto receptivo-expresivo del lenguaje, de moderado a severo, consistente con F80.2 (CIE-10), con mayor afectación en el dominio expresivo que en el receptivo. Brecha entre edad cronológica (2;4) y edades equivalentes de lenguaje (1;2–2;0) de aproximadamente 10–14 meses, cumple criterios de elegibilidad para NC ITP bajo retraso significativo en el dominio de comunicación. Inventario fonético reducido es consistente con el perfil de lenguaje limitado más que con un trastorno motor del habla primario; se continuará monitoreando conforme aumente el vocabulario expresivo.

Conductas de frustración (gritar, jalar) se interpretan como comunicación no convencional secundaria a vocabulario expresivo insuficiente, no como conducta primaria desregulada; responden bien a la introducción de señas funcionales (80% de precisión), lo cual es indicador positivo para el pronóstico con enseñanza temprana de comunicación aumentativa. Déficits pragmáticos (atención conjunta, turnos) y juego social por debajo de lo esperado se consideran secundarios al retraso de lenguaje en este momento; audición normal y ausencia de otros marcadores reducen la probabilidad de un trastorno del espectro autista, aunque se recomienda seguir monitoreando atención conjunta en próximas visitas dado que no se puede descartar por completo a esta edad.

Uso de dos idiomas en el hogar (español predominante, inglés en la guardería) no se considera causa del retraso de lenguaje; el perfil de retraso es evidente en ambos contextos lingüísticos según reportes de mamá y de la maestra Srta. Johana Reyes, y la evaluación en español confirma retraso real más que diferencia típica de desarrollo bilingüe. Familia motivada, consistente con asistencia a sesiones y seguimiento de estrategias en casa, biblioteca e iglesia.

Resultado 1 (comunicación funcional): Mateo usará 15–20 palabras o aproximaciones y 5 señas funcionales de manera espontánea para pedir y protestar, en 80% de las oportunidades observadas, en 6 meses. Estrategias: modelo de lenguaje aumentado (Hanen, técnica "seguir la iniciativa del niño"), introducción sistemática de señas con apoyo de video-modelado, práctica de vocabulario funcional en rutinas de comida y juego. Lucía y Diego recibirán coaching en cada visita; abuela Rosario incluida en una sesión mensual dado su rol activo de cuidado los miércoles.

Resultado 2 (regulación/reducción de frustración): disminuir episodios de gritar/jalar a 1 o menos por hora de observación directa, mediante introducción de tablero de comunicación con 12 símbolos (fases I–II de PECS) en casa y guardería, con apoyo de la maestra Srta. Johana Reyes.

Resultado 3 (interacción social): Mateo iniciará interacción con un compañero (p. ej. ofrecer juguete, imitar acción) en 3 de 5 oportunidades estructuradas en la guardería y en el grupo de juego de la Biblioteca Regional del Condado de Guilford, en 6 meses. Se acuerda invitar también a compañera Camila a actividades diádicas guiadas.

Resultado 4 (entrenamiento familiar): Lucía y Diego demostrarán el uso independiente de al menos tres estrategias de Hanen en video grabado en casa, revisado en la próxima visita, para apoyar generalización fuera de sesión.

Dado que Mateo cumple 3 años en junio de 2027, se iniciará planificación de transición de Parte C a Parte B en la próxima revisión; se recomienda alta de PT con Marcus Dell en esa misma revisión y continuar OT 1x/semana con Hannah Griggs. text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Vásquez ("Teo")
Date of Birth: 14 de marzo de 2022 (also recorded as 03/14/2022)
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Dates of Evaluation: 03/04/2026, 3-11-2026, and el martes 17 de marzo de 2026
Report Date: 2026-03-24
Parent/Guardian: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Carlos Vásquez (father)
Home Address: 2214 Willowbrook Drive, Greensboro, Guilford County, NC 27403
Home Phone: (336) 555-8821
Primary Home Language(s): Spanish (dominant), English (emerging)
Medicaid ID: 8827461925A
Secondary Insurance Member ID: NCH-5591172
NC ITP Child ID: ITP-220458
Record/Authorization Number: AUTH-26-004471
Referral Source: Angela Freeman, Service Coordinator, Piedmont Regional CDSA
Examiner: Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual English/Spanish
Employer of Examiner: Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC

2. REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Angela Freeman, his service coordinator at Piedmont Regional CDSA, following a routine developmental screening on 01/22/2026. The screening, conducted as part of Mateo's continued eligibility review under the NC Infant-Toddler Program, flagged concerns in expressive language and intelligibility. His mother, Lucía Rodríguez, reports that Mateo "habla poquito" and that unfamiliar listeners, including his pediatrician and extended family, frequently ask her to repeat or translate what he says. This evaluation was requested to update Mateo's current speech-language functioning for his upcoming IFSP review and to inform the transition planning process as he approaches his third birthday.

3. BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Background information was obtained through parent interview conducted primarily in Spanish with Lucía Rodríguez on 3 de marzo de 2026, review of prior Early Intervention records, review of records from Piedmont Regional CDSA, and informal consultation with staff at Little Explorers Early Head Start Center.

3.1 Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestational age at Moses H. Cone Memorial Hospital in Greensboro, NC, on 14 de marzo de 2022. Birth weight was 6 lbs 4 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucía Rodríguez reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care through WIC beginning in her second trimester. Mateo remained in the hospital for routine newborn care and was discharged after two days with his mother.

Medical history is notable for recurrent otitis media, with his pediatrician, Dr. Susan Park, documenting five episodes between March 2023 and November 2024. Mateo underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement on 06/02/2024 at Cone Health Outpatient Surgery Center. A follow-up audiological evaluation completed by Dr. Michael Chen on 9/15/2024 revealed normal hearing bilaterally with the tubes in place. No additional surgeries, hospitalizations, or significant illnesses were reported. Mateo is not currently on any medication and has no known allergies. Developmental milestones for gross and fine motor skills were reported as within normal limits; he walked independently at 13 months and currently feeds himself with a spoon and fork without difficulty.

3.2 Developmental History

Lucía Rodríguez reported that Mateo babbled consistently as an infant and produced his first recognizable words, "mamá" and "agua," around 14 months. However, vocabulary growth slowed noticeably after that point. By 24 months, Mateo was reportedly combining only a few two-word phrases, and by 30 months his word combinations remained limited and difficult for unfamiliar adults to understand. Lucía Rodríguez denied any history of regression in skills. Mateo was enrolled in Early Intervention through Piedmont Regional CDSA at 28 months of age, with an initial IFSP developed on 07/19/2024. He has received home-based speech-language services approximately twice monthly since that time.

3.3 Family and Language History

Mateo lives at home with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Carlos Vásquez; and his older brother, Diego Vásquez, age 7. Lucía Rodríguez reported that the household is Spanish-dominant, with roughly 90 percent of input to Mateo occurring in Spanish and the remainder in English, largely introduced through Diego and through television programming. Lucía Rodríguez herself immigrated from Guadalajara, Mexico, as a teenager and reports being fully bilingual, while Carlos Vásquez reports more limited English proficiency and communicates with Mateo almost exclusively in Spanish.

Lucía Rodríguez works two jobs to support the family: a daytime position as a server at Golden Corral on Wendover Avenue, and an evening position as a front-desk aide at the YMCA. Carlos Vásquez works full time installing flooring for a residential contractor based in High Point. Given the parents' demanding work schedules, Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Ríos, provides supplemental childcare several afternoons a week and reportedly speaks only Spanish with him. The family also keeps a small dog, Max, whom Mateo is reportedly very attached to and often mentions during play.

Diego is in second grade at Oak Ridge Elementary School, part of Guilford County Schools, where his teacher is Mrs. Patricia Lopez. Lucía Rodríguez noted that Diego has become increasingly English-dominant since starting school and now frequently code-switches with Mateo at home, which she believes has increased Mateo's exposure to English in recent months. The family has also received support from Guilford County Department of Social Services in the past for food and housing assistance, and Lucía Rodríguez reported ongoing contact with Smart Start of Guilford County regarding childcare subsidy eligibility.

3.4 Educational History

Mateo has attended Little Explorers Early Head Start Center five days a week since September 2024. His current classroom teacher is Ms. Patricia Reyes, and his classroom assistant is Mr. James Thornton. Both report that Mateo is social and eager to interact with peers but is often misunderstood, and that he will frequently point or gesture rather than attempt a verbal request when he senses he will not be understood. Ms. Reyes noted that Mateo has one particular friend in the classroom, Ethan, with whom he plays regularly, often through parallel play with minimal verbal exchange. Program staff referred the family to Smart Start of Guilford County for continued enrollment support and have coordinated periodically with Angela Freeman regarding Mateo's IFSP goals within the classroom setting.

4. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following procedures were used to assess Mateo's speech and language functioning:

- Review of records from Piedmont Regional CDSA, Moses H. Cone Memorial Hospital, and Little Explorers Early Head Start Center
- Parent interview and case history questionnaire, completed in Spanish with Lucía Rodríguez
- Clinical observation of Mateo in both structured and unstructured play, conducted bilingually
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish and English editions
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), screening items only
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Semantics subtests
- Informal oral-motor examination
- Language sample analysis, approximately 100 utterances, coded in SALT

Testing was completed across three sessions, on 03/04/2026, 3-11-2026, and el martes 17 de marzo de 2026, each lasting approximately 45 minutes. Sessions were conducted at Mateo's home beginning at 9:30 a.m. and, for the final session, at Little Explorers Early Head Start Center beginning at 1:00 p.m., per scheduling availability. Both parents were present for portions of the first session; Carlos Vásquez joined briefly by phone at 10:15 a.m. to answer questions regarding medical history.

5. BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo presented as a friendly, curious child who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner across all three sessions. He transitioned well between activities and attended to structured tasks for approximately 10 to 12 minutes before requiring a break or a change of activity. Mateo used gesture, pointing, and some vocalization to communicate throughout testing, and he was observed to use several intelligible single words in both Spanish and English, including "mas," "perro," and "ball." When frustrated that he was not understood, he occasionally repeated the same attempt louder rather than revising his articulation, a pattern consistent with reports from Lucía Rodríguez and from classroom staff. No unusual behaviors, sensory sensitivities, or attentional concerns were noted that would be expected to significantly affect test validity. Results are considered a reliable estimate of Mateo's current speech-language functioning.

6. TEST RESULTS

6.1 Receptive and Expressive Language

On the Spanish edition of the PLS-5, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 68 (2nd percentile), yielding a Total Language Score of 70 (2nd percentile), with a 95 percent confidence interval of 64-76. On the English edition, administered to capture his emerging second-language skills, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 62 and an Expressive Communication standard score of 55, both well below age expectations, which is consistent with his more limited English exposure rather than an independent area of concern.

On the BESA Morphosyntax subtest, Mateo scored at the 3rd percentile in Spanish, with frequent omission of articles and inconsistent use of verb tense markers. On the BESA Semantics subtest, he scored at the 9th percentile, demonstrating a reduced vocabulary relative to same-age Spanish-English bilingual peers. Screening items from the CELF Preschool-3 were administered in English and were consistent with significant delay, though results were interpreted cautiously given Mateo's limited English exposure.

Language sample analysis revealed a mean length of utterance of 1.8 morphemes, below the expected range of 2.5-3.5 morphemes for his chronological age. Mateo's utterances were coded with [EW] for several English word insertions into otherwise Spanish utterances, consistent with typical bilingual code-mixing rather than disordered language use. He combined two words in approximately 4 of 10 utterances and rarely produced three-word combinations.

6.2 Articulation and Phonology

On the GFTA-3, Mateo obtained a standard score of 62 (1st percentile), with an age equivalent of 2;6–3;0. Phonological processes noted included final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and fronting of velar sounds. For example, Mateo produced "ato" for the target word "gato" and "tasa" for "casa," both consistent with velar fronting affecting /k/ and /g/. He also produced "pan" for "pan" correctly but omitted final consonants in words such as "sol," produced as "so." His speech intelligibility was estimated at approximately 30 percent to unfamiliar listeners and 60 percent to familiar listeners, consistent with parent and teacher report.

Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could approximate /k/ in isolation with moderate cues but was unable to maintain the sound at the word level. He demonstrated some success imitating /s/ in the final position with minimum cues, suggesting this may be a reasonable early treatment target.

6.3 Oral-Motor and Feeding

Informal oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure and strength of the lips, tongue, and jaw for speech and feeding purposes. No concerns with chewing, swallowing, or drooling were reported or observed. Diadochokinetic rates were judged to be mildly reduced for his age but not of clinical concern at this time.

Summary Score Table

| Measure | Domain | Score Type | Score | Percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Auditory Comprehension | Standard Score | 76 | 5th |
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Expressive Communication | Standard Score | 68 | 2nd |
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Total Language | Standard Score | 70 | 2nd |
| BESA | Morphosyntax | Percentile | — | 3rd |
| BESA | Semantics | Percentile | — | 9th |
| GFTA-3 | Articulation | Standard Score | 62 | 1st |

7. CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Results of this evaluation indicate that Mateo presents with a significant delay in both receptive and expressive language skills, as well as a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder, in his dominant language of Spanish. These findings cannot be attributed solely to normal bilingual development, as Mateo's scores in Spanish, his dominant and most-exposed language, fall well below expected ranges relative to Spanish-English bilingual normative samples on the BESA. His history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement is a relevant contributing factor to consider, though his hearing has since been documented as within normal limits.

Mateo's profile is consistent with Developmental Language Disorder (ICD-10 code F80.9) co-occurring with a Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10 code F80.0). His reduced intelligibility, limited morphosyntactic development, and reduced vocabulary in his dominant language, combined with documented slow progress despite twelve months of home-based Early Intervention services, support continued and likely increased intervention intensity moving into the transition period from the NC Infant-Toddler Program.

8. SUMMARY

Mateo Alejandro Vásquez, a 4;2-year-old Spanish-English bilingual boy, was evaluated due to parent and provider concern regarding expressive language and intelligibility. Testing revealed significant delays in receptive and expressive language in Spanish, his dominant language, along with a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder characterized by multiple phonological process errors. These findings are consistent with Developmental Language Disorder and Speech Sound Disorder and are not attributable to typical bilingual language acquisition patterns. Mateo's strengths include social engagement, use of compensatory gesture, and stimulability for several target sounds with cueing.

9. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for continued speech-language intervention services under his existing IFSP, with recommended increase in frequency from twice monthly to weekly direct services, provided bilingually or with coordinated interpreter support.
2. Treatment should address expressive vocabulary growth, morphosyntactic development (verb tense marking, article use), and articulation targets including /k/, /g/, and final consonant production, using a combined naturalistic and structured approach such as Cycles for phonology.
3. The family and Rosa Ríos should continue to be included in home-practice strategies, consistent with a Hanen-style coaching model, given the amount of caregiving time she provides.
4. Mateo's audiological status should be monitored given his history of recurrent otitis media; a repeat hearing screening is recommended within the next six months.
5. Given Mateo's approaching third birthday, the family should begin transition planning with Angela Freeman at Piedmont Regional CDSA to coordinate referral to Guilford County Schools Exceptional Children's Preschool Program for continued services at age three.
6. Classroom staff at Little Explorers Early Head Start Center, including Ms. Reyes and Mr. Thornton, should be provided with strategies to support Mateo's verbal attempts and reduce reliance on gesture, particularly during interactions with peers such as Ethan.
7. The family should continue to be connected with community supports, including Smart Start of Guilford County for continued childcare subsidy and WIC for ongoing nutrition services, as these supports reduce caregiving strain given Lucía Rodríguez's current work schedule across Golden Corral and the YMCA.
8. Re-evaluation is recommended in six to twelve months or at the time of transition to Part B services, whichever occurs first.

10. ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo meets North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program eligibility criteria for a developmental delay in the area of communication. This determination is based on a composite score more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean on standardized measures administered in his dominant language. Continued services under his IFSP are recommended as outlined above, with a full IFSP review scheduled for 06/02/2026.

This report was prepared by Jennifer Marsh, M.S., CCC-SLP, on behalf of Piedmont Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC, under authorization number AUTH-26-004471. Questions regarding this report may be directed to the examiner at (336) 555-7740 or jmarsh@piedmontpedsslp.com.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY:

Due to persistent effusion, myringotomy w/ bilateral PE tube placement was performed on March 2, 2024 by Dr. Rebecca Sim, ENT, at Piedmont Regional Medical Center. Tubes extruded spontaneously by approx 14 months post-placement; no tubes currently in place. Most recent hearing screen, July 30, 2026, was WNL bilaterally per report received from Dr. Sim's office.

No hx of seizure, head injury, or hospitalization beyond the above. Vision screening WNL per pediatrician Dr. Patel at pt's 4-year well-check. Pt is up to date on immunizations per CG report and chart review. No current meds. Dx hx incl specific lang delay (ICD-10 F80.1) established at pt's initial Piedmont CDSA eval approx 1 year prior; no formal dx of ASD, though CG and Denise Walker (service coordinator) note some sensory-seeking behaviors (e.g., craving deep pressure, mouthing non-food items) that may warrant OT eval.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY:
Home lang environment is bilingual; Lucía Flores reports approx 70% Spanish/30% English input at home, w/ Carlos Flores speaking primarily English w/ pt and Lucía Flores speaking primarily Spanish. Sofía Flores, pt's older sister, is reportedly a fluent bilingual speaker and often translates/mediates btwn pt and English-speaking adults, incl at Tiny Tadpoles Learning Cottage pickup. Lucía Flores works part-time as a seamstress at Carolina Fabric Works; Carlos Flores works full-time in logistics at Southeast Distribution Partners.

No family hx of speech/lang delay reported on the maternal side; Lucía Flores notes a paternal great-uncle reportedly had a "stutter" as a child that resolved w/o tx, though details are limited. No other known hx of speech, lang, or hearing disorder in either family.

Per CG and Ms. Lopez report, pt's receptive lang in both langs appears stronger than his expressive lang; pt reliably follows routine 1-step directions in both Eng and Span but is inconsistent w/ 2-step directions, esp in a less-dominant lang or w/ unfamiliar vocab. Pt uses approx 15-20 word combinations reported across both langs combined but frequently substitutes gesture + single word for multiword utterances, esp when frustrated or in a hurry to communicate.

PREVIOUS SERVICES:
Pt was enrolled in NC's Infant-Toddler Program via Piedmont CDSA at 24 months following parental concern raised at a Smart Start playgroup screening. Pt received home-based developmental services approx 1x/wk from 24 to 36 months; services were discontinued at the transition to preschool-age eligibility pending this comprehensive eval. Last IFSP review was conducted on February 11, 2026; next review is tentatively scheduled for October 5, 2026.

ORAL-PERIPHERAL EXAM:
Structures WNL for symmetry, strength, and ROM. No signs of dysarthria, cleft, or other structural anomaly. Dentition age-appropriate; no overt feeding/swallowing concerns reported by CG or observed during session (pt was offered a snack during the break).

HEARING:
Per hx above, most recent hearing screen (July 30, 2026) WNL bilaterally. No current parental concern re: hearing; pt responds consistently to name and environmental sounds per CG report.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS:
Pt separated from CG w/o difficulty and engaged readily w/ toys in the therapy room. Attention to task was variable; pt required mod cues and frequent redirection, esp during structured/tabletop tasks, and benefited from brief movement breaks btwn subtests. Pt demonstrated functional and some symbolic play skills (e.g., feeding a stuffed dog toy, which pt spontaneously called "Rocky" after his own pet, and pushing cars w/ accompanying sound effects). Pt was socially engaged w/ the examiner, made good eye contact, and used gesture + vocalization to request desired items/activities when words were unavailable.

Articulation was difficult to understand for the examiner (an unfamiliar listener); intelligibility was estimated at approx 40% in connected speech, improving to approx 65% w/ known context/topic and CG interpretation. Mother reports pt's productions are clearer to her and to doña Lupe than to unfamiliar listeners, consistent w/ "known listener" intelligibility patterns often observed in young bilingual/multilingual-exposed children and not w/ reduced severity.

ASSESSMENT TOOLS AND PROCEDURES:
The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both Eng and Span as appropriate, w/ Span items/norms administered first given pt's lang dominance, per best practice for bilingual assessment:

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English form (select items for comparison)
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax and Semantics subtests
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Informal Spanish articulation screening (author-constructed word list)
- Language sample analysis (combined Eng/Span, approx 100 utterances), SALT-style coding incl maze codes [EW] and [FP]
- MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI), bilingual short forms (parent report)
- Informal oral-motor/structural-functional exam
- Play-based language sampling and clinical observation

TEST RESULTS:

PLS-5 Spanish (primary/dominant lang, admin'd first):
Auditory Comprehension: standard score 76 (percentile 5), 95% CI 70-82
Expressive Communication: standard score 71 (percentile 3), 95% CI 65-77
Total Language Score: standard score 72 (percentile 3), 95% CI 67-77

PLS-5 English (select items, non-dominant lang; item-level data recorded for comparison, not formally normed given order of administration):
Auditory Comprehension items correct: 11/20
Expressive Communication items correct: 8/20

BESA Morphosyntax (Spanish): scaled score 6, age equivalent 2;9
BESA Semantics (Spanish): scaled score 7, age equivalent 3;0

GFTA-3 (English, Sounds-in-Words): standard score 68, percentile 2. Errors noted on /s/, /z/, /r/, and /l/, along w/ final consonant deletion patterns across both langs.

Informal Spanish articulation screening: error patterns noted on /ɾ/ (tap r), consistent substitution of [w] for /l/ (e.g., pt produced "guata" for target "bota" approx 3 of 5 trials), and final consonant deletion in both langs (e.g., target "pelo" produced as "peo").

LANGUAGE SAMPLE ANALYSIS:
A combined Eng/Span language sample (approx 100 utterances) was collected during play-based interaction. MLU (words) was calculated at 1.8 morphemes, below expectations for CA 4;2. Utterances were coded for mazes [EW] (word repetition/revision) and [FP] (filled pause), both occurring at low-mod frequency, suggesting word-finding difficulty rather than a primary fluency disorder. Pt frequently code-switched mid-utterance (e.g., "Mateo want more" / "quiero más agua"), which is consistent w/ typical bilingual development and was not counted as evidence of disorder in itself.

Representative utterances incl: "mamá dame eso" (mom give me that), "more pea" (more please), and "Rocky go" referring to the family dog Rocky. Several productions were phonologically reduced, e.g., target "galleta" produced as "gaya" and target "water" produced as "wawa".

CDI (parent report, combined vocab checklist across both langs): pt's CG-reported combined vocab (concepts understood in either lang counted once) fell at approx the 5th percentile for CA, w/ reported productive vocab of approx 65 words total across both langs.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS:
Based on standardized testing, parent/CG report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents w/ a Language Disorder affecting both Spanish (primary/dominant lang) and English, characterized by deficits in both receptive and, more significantly, expressive lang skills relative to CA expectations. Scores fall consistently in the disordered range across both domains and both langs, supporting a primary lang impairment rather than a lang-difference-only profile often seen in typically-developing bilingual children (i.e., deficits present across BOTH langs, not just the non-dominant one).

Pt also presents w/ a concomitant Speech Sound Disorder; phonological patterns (final consonant deletion, liquid gliding, stopping) are present across both langs, consistent w/ a phonological, rather than purely articulation-based, etiology. Pt's hx of recurrent OM w/ PE tube placement on March 2, 2024 may have been a contributing factor historically, though current hearing is WNL per recent screening. Mild sensory-seeking behaviors noted during session (per above) may warrant OT screening; this was discussed w/ Lucía Flores and will be relayed to Denise Walker at Piedmont CDSA for consideration at the next IFSP review.

Pt's intelligibility deficits, combined vocab delay, and MLU below age expectation support a dx of Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) w/ comorbid Phonological Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0). Prognosis is judged good w/ consistent intervention, given pt's strong social engagement, imitation skills, functional play, and supportive family involvement.

DIAGNOSIS SUMMARY:
1. Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder, ICD-10 F80.2
2. Phonological Disorder, ICD-10 F80.0
3. Hx of Otitis Media w/ PE tube placement, resolved, ICD-10 H65.9

RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Pt qualifies for and is recommended for individual speech-lang tx 2x/wk, 30-min sessions, targeting expressive vocab, multiword utterance production, and phonological patterns, delivered bilingually (Span primary, Eng secondary) per family preference.
2. Continue services through Piedmont CDSA's Infant-Toddler Program; recommend adding this eval's findings to pt's IFSP at the review scheduled October 5, 2026.
3. Refer for OT screening to assess sensory-processing concerns noted above; family to discuss timing w/ Denise Walker.
4. Recommend hearing re-screen in 6 mo given hx of recurrent OM, even though current screening is WNL.
5. CG education re: bilingual lang strategies (consistent modeling in both langs, expansion of child utterances, commenting rather than quizzing) to be provided to Lucía Flores and Carlos Flores, doña Lupe, and Miss Ana given their roles as primary CGs across the week.
6. Recommend classroom collaboration w/ Ms. Lopez and la maestra Carmen at Tiny Tadpoles Learning Cottage re: simplified directions, visual supports, and structured peer-pairing (e.g., pairing pt w/ Liam for structured play given existing rapport, and gently encouraging turn-taking w/ Emma).
7. Encourage continued participation in community lang-rich activities, incl the lapboard library program at the Garner branch of Wake County Public Library and the Sunday children's program at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida, as both provide valuable peer and lang exposure in low-pressure settings.
8. F/u re-eval recommended in 6 mo or per IFSP review cycle, whichever comes first, to monitor progress and adjust tx goals accordingly.

This report and its recommendations were discussed w/ Lucía Flores at the conclusion of testing, w/ interpreter Maria Santos present to support full comprehension of findings given mother's preference to review results in detail in Spanish. A written summary will be provided in Spanish translation per family request, coordinated through Piedmont CDSA.

Report prepared by:

Jessica Chen, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Raleigh, NC
August 22, 2026
