text:
TRIANGLE BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE THERAPY, PLLC

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

HEADER INFORMATION

- Client Name: Mateo Alejandro Vasquez Ortiz ("Teo")
- Date of Birth: 06/14/2021
- Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;8
- Evaluation Dates: 3 de marzo de 2026 and el martes 4 de junio de 2026 (follow-up observation)
- Referral Date: 01/09/2026
- Report Date: June 10, 2026
- Clinician: Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (English/Spanish)
- Employer: Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC, also referred to in this report as Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language or TBSLT
- Medicaid ID: 804552913A
- Insurance Member ID: BCB22981540
- NC ITP Child ID: ITP-0411782
- Clinical Record Number: TBSLT-00938
- Prior Authorization Number: PA-2026-04471

REFERRAL AND IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

- Mateo is a 4;8-year-old boy who was referred by Monica Reyes, service coordinator at the Wake County Children's Developmental Services Agency (CDSA), for a comprehensive speech and language evaluation.
- The referral followed a routine developmental screening at Little Sprouts Daycare and Preschool, where Teo's teacher, Ms. Ana Lopez, raised concerns about limited intelligibility and short sentence length compared to same-age peers.
- Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez; his father, Carlos Vasquez; and his older sister, Camila Vasquez, age 7.
- The family's home address is 482 Juniper Hollow Lane, Garner, Wake County, ZIP 27529.
- Contact phone: (919) 555-0187. Contact email: lucia.rodriguez0614@fastmail.com.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

- This evaluation was conducted to determine Mateo's current speech and language skills and to guide eligibility and programming decisions through the NC Infant-Toddler Program.
- Information was gathered through parent interview, review of records, direct standardized testing, and classroom observation at Little Sprouts Daycare and Preschool.
- Lucía Rodríguez reported that she and her husband, Carlos Vasquez, are most concerned about Teo's difficulty being understood by unfamiliar listeners and his tendency to use gestures instead of words when frustrated.
- An interpreter, Gabriela Soto, assisted during portions of the parent interview conducted primarily in Spanish.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

- Mateo was born at 32 weeks gestational age at WakeMed Raleigh Campus on 06/14/2021, weighing 3 lb 12 oz.
- Apgar scores were 6 and 8 at one and five minutes, respectively.
- He spent six weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit at WakeMed Raleigh Campus under the care of neonatologist Dr. Rajesh Patel.
- Mother reported no maternal complications prior to the preterm delivery other than mild preeclampsia, which was managed medically.
- Mateo's pediatrician, Dr. Angela Kim, has followed him since discharge and reports that his growth has been within normal limits since August 2022.
- History is significant for recurrent otitis media, with four documented episodes between March 2023 and November 2024, treated with antibiotics and, eventually, bilateral myringotomy tubes placed on 01/18/2025 by Dr. Marcus Ellison, pediatric ENT.
- A hearing screening completed by audiologist Dr. Brian Walsh on 02/02/2025 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally following tube placement.
- No history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness is reported.
- Vision screening at the pediatrician's office on 04/15/2026 was within normal limits.
- Relevant diagnostic codes on file include F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, rule out) and F80.0 (phonological disorder).

FAMILY HISTORY AND HOME LANGUAGE ENVIRONMENT

- The home language environment is bilingual. Lucía Rodríguez reports speaking primarily Spanish with Mateo, while Carlos Vasquez uses a mix of English and Spanish.
- Camila is reported to be fluent in both languages and often serves as a language model and informal interpreter for her younger brother.
- Mateo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Ortiz, lives with the family three days a week and provides childcare; she speaks only Spanish with Teo.
- A family friend, Yesenia Flores, occasionally babysits in the evenings and reports similar concerns about Teo's intelligibility.
- Lucía Rodríguez works at Sunrise Medical Billing Solutions, and Carlos Vasquez works at Precision Auto Parts of Raleigh.
- Family history is positive for speech delay: Carlos Vasquez reports that he himself received speech therapy as a child, and a paternal uncle was described as a "late talker."
- The family's dog, Rocky, is frequently mentioned by Mateo and appears to be a strong motivator during play-based tasks.
- The family receives support from Wake County WIC and has previously attended parenting classes through Smart Start of Wake County.

DEVELOPMENTAL AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

- Gross and fine motor milestones were reported as age-appropriate, with independent walking achieved around 14 months (corrected age).
- First words were reported around 18 months, with slow vocabulary growth noted by the family and by early intervention staff.
- Mateo received early intervention services through the NC Infant-Toddler Program from September 2023 through June 2024, including monthly developmental therapy visits.
- He currently attends Little Sprouts Daycare and Preschool five days a week, where his primary teacher is Ms. Ana Lopez and his classroom aide is Mr. David Nguyen.
- Classroom observation noted that Teo interacts well with peers, including a close friend named Ethan, but frequently defaults to pointing and gesture during group activities.
- Ms. Lopez reported that Teo is well liked but is sometimes excluded from pretend play because peers "don't understand him."

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

- Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner.
- Attention to task was adequate for structured activities but decreased during unstructured play, particularly when competing stimuli were present.
- Articulation was judged to be significantly reduced in intelligibility, estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners without context, improving to 70% with contextual cues.
- Mateo used primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations spontaneously; he used longer utterances only with moderate cues.
- He was observed to say "wabbit" for the target word "rabbit", and "nana" for "banana", consistent with the phonological patterns described below.
- When shown a photo of the family dog, Teo said, "where Rocky go?" demonstrating use of a wh-question frame.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND TEST RESULTS

- The following standardized and informal measures were administered in English and Spanish as appropriate, with results interpreted in light of Mateo's bilingual exposure:
  - Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
  - Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
  - Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax subtest
  - Oral-motor examination and informal speech sample analysis
  - Parent and teacher questionnaires

| Measure | Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equivalent | 95% Confidence Interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 | Auditory Comprehension | 73 | 4th | 2;6–3;0 | 68-78 |
| PLS-5 | Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd | 2;3–2;9 | 63-73 |
| PLS-5 | Total Language Score | 70 | 2nd | 2;4–2;10 | 65-75 |
| GFTA-3 | Sounds-in-Words | 71 | 3rd | 2;8–3;2 | 66-76 |
| BESA | Morphosyntax | 65 | 1st | — | 60-70 |

- On the GFTA-3, Mateo demonstrated consistent substitution of /k/ and /g/ with /t/ and /d/, consistent with fronting, and liquid gliding of /r/ and /l/ to [w].
- Final consonant deletion was noted in 8/10 trials, and cluster reduction occurred in 3 of 5 opportunities.
- Spanish phoneme inventory showed inconsistent production of the trill /r/ and the tap [ɾ], both produced as [l].
- A connected speech sample of 50 utterances yielded a mean length of utterance of 2.3 morphemes in English and 2.6 morphemes in Spanish, both below expected ranges for his age.
- Receptive vocabulary tasks showed stronger performance in Spanish than in English, with Teo correctly identifying 18/20 items in Spanish compared to 12/20 in English.
- Oral-motor examination revealed adequate structure and function, with no evidence of dysarthria or significant oral-motor weakness.
- Diadochokinetic rates and non-speech oral movements were within functional limits.
- During structured tasks, Mateo required min cues to max cues to produce target sounds in isolation and syllables, and mod cues to generalize those sounds to words.

SESSION SCHEDULE

The following schedule reflects direct treatment sessions proposed under this evaluation, pending authorization PA-2026-04471:

| Day | Start Time | End Time | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:30 AM | Little Sprouts Daycare and Preschool, Room 2, 118 Acorn Grove Road, Garner |
| Wednesday | 1:15 PM | 1:45 PM | Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language clinic office, 3400 Westfield Court, Suite 210, Raleigh, 27612 |
| Friday | 10:00 AM | 10:45 AM | Home visit, 482 Juniper Hollow Lane, Garner |

- A make-up session was held on el martes 4 de junio at 11:00 AM at the clinic office due to a scheduling conflict at the daycare.
- Transportation to the Wednesday session is coordinated by Rosa Ortiz when Lucía Rodríguez is unavailable.

IMPRESSIONS

- Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and direct observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (F80.2) and a moderate-to-severe phonological disorder (F80.0).
- Deficits are present across both languages, which rules out typical second-language acquisition as the primary explanation for his profile; this supports a true language disorder rather than a language difference.
- Teo's reduced intelligibility and limited expressive language are significantly impacting his participation with peers, including Ethan, and his ability to be understood by unfamiliar listeners such as extended family and community members.
- Prognosis for improvement with consistent, bilingual intervention is considered good, given Mateo's strong engagement, intact hearing, and supportive family involvement.
- Continued monitoring of middle ear status is recommended given the history of recurrent otitis media and tube placement.

RECOMMENDATIONS

- Mateo qualifies for and should receive individual speech-language therapy services twice weekly for 30 minutes per session, targeting phonological processes and expressive syntax, provided by a bilingual clinician through TBSLT.
- Treatment should use a combination of Cycles phonological approach for speech sound production and Hanen-based strategies to support expressive language in daily routines.
- A trial of PROMPT techniques is recommended to address persistent substitution patterns affecting intelligibility.
- Continued coordination with Little Sprouts Daycare and Preschool staff, including Ms. Lopez and Mr. Nguyen, is recommended to support carryover of targets into the classroom.
- Family members, including Lucía Rodríguez, Carlos Vasquez, Rosa Ortiz, and Camila Vasquez, should receive coaching in bilingual language facilitation strategies to use during daily routines at home.
- Referral back to Dr. Angela Kim is recommended to confirm resolution of middle ear effusion at the next well-child visit.
- Reassessment is recommended in 6 months to monitor progress and update the plan of care.
- Continued eligibility and service coordination through Monica Reyes at the Wake County CDSA is recommended to ensure continuity of services.

BILLING AND AUTHORIZATION

- Services under this plan will be billed under procedure code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production and language) and 92507 (individual treatment).
- This evaluation was billed to Medicaid ID 804552913A and secondary insurance Member ID BCB22981540.
- Authorization for ongoing services has been requested under number PA-2026-04471, referencing clinical record TBSLT-00938 and NC ITP Child ID ITP-0411782.

This report was prepared by Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist, on behalf of Triangle Bilingual Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC (TBSLT). Questions regarding this report may be directed to the clinic office at (919) 555-0241 or jhayes@trianglebilingualslp.com.

CAROLINA BILINGUAL SPEECH & HEARING ASSOCIATES, PLLC
Serving Children and Families Across the Triangle

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION

Client Name: Mateo Hernández Rodríguez
Date of Birth: August 14, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Dates of Evaluation: October 2, 2025 and October 9, 2025
Date of Report: October 16, 2025
Parents/Guardians: Lucía Rodríguez Pérez (mother) and Carlos Hernández Flores (father)
Home Address: 412 Chestnut Ridge Lane, Durham, NC 27705
Home Phone: (919) 555-0148
Medicaid ID: 748203561B
Case/Record Number: AD-10492
Referral Source: Dr. Nguyen, pediatrician
Evaluating Clinician: Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Bilingual Speech & Hearing Associates, PLLC
Service Coordinator: Miss Ana, Agencia de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios de Intervención Temprana del Triángulo (ADISIT)

2. REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Nguyen following concerns raised at his four-year well-child visit. His mother, Lucía, reported that Mateo is difficult to understand even by familiar listeners, and that his teacher at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center noted limited participation during circle time and group songs. The family currently receives early intervention support coordinated through ADISIT, and this evaluation was requested both to document current functioning and to update Mateo's Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) ahead of his annual review.

3. BACKGROUND AND DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY

3.1 Birth and Medical History

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Pinewood Regional Medical Center following an uncomplicated pregnancy and vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 6 lbs, 14 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, respectively. Lucía reported no maternal illness, medication use, or substance exposure during pregnancy. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening prior to discharge and has had no hospitalizations or surgeries since birth. Between 12 months and 18 months of age he experienced three episodes of otitis media, each treated successfully with oral antibiotics; no tympanostomy tubes were placed, and no episodes have recurred since March 2023. A recent audiological evaluation completed on September 20, 2025 confirmed hearing within normal limits bilaterally, with normal tympanometry. Lucía also reported that Mateo is a picky eater but has no diagnosed feeding or swallowing concerns, and that gross and fine motor milestones were met within expected ranges.

3.2 Family and Language History

Mateo lives at home with his parents and his older sister, Sol, age 7, who attends Riverside Elementary School in Durham. The household is bilingual: Lucía and the family's longtime babysitter, doña Lupe, speak primarily Spanish with Mateo, while Carlos and Sol frequently speak English with him at home. Lucía estimated that Mateo's daily language exposure is roughly balanced between Spanish and English. She described his early milestones as delayed relative to his sister's: his first words emerged around 22 months, and he was not reliably combining two words until approximately 3 years of age. Carlos added that Mateo often uses gestures and pulls family members toward objects he wants rather than naming them.

Doña Lupe, a neighbor who has cared for the children since infancy, provides childcare three afternoons each week while Carlos works at Triangle Builders Construction LLC and Lucía attends evening nursing classes. Mateo sees his cousins, Diego and Valentina, most weekends at extended-family gatherings, where Lucía reports he tends to play alongside rather than with the other children. The family's dog, Rocky, a golden retriever, is described as Mateo's constant companion and reportedly sits beside him during home practice of speech homework.

4. ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND TEST RESULTS

Assessment procedures included standardized testing, a spontaneous language sample, an oral-motor examination, parent interview, and clinical observation across both evaluation sessions. Testing was conducted primarily in English with Spanish supports offered as needed given Mateo's bilingual exposure; no significant difference in performance was noted across languages. Mateo was cooperative and engaged throughout both sessions, though he required frequent redirection to task.

4.1 Standardized Test Results

| Measure | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Descriptive Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) – Auditory Comprehension | 76 | 5th | Below Average |
| PLS-5 – Expressive Communication | 71 | 3rd | Below Average |
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3) | 68 | 2nd | Below Average |
| Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3) – Core Language | 73 | 4th | Below Average |

Ninety-five percent confidence intervals for the PLS-5 composite scores ranged from 65-79 for Expressive Communication and 69-83 for Auditory Comprehension. Age-equivalent scores for receptive language fell within the 2;6–3;0 range, roughly 18-20 months below his chronological age.

4.2 Speech Sound Production

Analysis of the GFTA-3 revealed multiple sound errors affecting overall intelligibility, estimated at approximately 40% intelligible to unfamiliar listeners in connected speech. Mateo demonstrated final consonant deletion, stopping of fricatives, and cluster reduction across both English and Spanish productions. He produced /k/ as [t] in word-initial position and consistently omitted /s/ in consonant clusters. During a stimulability probe, Mateo attempted the target word for "sun" and said "tol" for the target "sol", substituting /t/ for /s/. With moderate cues, he self-corrected to an approximation closer to [soʊ]. He produced 8/10 trials of word-final /n/ correctly but only 3 of 10 trials of word-initial /s/ clusters, and 5/10 trials of the liquid /ɾ/ in medial position.

4.3 Language Sampling

A fifty-utterance language sample was collected during play-based interaction with blocks and a toy kitchen set. Mean length of utterance was 2.4 morphemes, below expectations for his age. Mateo relied primarily on two- and three-word combinations and supplemented limited verbal output with gesture and pointing. He required minimal to moderate cues to answer wh-questions accurately and demonstrated notable difficulty retelling a simple three-step sequence of events, managing only 1 of 3 steps independently.

5. BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo separated easily from his mother at both sessions and engaged readily with Jennifer Alvarez throughout testing. He brought a stuffed dinosaur from Little Sprouts Early Learning Center to the second session, which he reported his classmates Emily and Jayden had given him for his birthday. His teacher, la maestra Carmen, and classroom aide, Mr. Tom, both report by phone consultation that Mateo is social and affectionate but becomes frustrated when peers do not understand his requests, occasionally resulting in grabbing toys or pushing. At home, Lucía and doña Lupe note similar frustration when Mateo cannot make himself understood to his sister, Sol, during play.

6. CURRENT SERVICE SCHEDULE

Mateo currently receives speech-language therapy twice weekly through ADISIT, per the schedule below.

| Day | Start Time | End Time | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | Little Sprouts Early Learning Center |
| Wednesday | 3:30 PM | 4:15 PM | Carolina Bilingual Speech & Hearing Associates, PLLC clinic, Chapel Hill |
| Friday | 10:00 AM | 10:30 AM | ADISIT community office, Durham |

7. CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Results of this evaluation indicate that Mateo presents with a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder and a Speech Sound Disorder affecting intelligibility in both English and Spanish. His standardized scores fall more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean across receptive and expressive domains, and his articulation skills are significantly delayed relative to age expectations. Diagnostic impressions are consistent with ICD-10 code F80.2 (Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder) and F80.0 (Phonological Disorder). Billing for this evaluation is reflected under CPT code 92523.

Mateo's bilingual exposure does not account for the magnitude of his delays, as difficulties are present across both languages per parent report and classroom observation from la maestra Carmen. Family and caregiver involvement, including from doña Lupe and Carlos, remains a clear strength supporting ongoing intervention, as does Mateo's motivation during structured play tasks.

8. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Continue individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, transitioning toward a Hanen-based coaching model so Lucía and Carlos can embed language stimulation strategies into daily routines.
2. Introduce PROMPT techniques to address motor-based articulation errors, particularly cluster reduction and stopping of fricatives.
3. Consider a brief Cycles approach trial targeting final consonant deletion given its persistence across both languages.
4. Update IFSP Outcome 1 (expressive language) and IFSP Outcome 3 (speech intelligibility) to reflect current present levels; Outcome 2 (social play with peers) may be discontinued given adequate progress noted by Jennifer Alvarez.
5. Coordinate with Little Sprouts Early Learning Center staff, including la maestra Carmen and Mr. Tom, to implement visual supports during circle time and structured turn-taking opportunities with peers such as Emily and Jayden.
6. Encourage continued Spanish-language modeling from Lucía and doña Lupe, as bilingual exposure should be supported rather than reduced.
7. Re-evaluate in 6 months to monitor progress and determine continued eligibility for services through ADISIT.

9. IFSP OUTCOMES

The family's current IFSP, last reviewed on April 11, 2025, includes three outcomes. IFSP Outcome 1 addresses expressive vocabulary growth across both languages; IFSP Outcome 2 addresses turn-taking in play with peers, including Emily and Jayden; and IFSP Outcome 3 addresses speech sound intelligibility for familiar and unfamiliar listeners. The next IFSP review is scheduled for April 11, 2026.

This report was prepared by Jennifer Alvarez, M.S., CCC-SLP, and may be shared with ADISIT, Dr. Nguyen, and Little Sprouts Early Learning Center with parental consent. Questions may be directed to Carolina Bilingual Speech & Hearing Associates, PLLC at (919) 555-0172 or jalvarez@carolinabilingualslp.com.

October 9, 2026

Dear Lucía Hernández Gómez and Francisco López Ramírez,
Estimados Lucía Hernández Gómez y Francisco López Ramírez,

Thank you for meeting with us on October 2, 2026 for María José Hernández López's annual IFSP review. It was wonderful to see how much Majo has grown since her last review. This letter is a summary of what we talked about, written in plain language so that it is easy to read and share with anyone who helps your family. Gracias por reunirse con nosotros para hablar sobre el progreso de María José, a quien todos en casa llaman cariñosamente "Majo."

**Quién estuvo en la reunión / Who was at the meeting**

We were glad to have so many people who care about Majo at the table. Ana Patricia Ruiz, your service coordinator from CDSA of the Piedmont Triad, led the meeting and can be reached at (336) 555-0199 or ana.ruiz@cdsapiedmont.org. I am Daniela Ortiz, your bilingual speech-language pathologist, and I work with Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC, the agency that sends me to your home each week. Carlos Vega joined us as our Spanish interpreter so that both of you could participate fully, aunque sé que ustedes dos entienden y hablan inglés bastante bien también. Michelle Tran, the occupational therapist, and Sarah Jennings, the physical therapist, also attended, along with Melissa Owens, who teaches Majo's classroom at Kernersville Early Head Start Center.

**Nuestra familia / About our family**

María José Hernández López was born on August 14, 2024, a few weeks early at 35 weeks gestation, weighing 5 lbs, 2 oz at birth. She is now 26 months old. She lives at 1420 Weatherstone Drive in Winston-Salem, 27107, in Forsyth County, with both of her parents and her two older brothers. Her big brother Juan Carlos Hernández López, known to everyone as "Juanito," is nine years old and in Ms. Diane Carter's third-grade classroom at Easton Elementary School, part of Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Schools. Her other brother, José Luis Hernández López, whom the family calls "Pepe," is four and attends a Head Start preschool program nearby.

Lucía Hernández Gómez told us, "estoy en casa con los niños casi todo el tiempo, pero trabajo medio tiempo en las tardes." She works part-time afternoon shifts at Case Farms poultry plant while Francisco López Ramírez works full-time in framing and drywall for Blue Ridge Construction Group. Because their work schedules overlap on some days, Majo's grandmother, Guadalupe Martínez Soto, known in the family as "Lupita," helps with childcare several afternoons a week. Majo's uncle, Jesús Ramírez Castro, called "Chuy" by everyone, also stops by on weekends and is one of Majo's favorite playmates. Her cousin Mateo Hernández Ruiz, nicknamed "Teo," is close in age to Pepe and the two boys often play together with Majo and the family dog, Rocky, in the backyard.

Lucía Hernández Gómez shared, "a veces me preocupa que Majo no hable tanto como sus hermanos a su edad. Juanito ya hablaba mucho a los dos años, y Majo todavía dice pocas palabras." She also said, in English, "I just want her to be able to tell me what she needs before she gets frustrated." Francisco López Ramírez added, "y cuando estamos en la casa de mi mamá, Lupita dice que entiende poco de lo que Majo trata de decir."

**Lo que nos importa a nosotros como familia / Our family's concerns and priorities**

During the meeting, Lucía Hernández Gómez and Francisco López Ramírez told us that their top priorities are: (1) helping Majo use more words so she is not frustrated, (2) making sure she can communicate with both grandparents and extended family in Spanish and with her teachers in English, and (3) understanding what to expect before she starts preschool. "Queremos que ella pueda jugar y comunicarse con sus primos y con sus maestras, en los dos idiomas," said Lucía Hernández Gómez. Francisco López Ramírez added that he hopes Majo will be ready to join her brother Pepe's preschool program next fall.

**La rutina diaria / Daily routines**

Understanding Majo's daily routine helps us build strategies that fit naturally into family life. Majo wakes up around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with her brothers around 7:00 a.m., often tortillas con huevo or cereal. Francisco López Ramírez drops Juanito at Easton Elementary School before heading to work, and Lucía Hernández Gómez takes Majo to Kernersville Early Head Start Center by 8:30 a.m.. Majo naps at the center around 12:30 p.m. and comes home by 3:30 p.m., where she plays with Pepe, Teo, and Rocky until dinner, usually around 6:00 p.m.. Bath time is around 7:30 p.m., and she is in bed by 8:00 p.m.. On weekends, the family often visits Lupita and Chuy, where Majo hears a lot of Spanish conversation and plays with cousins.

**Otras agencias que ayudan a nuestra familia / Other agencies supporting our family**

Several agencies are part of Majo's circle of support. The family has been working with Forsyth County Department of Social Services, often called "DSS" for short, for help with housing assistance paperwork. Lucía Hernández Gómez also receives nutrition support through Forsyth County WIC Program, and the family was connected to parenting classes through Smart Start of Forsyth County. Majo attends her classroom through Forsyth Early Head Start, which funds her placement at Kernersville Early Head Start Center. Because the family primarily speaks Spanish at home, CDSA of the Piedmont Triad also referred them to the Centro de Recursos para Familias Latinas de Carolina del Norte (CRFLCN) for additional translation support and community resources. CRFLCN has helped the family understand school enrollment paperwork for Pepe's upcoming preschool transition and connected Francisco López Ramírez with a workers' rights workshop.

Majo's pediatrician, Dr. Robert Kim at Forsyth Medical Center, has been monitoring her growth and referred the family for this early intervention evaluation after noticing delayed babbling at her 18-month well-child visit.

**Lo que encontramos en la evaluación / Evaluation results**

On September 30, 2026, I administered the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) in both English and Spanish, alternating by context to capture Majo's full language skills. On the Auditory Comprehension subtest, she earned a standard score of 73, within the range of 70-80, placing her at the 4th percentile. On Expressive Communication, she earned a standard score of 68, also at the 2nd percentile, with an age equivalent of 14 months. Her chronological age at testing was 2;1. Michelle Tran's sensory profile screening showed typical results, and Sarah Jennings noted that gross motor skills are age-appropriate.

During play-based assessment, Majo used approximately 12 single words consistently across English and Spanish, including "agua," "pan," "más," "no," and "up." She combined two words together in only 1 of 10 opportunities, far below the expected 8 of 10 for her age. She imitated target words with moderate verbal cues about 60% of the time, and spontaneously produced words independently in 3 of 10 trials. Based on these results and parent report, Majo meets eligibility criteria under F80.9 for a developmental delay in expressive and receptive communication.

**Resultados del IFSP: metas y estrategias / IFSP outcomes and strategies**

Based on your family's priorities, we developed the following outcomes together.

**Outcome 1:** Majo will use two-word combinations in both English and Spanish to request and comment during daily routines, increasing from 1 of 10 to 6 of 10 opportunities within six months. Strategies include using the Hanen "OWL" approach (Observe, Wait, Listen) during mealtime and play, modeling bilingual two-word phrases such as "más agua" and "more milk," and pausing expectantly before handing Majo a preferred item so she has a chance to communicate first. Lucía Hernández Gómez and Francisco López Ramírez agreed to practice this during breakfast and bath time, and Lupita will be shown the same strategy so she can use it during her afternoons with Majo.

**Outcome 2:** Majo will follow simple one-step directions in both languages with no more than minimal cues, improving from 40% to 80% accuracy within six months. Strategies include giving one direction at a time paired with a gesture, such as "ven aquí" with an open-arm gesture, and celebrating any attempt enthusiastically to build confidence. Ms. Melissa Owens will use the same strategy in the classroom, where Majo's classmates Emily Carter and Bryson Daniels often model language during group activities.

**Outcome 3:** Majo will be understood by familiar and unfamiliar listeners in both English and Spanish to prepare for her transition to preschool next year. We will use a combination of PROMPT tactile cueing to support clearer consonant production, targeting early sounds like /p/, /m/, and /b/, and will track her progress monthly. Family will be encouraged to narrate daily routines in whichever language feels most natural, since building a strong first language actually supports the second.

**Frecuencia y duración del servicio / Service frequency and duration**

Speech-language therapy will continue at a frequency of two 45-minute sessions per week in the home, billed under CPT 92507, beginning October 16, 2026 and continuing through the next annual review. Occupational therapy consultation with Michelle Tran will occur monthly, and physical therapy monitoring with Sarah Jennings will occur quarterly, per the team's recommendation. Service coordination through Ana Patricia Ruiz at CDSA of the Piedmont Triad will continue at least every six months, or sooner if the family has concerns; her direct line is (336) 555-0199.

**Fechas importantes / Important dates**

Majo's original IFSP was written on October 22, 2024, shortly after her referral. This annual review took place on October 2, 2026. Her next full annual review is scheduled for October 2, 2027, with a six-month check-in planned for April 9, 2027. Please keep this letter with your other IFSP paperwork. Her Medicaid identification number is NC4487213J, and her CDSA case number is CDSA-2024-00871, which you may need when speaking with any of the agencies listed above.

**Cómo comunicarse con nosotros / How to reach us**

If you have any questions before our next visit, please call our office at (336) 555-0142 or reach Ana Patricia Ruiz directly at ana.ruiz@cdsapiedmont.org. Gracias de nuevo por confiar en nosotros con el cuidado y el desarrollo de Majo. Es un privilegio trabajar con una familia tan dedicada, y estamos aquí para apoyarlos en cada paso.

With warm regards / Con cariño,

Daniela Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC

Fuente de referencia: Dr. Robert Kim, pediatra, y la coordinadora de servicios Angela Rivas de CDSA del Piedmont Occidental

RAZÓN DE LA REFERENCIA

María José de la Cruz Soto fue referida al Little Learners Program por su pediatra, el Dr. Robert Kim, después de una visita de rutina en la que la madre, Patricia Soto, expresó preocupación por el habla y el lenguaje de Majo. Según la madre, Majo usa principalmente palabras sueltas y gestos, y rara vez combina dos o más palabras. La maestra de María José, la Srta. Combs-Whitley, también notó en Escuela Primaria Laurel Hollow que la niña tiene dificultad para seguir instrucciones de dos pasos y que su habla es difícil de entender para adultos que no la conocen bien. El padre, Eduardo de la Cruz, reportó que en casa Majo se frustra con facilidad cuando no la entienden y a veces se tira al piso o llora. La coordinadora de servicios del CDSA del Piedmont Occidental, Angela Rivas, solicitó esta evaluación bilingüe para determinar elegibilidad para servicios de habla-lenguaje bajo el IFSP de la familia y para actualizar el Resultado 2 del plan actual, relacionado con comunicación funcional.

ANTECEDENTES DE NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO

Majo nació a las 39 semanas de gestación mediante parto vaginal sin complicaciones mayores, con un peso al nacer de 3,180 gramos y puntuaciones de Apgar de 8 y 9. No requirió ingreso a la unidad neonatal. La madre reportó un embarazo sin complicaciones, aunque mencionó haber tenido presión arterial ligeramente elevada en el tercer trimestre, controlada sin medicamento. Los hitos motores gruesos se alcanzaron dentro de rangos típicos: se sentó sola a los 6 meses y caminó sin apoyo a los 13 meses. Sin embargo, los hitos del lenguaje se retrasaron: según la madre, Majo dijo sus primeras palabras alrededor de los 18 meses y aún no combina frases de dos palabras de manera consistente a los 4;2. La familia completó previamente un cuestionario de desarrollo con la abuela materna, Rosa Jiménez, quien cuida a Majo tres días por semana mientras los padres trabajan.

HISTORIA MÉDICA

María José ha tenido múltiples episodios de otitis media, con tres tratamientos de antibiótico documentados entre los 18 y 30 meses de edad. Se le colocaron tubos de ventilación (miringotomía) el 9 de febrero de 2024 por el otorrinolaringólogo del grupo médico local; desde entonces, los episodios han disminuido notablemente. Una evaluación audiológica reciente, realizada el 2 de abril de 2026, mostró audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos, con timpanogramas tipo A bilaterales. La visión fue evaluada como normal en su revisión pediátrica más reciente. No toma medicamentos de forma regular. El Dr. Robert Kim documentó un diagnóstico de F80.1 (trastorno del desarrollo del lenguaje, tipo expresivo) en el expediente médico, pendiente de confirmación con esta evaluación. La familia también recibe servicios de terapia ocupacional por sensibilidad táctil leve, coordinados por Jennifer Alvarado, OTR/L, y terapia física para debilidad de tono muscular en el tronco, a cargo de Thomas Nguyen, PT, DPT, ambos a través del mismo CDSA del Piedmont Occidental. Las sesiones de terapia del habla anteriores, facturadas bajo el código 92523 (evaluación) y el código 92507 (tratamiento individual), comenzaron en enero y se interrumpieron en marzo por motivos de transporte.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE IDIOMAS

Majo vive en 214 Birchwood Lane, Marrow Creek, NC 28655, en el condado de Ashcombe, con sus padres y dos hermanos. Su hermano mayor, Diego de la Cruz Soto, tiene seis años y asiste a primer grado en la misma escuela. Su hermana menor, Valentina de la Cruz Soto, tiene un año y aún no habla. La abuela materna, Rosa Jiménez, vive cerca y ayuda con el cuidado de los niños varios días a la semana; según la madre, Rosa le habla a Majo casi exclusivamente en español.

[X] Hogar  [X] Guardería  [ ] Con la abuela a tiempo completo  [ ] Otro

La madre, Patricia Soto, trabaja como recepcionista en Marrow Creek Family Dentistry y habla español e inglés con fluidez. El padre, Eduardo de la Cruz, trabaja en producción en Ashcombe Furniture Works y prefiere comunicarse en español, aunque entiende inglés básico. En el hogar:

[X] Español como idioma principal  [X] Inglés como segundo idioma  [ ] Solo inglés  [ ] Solo español

La madre reportó que ella y el padre hablan español con Majo y con sus hermanos la mayoría del tiempo, pero que Diego empezó a usar más inglés desde que entró a primer grado, y que a veces mezcla ambos idiomas al dirigirse a su hermana. Majo asiste a Little Learners Daycare cuatro días a la semana, de 8:00 a.m. a 4:30 p.m., donde el personal le habla principalmente en inglés. Según la directora de la guardería, Majo entiende instrucciones simples en inglés pero responde casi siempre en español o con gestos. En Little Learners Daycare, su mejor amiga es Sofía, una niña de edad similar con quien juega durante el recreo. La familia también convive con el perro de la casa, Canela, a quien Majo menciona con frecuencia durante las sesiones.

No hay historial familiar reportado de trastornos del habla o lenguaje en los padres; sin embargo, la madre mencionó que un tío materno tuvo "problemas para hablar" de niño y recibió terapia, aunque no recuerda detalles diagnósticos.

OBSERVACIÓN CONDUCTUAL

La evaluación se llevó a cabo en el hogar de la familia durante dos sesiones, con la participación de la intérprete Marisol Peña para apoyar la comunicación con la familia y verificar la interpretación de instrucciones de las pruebas. Majo se mostró inicialmente tímida, escondiéndose detrás de su madre, pero se calentó rápido una vez que se le ofrecieron juguetes y libros. Durante el juego libre, interactuó con figuras de animales y nombró varias en español ("perro", "gato", "vaca"), aunque con articulación poco clara. En un momento, mientras jugaba con un perro de juguete, dijo "Canela come", refiriéndose a su mascota real.

[X] Cooperó con la mayoría de las tareas  [ ] Se negó a participar  [ ] Requirió descansos frecuentes

El contacto visual fue apropiado y respondió a su nombre de forma consistente. Mostró atención conjunta con adultos y buscó aprobación después de completar tareas. La vecina de la familia, Diane, quien ayuda con el transporte de los niños algunos días, estuvo presente brevemente durante la primera sesión y confirmó observaciones similares sobre la comunicación de Majo fuera del hogar.

RESULTADOS DE LA EVALUACIÓN

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas, con apoyo de interpretación según fue necesario:

Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish Edition
- Comprensión Auditiva: puntuación estándar de 76 (70-82, IC del 95%), percentil 5
- Expresión del Lenguaje: puntuación estándar de 68 (61-75, IC del 95%), percentil 2
- Puntuación Compuesta del Lenguaje Total: 70, percentil 2
- Edad equivalente de lenguaje expresivo: 2;6–3;0

Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3)
- Conceptos y Siguiendo Direcciones: puntuación escalar de 6
- Estructura de Oraciones: puntuación escalar de 4
- Vocabulario Expresivo: puntuación escalar de 5

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Sonidos en palabras: puntuación estándar de 72, percentil 3

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (datos complementarios de habilidades pragmáticas tempranas)
- Desempeño consistente con edad equivalente de 24 meses en áreas pragmáticas e interacción.

Durante la administración, Majo requirió claves moderadas (mod cues) para completar ítems de seguimiento de instrucciones de dos pasos, y logró 3 de 5 ítems correctos con apoyo visual adicional. En tareas de nombrar objetos, respondió correctamente en 8/10 ítems cuando se le dio la opción de responder en español, comparado con 4/10 cuando se requería respuesta en inglés, lo cual sugiere que su desempeño en inglés refleja exposición limitada más que un déficit primario en ese idioma.

ARTICULACIÓN Y FONOLOGÍA

Majo presenta un inventario fonético reducido para su edad. Omite consonantes finales en aproximadamente el 60% de las palabras monosilábicas y bisilábicas, y simplifica grupos consonánticos (por ejemplo, "pato" por "plato"). Sustituye el fonema /ɾ/ por [w] en posición inicial e intervocálica, como en "wojo" por "rojo". También muestra procesos de frontalización velar, sustituyendo /k/ por /t/ en algunas palabras. Su inteligibilidad fue estimada en aproximadamente 40% para oyentes no familiarizados y 70% para su madre, quien frecuentemente interpreta sus intentos comunicativos.

Durante una muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, se transcribió el siguiente intercambio, codificado con convenciones SALT:

Madre: "¿Qué quieres?"
Majo: "agua [EW]" (buscando la palabra correcta)
Madre: "¿Quieres agua?"
Majo: "sí, agua"

En otro momento, al señalar un dibujo de un perro, dijo "guau guau" en lugar del nombre del animal, consistente con uso limitado de vocabulario convencional para su edad.

LENGUAJE: SEMÁNTICA, SINTAXIS Y PRAGMÁTICA

El vocabulario expresivo de Majo se limita principalmente a sustantivos familiares (comida, animales, miembros de la familia) y algunos verbos de alta frecuencia. Combina dos palabras de forma ocasional ("mamá agua", "no quiero"), pero rara vez produce oraciones de tres o más palabras. No usa marcadores gramaticales como artículos o plurales de manera consistente, y omite verbos copulativos. En términos pragmáticos, inicia interacciones comunicativas con adultos familiares, pero tiene dificultad para reparar malentendidos cuando no se le comprende; en esos momentos, suele señalar, repetir la misma palabra con mayor volumen, o frustrarse.

Durante el juego simbólico con la intérprete, Marisol Peña observó que Majo seguía el modelo de juego de adultos pero rara vez iniciaba temas nuevos de manera verbal. En la escuela, según la Srta. Combs-Whitley, María José juega principalmente con un compañero, Liam, durante actividades estructuradas, pero se mantiene al margen de juegos grupales más complejos que requieren negociación verbal.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Los resultados de esta evaluación bilingüe son consistentes con un trastorno del desarrollo del lenguaje de tipo mixto (receptivo-expresivo), con un componente fonológico significativo, equivalente al código diagnóstico F80.2. El desempeño de María José de la Cruz Soto en ambos dominios, comprensión y expresión, cae por debajo de -1.5 desviaciones estándar en comparación con normas en español para su edad, y sus patrones de habla muestran procesos fonológicos que afectan significativamente la inteligibilidad. No se observó evidencia de que las dificultades se expliquen únicamente por exposición limitada a un segundo idioma: su desempeño en español, su idioma dominante y de mayor exposición en el hogar, también se encuentra por debajo de lo esperado para su edad.

[X] Se recomienda elegibilidad para servicios de habla-lenguaje  [ ] No se recomienda elegibilidad  [ ] Se requiere reevaluación

Las dificultades observadas afectan la participación de Majo tanto en el hogar como en Little Learners Daycare y en su salón de Escuela Primaria Laurel Hollow, y es probable que continúen impactando su desarrollo social y preacadémico sin intervención.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda terapia de habla-lenguaje individual dos veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos, a través de Little Learners Program, con enfoque bilingüe que priorice el español como idioma dominante mientras se apoya el desarrollo del inglés de forma paralela.

2. Se recomienda el uso del enfoque Cycles Approach para abordar los procesos fonológicos identificados, junto con estrategias del modelo Hanen para fomentar la comunicación funcional en el hogar, dado el alto nivel de involucramiento de los padres.

3. Se sugiere introducir apoyos visuales básicos inspirados en PECS para reducir la frustración comunicativa en momentos de alta demanda, especialmente en la transición entre el hogar y Little Learners Daycare.

4. Se recomienda actualizar el Resultado 2 y agregar un nuevo Resultado 3 del IFSP relacionado específicamente con inteligibilidad del habla y combinación de palabras, con revisión en seis meses.

5. Se recomienda continuar la coordinación con terapia ocupacional (Jennifer Alvarado) y terapia física (Thomas Nguyen) para asegurar un plan de servicios integrado, y mantener comunicación con el pediatra, Dr. Robert Kim, respecto al progreso.

6. Se recomienda que la familia continúe exponiendo a Majo consistentemente al español en el hogar, incluyendo con la abuela, Rosa Jiménez, y que el personal de Little Learners Daycare reciba orientación básica sobre estrategias de apoyo bilingüe, en coordinación con la maestra, Srta. Combs-Whitley.

7. Se recomienda solicitar apoyo adicional a través de la oficina de WIC del condado de Ashcombe si la familia necesita recursos nutricionales durante este periodo de servicios intensivos, según lo discutido con la coordinadora de servicios, Angela Rivas.

8. Se recomienda reevaluación formal en un año, o antes si el progreso no es el esperado, para determinar continuidad de elegibilidad y actualizar metas.

Esta evaluación y sus recomendaciones fueron discutidas con la familia, con el apoyo de la intérprete Marisol Peña, el 15 de mayo de 2026. Los padres, Patricia Soto y Eduardo de la Cruz, expresaron estar de acuerdo con el plan propuesto y firmaron el consentimiento informado correspondiente.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT / INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Child / Niña: María José Fernández Castillo ("Majo")
Date of Birth: April 9, 2022
Age at Evaluation: 4;2
Record ID: SLP-22819-C
Medicaid ID: 987654321A
Date of Referral: November 18, 2025
Dates of Evaluation: December 2, 2025 and December 9, 2025
Evaluator: Melissa Hwang, M.S., CCC-SLP
Interpreter: Carmen Ríos
Referring Provider: Dr. Amanda Singh, Pediatrics

Majo arrived to her first appointment on December 2, 2025 at 9:30 a.m. holding tight to the hand of her mother, Lucía Castillo Reyes, who had taken the morning off to bring her in. Majo is a 4;2-year-old girl referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by her pediatrician, Dr. Amanda Singh, after a well-child visit in which Lucía Castillo Reyes voiced concern that "Majo no se le entiende casi nada" — that almost nothing Majo says can be understood by people outside the family. The family was also referred by Brianna Lewis, Service Coordinator at Piedmont CDSA, where Majo has an open Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) dated August 14, 2025 with Outcome 2 addressing expressive language. This evaluation was requested to update that plan ahead of the annual review scheduled for January 20, 2026.

The family lives at 118 Spindle Court, Kannapolis, NC 28081, in Cabarrus County, in a house they share with Majo's maternal grandmother. Majo is the youngest of three; her older sister, Valentina Fernández Castillo, is in the fifth grade, and her little brother, Diego Fernández Castillo, is a toddler. Mamá, Lucía Castillo Reyes, works nights at Valle Verde Poultry, where she has been on the processing line for about three years; "trabajo de las once de la noche a las siete de la mañana," she explained — she works 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.. Papá, Javier Fernández Soto, trabaja para Triad Construction Co., una compañía de construcción, where he has worked as a framer since before Majo was born; on the days Javier Fernández Soto is not on a job site with Triad Construction Co., he picks the children up from school. Because both parents' schedules are demanding, Majo's maternal grandmother, Rosa Castillo Reyes, helps with daytime care; she also works a few lunch shifts a week as a cook at El Rancho Alegre, a restaurant near the home, el restaurante donde "todos me conocen." Majo's aunt, Marisol Castillo Reyes, who works as a cashier at Ahorra Más Grocery — la tienda Ahorra Más Grocery — frequently keeps Majo and her cousin, Ángel Castillo, on weekends. An uncle, Pedro Fernández Soto, works at Hilltop Family Farms, and the family sometimes visits him there on Saturdays, something Majo talks about often. When both parents and the grandmother are unavailable, a family friend, Yolanda Pérez, who is employed by Sparkle Clean Services, babysits Majo and her siblings in the evenings.

Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home. Lucía Castillo Reyes reported that Majo was exposed almost exclusively to Spanish until she began attending Los Patitos Felices at 26 months of age, where instruction is primarily in English with a bilingual assistant present part of the week. Lucía Castillo Reyes estimates Majo's current exposure at approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English, mostly through Los Patitos Felices, her sister Valentina Fernández Castillo, and children's programs on television. Javier Fernández Soto added that at home, "le hablamos en español, pero ella a veces contesta en inglés con su hermana" — they speak Spanish to her, but she sometimes answers her sister in English. No regression or loss of either language was reported. Lucía Castillo Reyes denied any family history of late talking, dyslexia, or developmental disability on either side, though she noted that Majo's cousin Ángel Castillo also received speech therapy as a toddler.

Majo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Cabarrus Valley Medical Center on April 9, 2022, following an uncomplicated pregnancy. Birth weight was 6 lbs 3 oz, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. Lucía Castillo Reyes reported no NICU stay and no feeding difficulties as an infant, though Majo had frequent ear infections between 8 months and 2 years of age, culminating in placement of bilateral pressure-equalization tubes at 22 months by Dr. Patel, an otolaryngologist. A follow-up hearing screening after the tube placement was within normal limits bilaterally. Majo passed her newborn hearing screening and has had no further hearing concerns reported. There is no history of seizures, head injury, or hospitalization beyond the tube placement procedure, which was billed under CPT 69436. Majo previously received speech-language services through Piedmont CDSA beginning at 30 months, initially evaluated by Ms. Ortiz, whose report noted a receptive-expressive gap consistent with a diagnosis of Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder, ICD-10 F80.2. Majo has received home-based early intervention speech therapy approximately weekly since that time, most recently using Hanen-based strategies and some structured PROMPT cueing for articulation.

Majo currently attends Los Patitos Felices five days a week from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., where her lead teacher, Ms. Patterson, and the assistant, Srta. Alvarez, both describe her as a sociable, affectionate child who prefers gesture and short phrases to longer sentences. Her two closest classmates there are Emily Johnson and Josué Ramírez; Lucía Castillo Reyes reported that Majo "juega bien con Josué Ramírez, pero se frustra cuando no la entienden los demás niños" — she plays well with Josué Ramírez but becomes frustrated when the other children cannot understand her. At home, Majo is close to the family dog, Luna, and reportedly narrates simple routines to Luna in Spanish, saying things like "Luna, siéntate" when asking the dog to sit — one of the few multi-word instructions she produces clearly. Ms. Patterson reported no concerns with Majo's play skills, attention, or peer interactions aside from the intelligibility difficulties already described.

During today's session, Majo separated easily from Lucía Castillo Reyes and engaged readily with Melissa Hwang and Carmen Ríos, who provided interpretation and cultural-linguistic consultation throughout testing to support accurate administration and scoring in both languages. Majo required occasional redirection to remain seated but was cooperative overall, completing all planned tasks across the two sessions on December 2, 2025 and December 9, 2025. Standardized testing was administered in English and Spanish, with informal language sampling conducted in both languages to capture a complete picture of Majo's combined linguistic system, consistent with best practice for bilingual language assessment.

Majo was administered the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions, along with selected subtests of the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals, Fifth Edition (CELF-5) for cross-validation, and an oral-motor and speech sound screening. On the PLS-5 English edition, Majo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 78 (7th percentile; 95% confidence interval 71-85), an Expressive Communication standard score of 70 (2nd percentile; 95% confidence interval 63-77), and a Total Language Score of 73 (4th percentile; 95% confidence interval 67-79). On the PLS-5 Spanish edition, administered by Carmen Ríos under the direct supervision of Melissa Hwang, Majo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 82 (12th percentile), an Expressive Communication standard score of 76 (5th percentile), and a Total Language Score of 78 (7th percentile). Combined, using a conceptual scoring approach that credits a concept produced in either language, Majo's Total Language Score rose to 85 (16th percentile), reflecting a broader linguistic system than either single-language score suggests.

Measure / Medida | English SS | Spanish SS | Combined (Conceptual)
Auditory Comprehension | 78 | 82 | 88
Expressive Communication | 70 | 76 | 82
Total Language Score | 73 | 78 | 85
Age Equivalent | 2;6–3;0 | 2;9–3;2 | 3;1–3;6

Speech sound production was assessed through single-word naming and a connected speech sample in both languages. In English, Majo's intelligibility was estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners in connected speech and 60% in single words; in Spanish, intelligibility was somewhat higher, estimated at 55% connected and 70% single words, consistent with Lucía Castillo Reyes's report at home. Majo demonstrated final consonant deletion, consistently producing "ga" for the target "gato" and "pa" for "pan". Cluster reduction was also noted, with Majo producing "fesco" for "fresco" and "paso" for "plato". In English, she substituted /w/ for /r/, saying "wabbit" for "rabbit", and fronted /k/ and /g/ to /t/ and /d/, respectively, producing "tat" for "cat". With moderate verbal cues, Majo was able to self-correct approximately 3 of 10 trials, improving to 6 of 10 with maximal cues and visual support. The oral-motor examination was within normal limits for structure and function, with adequate range of motion, strength, and diadochokinetic rate for her age; no concerns regarding feeding or swallowing were identified.

In the spontaneous language sample, Majo produced primarily one- and two-word combinations with occasional longer utterances, such as "mamá no aquí" and "Luna come pan." Her mean length of utterance was calculated at 1.8 morphemes in Spanish and 1.6 morphemes in English, both well below expectations for her age in either language. SALT coding of the sample flagged frequent omission of grammatical morphemes, coded [EW] for omitted word endings, particularly plural -s and the Spanish gender/number agreement markers; for example, Majo said "dos perro" rather than "dos perros", and "la pelota rojo" rather than "la pelota roja". She used almost no pronouns, relying instead on nouns and pointing, and she asked no questions during the sample apart from one instance of "qué eso?"

Lucía Castillo Reyes described the functional impact of Majo's communication difficulties at home and in the community: "Cuando vamos a la tienda, ella señala todo porque no sabe cómo pedirlo, y a veces los otros niños se ríen cuando trata de hablar en la escuela." Javier Fernández Soto added that he worries about her transition to kindergarten, saying, "Si no le entienden en el 'Los Patitos Felices', ¿qué va a pasar cuando empiece la escuela grande?" Both parents expressed strong motivation to support Majo's communication development at home and were receptive to coaching in strategies they could use during daily routines, including mealtimes with Diego Fernández Castillo and bath time, which Majo especially enjoys.

Impresiones / Impressions: Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Majo presents with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with her prior diagnosis (ICD-10 F80.2) and not attributable to her bilingual language exposure; her language skills are reduced relative to typically developing bilingual peers in both languages, which supports a primary language impairment rather than a difference associated with second-language acquisition. She also presents with a moderate speech sound disorder characterized by phonological process errors (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, fronting) that reduce intelligibility across both languages, now further complicated by a history of chronic otitis media and tube placement, though her current hearing status is documented as within normal limits. Majo's strengths include strong nonverbal communication, social motivation to interact with peers such as Josué Ramírez and Emily Johnson, and a supportive, engaged family system.

Recomendaciones / Recommendations: It is recommended that Majo continue to receive speech-language therapy through Piedmont CDSA at a minimum frequency of twice weekly, delivered bilingually or in close coordination between an English-speaking and a Spanish-speaking provider, with specific attention to expanding mean length of utterance, grammatical morpheme use in both languages, and vocabulary diversity. Continued use of Hanen-based parent coaching strategies is recommended, given the family's strong engagement, alongside structured PROMPT tactile-cueing approaches to target the specific phonological processes identified above; a structured Cycles approach to phonology may also be appropriate given the number of processes affecting intelligibility. It is recommended that Majo's IFSP be updated at the upcoming review on January 20, 2026 to reflect these findings, with a new outcome addressing speech sound intelligibility alongside the existing Outcome 2 for expressive language. Referral back to Dr. Patel for a repeat hearing evaluation is recommended given the history of recurrent otitis media, to rule out any fluctuating conductive component that could be contributing to her language and speech delays. Coordination with Los Patitos Felices staff, including Ms. Patterson and Srta. Alvarez, is recommended to support carryover of targeted vocabulary and phonological targets into the classroom setting. Finally, given the complexity of coordinating services across Lucía Castillo Reyes's night shift at Valle Verde Poultry and Javier Fernández Soto's schedule with Triad Construction Co., it is recommended that Brianna Lewis assist the family in identifying consistent caregiver availability, whether through Rosa Castillo Reyes, Marisol Castillo Reyes, or Yolanda Pérez, for therapy visits and the upcoming IFSP review.

This report was prepared by Melissa Hwang, M.S., CCC-SLP, with interpretation and cultural-linguistic consultation provided by Carmen Ríos. Questions may be directed to intake@carolinapedsslp.com or (704) 555-0168. Report distributed to the family, Dr. Amanda Singh, and Brianna Lewis at Piedmont CDSA on December 15, 2025.

CDSA Case ID: NC-CDSA-48217
Medicaid ID: 7734829105F
Referring Provider: Dr. Patel, Pediatrics

Dear Lucía and Thomas Flores,

Thank you for bringing Mateo in for his speech and language evaluation. It was a pleasure to meet your family and to see how hard Mateo works to communicate every day. This letter explains what we did during the visit, what we found, and what we recommend next. We wrote it in plain language on purpose, so please call us with any questions at all.

**Reason for Referral**

Mateo was referred by Dr. Patel at his 26 month well-child visit because his vocabulary and sentence length seemed behind what is typical for his age. His service coordinator at the CDSA office in Wake County, Monica Reyes, also raised concerns after a home visit, noting that Mateo mostly pointed and used single words rather than short sentences. Lucía and Thomas agreed that a full speech and language evaluation would help the family and the CDSA team plan next steps together.

**Birth and Medical History**

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestational age following an uncomplicated pregnancy. His birth weight was 6 pounds 11 ounces, and his Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes. He stayed with his mother in the regular newborn nursery at WakeMed Cary Hospital and was discharged on day two. Lucía reported no complications during the pregnancy or delivery, and no NICU stay was needed.

Mateo's medical history is largely unremarkable. He has had three ear infections, the most recent treated in May 2026 with amoxicillin, and he passed a hearing screening at his pediatrician's office on June 3, 2026 in both ears. He has no history of seizures, head injury, or hospitalization beyond his birth. His vision was screened as normal at his two-year checkup. Lucía noted that he snores loudly most nights and sometimes breathes through his mouth, which we will mention in our recommendations below.

Mateo's motor milestones were all within typical ranges: he sat independently at 6 months, walked at 13 months, and currently runs, climbs stairs with one hand held, and feeds himself with a spoon. His fine motor skills, including stacking blocks and turning pages, are age-appropriate.

**Family and Language History**

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía and Thomas Flores, his older sister Rosa, age five, and his younger brother Will, age one, in Garner, North Carolina. Lucía works part-time at Triangle Linen Services and speaks primarily Spanish with the children at home, while Thomas works full days as an electrician and speaks primarily English. Lucía estimated that Mateo hears Spanish and English in roughly equal amounts across a typical week, making him a simultaneous bilingual learner rather than a sequential one.

The children's grandmother, doña Lupe, watches Mateo and his siblings two afternoons a week while Lucía is at work. doña Lupe speaks only Spanish with the children and reported that Mateo understands her simple directions in Spanish, such as "dame la pelota," but rarely answers her in words. Lucía also mentioned that her cousin Paz sometimes helps with pickup from daycare and has noticed the same pattern: Mateo gestures and points far more than he talks.

Mateo attends Sunshine Beginnings Daycare four days a week as part of the center's Early Head Start classroom for toddlers. His teacher there, Miss Ana, reports that he plays alongside peers but prefers parallel play to interactive play, and that he gets frustrated when classmates like his friend Diego do not understand his gestures. Thomas is sometimes known there simply as Mr. Tom, since he is the parent who most often does drop-off.

The family also attends a Saturday Spanish story-time group through Smart Start of Wake County, run by la maestra Carmen, where Mateo listens to short books and songs. The family received WIC nutrition support through WIC when Mateo was an infant and currently works with Monica Reyes at the CDSA office as their service coordinator for early intervention. Lucía mentioned that the family also briefly worked with a caseworker through DSS two years ago for a housing referral, unrelated to Mateo's current services.

**Assessment Procedures**

The evaluation took place over 9:30 a.m. to 11:15 a.m. at our office in Cary. Because Lucía prefers to discuss detailed clinical information in Spanish, our bilingual interpreter, Elena Soto, assisted with parts of the interview and the Spanish-language testing. I conducted direct testing in both English and Spanish, following standard bilingual assessment guidelines, and gathered a language sample during structured play.

The following measures were administered:

- Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), English and Spanish editions
- MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories (CDI), Spanish-English bilingual short form, completed by Lucía and Thomas
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical observation and language sample analysis during structured and unstructured play
- Oral mechanism examination
- Parent interview and case history review

Mateo separated easily from his parents and engaged well with toys, though he required frequent redirection to stay on task. He used mod cues to attend to two-step directions and needed visual supports paired with verbal instructions for best performance.

**Test Results**

| Measure | Subtest | Standard Score | Percentile | Confidence Interval | Age Equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 (English) | Auditory Comprehension | 78 | 7th | 73-83 | 1;10-2;1 |
| PLS-5 (English) | Expressive Communication | 70 | 2nd | 65-75 | 1;6-1;9 |
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th | 76-88 | 2;0-2;3 |
| PLS-5 (Spanish) | Expressive Communication | 74 | 4th | 68-80 | 1;8-1;11 |
| GFTA-3 | Sounds-in-Words | 85 | 16th | 79-91 | 2;6–3;0 |

On the MacArthur-Bates CDI, Lucía and Thomas together reported a combined expressive vocabulary of approximately 55 words across both languages, which falls below the 10th percentile for his age in either language alone but closer to the 25th percentile when total conceptual vocabulary across both languages is considered, consistent with current bilingual assessment guidance.

**Speech Sound Production**

Mateo's oral mechanism exam was within normal limits for structure and function, with adequate strength, range of motion, and symmetry for speech. His intelligibility was judged to be approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners within context.

During the language sample, Mateo produced several consistent phonological patterns. He substituted /t/ for /k/ in word-initial position, as in "tat" for cat, and simplified consonant clusters, producing "poon" for spoon. He demonstrated final consonant deletion in words like "ca" for cat when in final position of a sentence, and he backed /t/ to [k] inconsistently in connected speech.

Several of his quoted productions during play were especially informative. When his sister joined the room, he looked up and said "Osa no," his approximation of his sister Rosa's name paired with a protest, likely meaning he did not want her to take his toy. Later, while playing with a stuffed animal, he pointed to the family dog resting nearby and said "Bibo go," clearly referencing the family's dog Bingo, whose name he consistently shortens. When his baby brother fussed in the next room, Mateo turned toward the sound and said "Wi no no," an apparent reference to his brother Will, suggesting some awareness of his brother's distress and an attempt to comment on it. These spontaneous productions show that Mateo is attempting multi-word combinations and is motivated to communicate about people and routines that matter to him, even though his sound system is not yet supporting many adult-like forms.

He showed stimulability for /k/ in isolation with max cues, producing an accurate [k] on 6 of 10 trials, which is a favorable prognostic sign.

**Impressions**

Taken together, Mateo's results indicate a mixed receptive-expressive language delay, with expressive language more significantly affected than receptive language, in the context of typical bilingual development. His low scores on English-only and Spanish-only measures, combined with his stronger performance when both languages are considered together, support ruling out typical bilingual variation as the sole explanation for his delay. His speech sound patterns are also beyond what would be expected purely from bilingual phonological development at his age.

Diagnostic impression: Mixed expressive-receptive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) with an associated phonological disorder (ICD-10 F80.0), affecting both English and Spanish. Mateo continues to qualify for early intervention services through the CDSA system under North Carolina's eligibility criteria for communication delay.

Given Lucía's report of loud snoring and mouth breathing, we also recommend a referral to an ear, nose, and throat specialist to rule out enlarged tonsils or adenoids as a contributing factor, and we have shared this concern with Dr. Patel's office directly.

**Recommendations**

1. Mateo should begin individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, with sessions delivered bilingually or alternating between English and Spanish, targeting both expressive vocabulary growth and early phonological patterns.
2. We recommend a Hanen-based coaching approach for the family, so that Lucía, Thomas, and doña Lupe can all support Mateo's communication consistently across settings and languages.
3. A trial of core vocabulary picture supports, similar to PECS strategies, may help Mateo bridge from gestures to words during moments of frustration, particularly at daycare with Miss Ana.
4. We recommend continued close communication between our office, the family's service coordinator Monica Reyes at the CDSA office, and Mateo's classroom team at Sunshine Beginnings Daycare, so that goals are reinforced across all settings.
5. An updated IFSP should be scheduled to add Outcome 3 (expressive communication) and revise Outcome 1 (receptive language) to reflect these results; we have requested a joint planning meeting with Monica Reyes within the next month.
6. We recommend a referral to an ENT specialist to evaluate snoring and mouth breathing, as chronic nasal obstruction can affect both resonance and overall communication development.
7. Follow-up reassessment is recommended in six months, or sooner if Mateo's rate of progress raises new questions, to track growth in both languages separately and combined.

Billing note for insurance purposes: today's evaluation was billed under CPT 92523 (speech sound and language evaluation) with modifier GN, as authorized under the family's current CDSA service plan.

**Summary for the Family**

Mateo is a bright, curious little boy who clearly wants to connect with the people around him, including his big sister Rosa, his baby brother Will, and his dog Bingo. Right now his words are not catching up to everything he wants to say, in either English or Spanish, and his speech sounds are harder to understand than we would expect for his age. The good news is that he is already combining words, he responded well to cues during testing, and his family and care team are already working together closely. With consistent therapy and support at home, at daycare, and through the CDSA program, we expect Mateo to continue making steady progress.

Please do not hesitate to call our office at (919) 555-0148 or email us at intake@carolinapedspeech.com with any questions about this report. We are also happy to join Mateo's next IFSP meeting if that would be helpful for the team.

Sincerely,

Dr. Sarah Whitfield, CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Speech Partners
License No. NC-SLP-22894

Estimada familia Lucía Rodríguez y Carlos Fernández:

Espero que se encuentren bien. Les escribo para contarles cómo le fue a Mateo en nuestra sesión de terapia del habla y lenguaje el 6 de octubre de 2026 a las 3:30 p.m. en las oficinas del Centro de Desarrollo y Servicios para Niños del Condado de Durham (CDSA de Durham).

También me recordó que la próxima sesión de Mateo será el 20 de octubre de 2026 a las 10:00 a.m., en su casa, en Calle Roble 245, Durham. Como siempre, contamos con la ayuda de la intérprete Marta Jiménez, quien tradujo mis comentarios durante la llamada con la maestra.

López antes de la sesión, y me contó que Mateo jugó bien hoy con su compañero Santiago durante el círculo de la mañana. Durante la sesión de hoy, trabajamos en el sonido /k/ en palabras como "casa" y "copa". Mateo logró producir el sonido con claves mínimas en 8 de 10 intentos.
