O:
Session #: biweekly, home-based, 9:15 a.m.–9:55 a.m. today. CPT 92507 (tx), re-eval portion billed 92523.

Standardized measures re-administered this visit:
PLS-5 Spanish-English bilingual form: Auditory Comprehension SS 76 (5th percentile), Expressive Communication SS 71 (3rd percentile), Total Language SS 72 (CI 68-77).
Age equivalent: receptive 20 months, expressive 16 months.

Structured probe, 2-word combinations (home/school vocab, EN+ES mixed): 8/10 correct w/ mod cues (gestural + verbal model), 80% accuracy — up from 3/10 at initial IFSP.

Language sample (10 min, free play w/ toy animals): Mateo produced "más perro" and "agua por favor" spontaneously; imitated "quiero jugo" w/ min cues. When toy dog knocked over blocks, said "Rocky no" (referencing family dog at home, not toy) — spontaneous 2-word utterance, noted but not target-modeled.

Articulation screen: stimulable for /s/ in isolation, min cues; /k/ frontal distortion persists, target "cookie" produced as [tuki].

Observed at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center on September 29, 2026, 10:00 a.m.–10:30 a.m.: Mateo in mixed-age toddler room w/ classmate Liam; teacher Ms. Donna Pruitt reports he points/vocalizes but rarely combines words in classroom setting; peer interaction brief, mostly parallel play.

A:
Mateo continues to present w/ delayed receptive and expressive language consistent w/ ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder), with persisting phonological pattern affecting intelligibility. Progress noted toward Outcome 1 (8/10, 80%, up from baseline 3/10) supports continued eligibility and current service intensity. Spontaneous 2-word combo in natural play ("Rocky no") suggests emerging generalization beyond structured probes. Tantrum behavior (Priority 2) likely communication-based; recommend functional communication strategies embedded in sibling play routines. Family's bilingual home language supports continued dual-language intervention per CDSA bilingual EI guidelines; no evidence language delay is primarily attributable to bilingual exposure.

P:
Outcome 1 (continued): Mateo will use 2-word combinations to request and comment across ≥3 settings (home, Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, community) w/ 80% accuracy, min-mod cues, by next review.

Outcome 2 (new): Mateo will use 1 communicative word/gesture in lieu of tantrum behavior during shared play w/ Camila, observed 4/5 opportunities, within 3 months.
Strategy: teach abuela Rosa Morales and Camila simple sign/word prompts; coach during weekday afternoon play block (post-nap, 2:15 p.m.–3:00 p.m.).

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
IFSP Periodic Review Summary

CDSA: Central Piedmont CDSA, Alamance County office, 1105 S. Mebane St, Graham, NC 27253
CDSA phone: (336) 555-0199

Date of Birth: August 3, 2024

Case #: AL-2024-0317
Medicaid #: 9876543210A

Parents: Lucia Hernandez Ramirez (mother) and Carlos Flores Martinez (father)
Home address: 214 Persimmon Lane, Burlington, NC 27215
Home phone: (336) 555-0148

Service Coordinator: Jennifer Boyd
Speech-Language Pathologist: Ana Sofia Delgado, M.S., CCC-SLP, Piedmont Speech Kids, PLLC
Email: ana.delgado@piedmontspeechkids.com
Website: www.piedmontspeechkids.com

Date of IFSP review meeting: October 2, 2026
Prior IFSP date: April 9, 2026

I. Resumen / Summary

This is the periodic IFSP review for Mateo, a 26-month-old boy referred by his pediatrician, Dr. Michael Chen, for evaluation of expressive language delay and suspected Childhood Apraxia of Speech. Mateo carries a diagnosis of F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). Services were billed under 92507 (individual treatment) and 92523 (speech and language evaluation).

II. Family Concerns and Priorities (en las palabras de la familia)

During the meeting, Lucia shared, "Lo que mas me preocupa es que Teo no me dice lo que quiere, solo senala y llora." She added that her mother, Rosa Ramirez, who watches Mateo on weekday mornings before daycare, has noticed the same thing: "Mi mama dice que el entiende todo pero no habla casi nada, solo gruñe." At bedtime, Lucia said, "Yo le leo en espanol y el senala las imagenes pero no repite las palabras conmigo."

Carlos said in English, mixing in Spanish, "He gets frustrated real quick, se enoja y tira las cosas, and then he just goes quiet." Both parents want Mateo to be able to tell Lucia and his older sister, Valentina Flores, what he needs "sin tanto drama," and they want him ready for pre-k by 36 months. Carlos also asked whether being raised bilingual was "confundiendolo mas," and the team reassured the family that dual-language exposure does not cause or worsen the delay.

III. Daily Routines (Rutinas Diarias)

Mateo wakes around 6:30 a.m. and eats breakfast with Valentina before Rosa arrives to watch him. Lucia works nights at Pilgrim's Pride in Mebane and sleeps most mornings, so Rosa takes Mateo to Tadpole House Early Learning around 8:45 a.m.. Carlos works for Superior Construction LLC and picks Mateo up most days around 5:00 p.m.. At home, Mateo likes bath time and will request "mas agua" by pointing and vocalizing but rarely uses words. At dinner, the family reported he signs "mas" for more food but says few words. On weekends, the family often visits Mateo's tia, Esperanza Ramirez, for a Sunday asado, and Mateo plays with his cousins and the family dog, Canela, though he does not yet call the dog by name.

IV. Other Agencies Involved

The family receives WIC benefits through Alamance County WIC and has an open case with Alamance County DSS for a housing subsidy. Mateo is not currently enrolled in Alamance Community Action Early Head Start, though Lucia has applied; the waitlist was confirmed by Alamance Partnership for Children (Smart Start), which also referred the family to a parenting class offered in Spanish.

V. Present Levels of Development

Receptive language: On the PLS-5, Mateo earned an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 79 (8th percentile), age equivalent 18-20 months. Expressive Communication standard score was 65 (1st percentile), age equivalent 11-13 months. Confidence interval for the Total Language score was 68-78. On a Spanish-language supplemental screening, comprehension of single-step directions in Spanish was comparable to English, around 70% accuracy for both languages combined.

Speech sound production: Mateo produces primarily vowels and a few consonants (/m/, /b/, /d/). He attempted the target word "pelota" and produced [be]. For the word "agua" he produced [aba]. Inconsistency across repeated attempts of the same word is consistent with Childhood Apraxia of Speech features, though he is young for a definitive diagnosis.

Oral motor and feeding: within normal limits per parent report; no concerns raised by Dr. Chen.

At daycare, his teacher, Keisha Owens, reports Mateo imitates one-word models from peers, including his friend Isaiah, about 3 of 10 trials, and will hand toys to another classmate, Camila, when asked.

VI. Progress on Prior Outcomes

Outcome 1 (requesting with a word or approximation): Mateo met criterion with 8/10 trials using a word approximation ("ma" for "mas") across two sessions, up from 2/10 at the last review. This represents 80% accuracy, meeting the exit criterion for this outcome.

Outcome 2 (imitate CV and CVCV words with moderate cues): Mateo imitates with mod cues at 60% accuracy; outcome continues.

VII. New and Continuing Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1 (continuing): Mateo will use 2-3 word combinations to request and comment across home and daycare settings, 4 of 5 opportunities across three consecutive sessions.
Strategies: Caregiver coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies, emphasizing expansion of Mateo's utterances; Rosa and Lucia will practice narrating routines in Spanish and English; Keisha will model two-word phrases during snack and play at Tadpole House Early Learning.

Outcome 2: Mateo will produce target early-developing consonants (/m/, /b/, /p/, /d/) in CV and CVCV words with min cues at 80% accuracy across two consecutive sessions.
Strategies: PROMPT-informed tactile cueing during 1:1 sessions; home practice sheet with Spanish and English target words (mas, papa, bebe, dedo); visual supports paired with core vocabulary.

Outcome 3 (new): Family will connect with Alamance Community Action Early Head Start to secure a classroom placement within 90 days, supported by service coordinator Jennifer Boyd.

VIII. Service Delivery

Speech-language therapy: individual sessions, 92507, twice weekly, 30 minutes, in home and at Tadpole House Early Learning, provided in English and Spanish by Ana Sofia Delgado.
Developmental evaluation update billed under 92523 on September 18, 2026.
Service coordination: monthly, by Jennifer Boyd, Central Piedmont CDSA.

Lucia closed the meeting by saying, "Gracias por explicarme todo en espanol, se me hace mas facil entender asi," and asked that future written reports include a Spanish summary when possible.

Next periodic review scheduled for April 2, 2027. Annual IFSP due October 2, 2027.

Subject: Speech-Language Evaluation Report – Mateo Hernández Cruz / Evaluación de Lenguaje

Buenas tardes, Marisol, and hello Lucía and Carlos,

Attached below please find the full written report for Mateo's (Mateo Hernández Cruz's) speech-language evaluation completed on March 3, 2026 at the Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Área del Triángulo ("CDSA del Triángulo") clinic office. Como siempre, I've written it bilingually in parts so the whole family can read it comfortably. Please let me know if you'd like me to walk through it by phone before the IFSP meeting.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Child / Niño: Mateo Hernández Cruz ("Teo")
Date of Birth / Fecha de Nacimiento: June 14, 2022
Chronological Age / Edad Cronológica: 3;8
Evaluation Date / Fecha de Evaluación: March 3, 2026
CDSA Record #: CDSA-2026-04471
Medicaid ID: 920447185A
Referral Source: Marisol Ibáñez, Service Coordinator, Coordinación de Servicios para Familias del Piedmont ("Piedmont SC")
CDSA Office: Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Área del Triángulo (CDSA del Triángulo)
School District / Program: Durham Public Schools Pre-K Partnership classroom, housed at E.K. Powe Elementary School, Sala Azul room, lead teacher Ms. Alicia Fernández
Current Program: Durham Early Head Start (toddler classroom)
Home Address: 412 Hartness Avenue, Durham, North Carolina 27705
Parents/Guardians: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Carlos Hernández (father)
Siblings: Valentina Hernández (age 7), Noah Hernández (age 1)
Phone: (919) 555-0148
Email: lucia.rodriguez82@gmail.com

REASON FOR REFERRAL / MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Marisol Ibáñez following concerns raised by his mother, Lucía, and staff at Durham Early Head Start regarding limited expressive vocabulary, reduced intelligibility with unfamiliar listeners, and questions about his emerging bilingual development in Spanish and English. Lucía reported, "casi no le entiendo cuando quiere algo, y se frustra mucho." Carlos echoed similar concerns, noting that Mateo often resorts to pointing and pulling adults toward what he wants rather than using words.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO MÉDICO

According to Lucía, Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestation at Duke Regional Hospital in Durham following preterm labor. Birth weight was 2,310 grams (5 lbs, 1 oz), and Apgar scores were 6 at one minute and 8 at five minutes. Mateo was admitted to the Duke Regional Hospital Neonatal Intensive Care Unit for 19 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulties, including an NG tube for oral-motor and swallowing concerns. His attending neonatologist was Dr. Priya Anand, and feeding therapy in the NICU was provided by Hannah Doyle, OTR/L. Since discharge, Mateo's pediatrician has been Dr. Steven Okafor at Durham Pediatric Associates.

Lucía reports a history of recurrent otitis media beginning around 8 months of age, with bilateral myringotomy and tympanostomy tube placement at 18 months by Dr. Rebecca Sloane, ENT. Tubes remained in place without complication, and Mateo's most recent hearing screening, per audiology records on file at Durham Pediatric Associates, showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. A developmental pediatrician, Dr. Nadia Farrukh, diagnosed Mateo with Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.1) at 30 months of age and recommended referral to the CDSA del Triángulo for further evaluation and Part C services.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez and Carlos Hernández; his older sister, Valentina; his younger brother, Noah; and his maternal grandmother, Rosa Cruz, who moved in with the family shortly after Mateo's birth. Rosa speaks only Spanish and provides daytime childcare for Mateo and Noah while Lucía sleeps after her overnight shift. Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home among all family members; English exposure comes mainly through Valentina's homework, television programming, and Mateo's part-time attendance at Durham Early Head Start, estimated by this examiner at roughly 20% of his total daily language input.

Lucía works nights at the Harris Teeter Distribution Center as an overnight stocker, and Carlos works days as a forklift operator at Triangle Brick Company. Because of this schedule, Rosa Cruz serves as Mateo's primary daytime caregiver, and the family has relied heavily on community supports. The family has previously received assistance from the Durham County WIC Program (WIC) for nutritional support during Mateo's infancy, and Lucía credits a home visitor from Durham's Partnership for Children (Smart Start) with first encouraging her to contact the Durham County Department of Social Services (DSS) about developmental concerns when Mateo was a toddler. The family's DSS caseworker, Teresa Blackwood, continues to coordinate benefits alongside Marisol Ibáñez's IFSP work through the CDSA del Triángulo.

Lucía describes Mateo as an affectionate, social child who prefers playing with his older sister and the family's dog, Luna, over independent play. At Durham Early Head Start, his teachers note that he gravitates toward a classmate, Ximena Ortiz, who has become something of a peer model during group activities. Lucía shared a recent example: "Teo estaba jugando con Luna y le dijo 'ven' bien clarito, pero cuando quiso decir el nombre de su hermana le salió 'Baya'" instead of "Valentina."

ASSESSMENT TOOLS ADMINISTERED / INSTRUMENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English Bilingual Edition
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool, Second Edition (CELF-P2)
- Spontaneous bilingual language sample
- Parent interview and clinical observation across two sessions

Testing was conducted bilingually by this examiner, who is fluent in both languages; no outside interpreter was required.

TEST RESULTS / RESULTADOS

PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 82 (73-91 95% CI), 12th percentile, age equivalent 2;6–3;0
PLS-5 Expressive Communication: Standard Score 74 (66-82 95% CI), 4th percentile, age equivalent 2;0–2;6
PLS-5 Total Language Score: Standard Score 76, 5th percentile
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words: Standard Score 78, 7th percentile
CELF-P2 Core Language Score: Standard Score 80, 9th percentile

Articulation testing revealed that Mateo produced /k/ as [t] in word-initial position, saying "tasa" for "casa," and substituted /ɾ/ with [l], saying "lamo" for "ramo." He correctly produced /m/, /p/, and /b/ in 8/10 trials with minimal cues, and produced final consonant deletion on roughly 3 of 5 multisyllabic targets. During the spontaneous sample, Mateo used primarily 2-word to 3-word combinations in Spanish and single words in English, with an overall MLU of 2.4 morphemes.

CLINICAL OBSERVATIONS / OBSERVACIONES CLÍNICAS

Mateo engaged readily with this examiner, using eye contact and gesture to supplement his limited verbal output. He spontaneously said "más" to request a repeated turn with a cause-and-effect toy, and protested with "no quiero" when asked to transition activities. With moderate cues (mod cues), he successfully imitated two-word combinations such as "mamá ven" and "más agua." With maximal cues, he attempted three-word imitations but reduced them to the final two words. This pattern of response to cueing, along with his family and language history, continues to relate to IFSP Outcome 2: expanding expressive vocabulary and intelligibility across both languages.

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES

Based on standardized testing, parent report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) with a co-occurring Phonological Disorder (ICD-10 F80.0), evident across both Spanish and English. Because his difficulties are consistent in both languages rather than isolated to the language with less input, this pattern is not consistent with typical bilingual second-language acquisition alone, though his approximately 20% English exposure should be weighed when interpreting the English-only portions of today's testing. His history of prematurity, NICU course, and recurrent otitis media are all relevant contributing factors.

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES

1. Direct speech-language therapy twice weekly (CPT 92523 for today's evaluation; CPT 92507 for ongoing individual treatment sessions), delivered bilingually.
2. Caregiver coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies with Lucía, Carlos, and Rosa Cruz, given Rosa's role as primary daytime caregiver.
3. PROMPT-informed tactile-kinesthetic cueing to target /k/ and /ɾ/ production.
4. Continued coordination with classroom staff at Durham Early Head Start and planning for transition to Ms. Fernández's Pre-K classroom at E.K. Powe Elementary School in the fall.
5. Repeat audiological evaluation given history of tympanostomy tubes and recurrent otitis media.
6. Addition of IFSP Goal 3, targeting bilingual expressive vocabulary growth of at least 20 new words in each language over the next IFSP period.
7. Continued family support coordination through Marisol Ibáñez and the CDSA del Triángulo regarding WIC, DSS, and Early Head Start services.

Respectfully submitted / Atentamente,

Diana Whitfield, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

Número de identificación de niño en el NC ITP: ITP-2026-00841
Número de autorización/registro: AUTH-PD-66230

Mateo es un niño de cuatro años que reside en la ciudad de Siler City, en el condado de Chatham, Carolina del Norte, con su madre, Lucía Rodríguez-Paz, su padre, Javier de la Cruz, y su hermana mayor, Camila de la Cruz, de seis años. La familia también cuenta con el apoyo frecuente de la abuela materna, Rosa Martínez, quien cuida a Mateo varias tardes por semana mientras sus padres trabajan. La familia vive en un apartamento en la Calle Elm 214, Siler City, NC 27344. El teléfono de contacto de la familia es (919) 555-0187 y el correo electrónico de la madre es lucia.rodriguezpaz@example.com.

Mateo fue remitido para esta evaluación por su médico de cabecera, Dr. Patel, debido a preocupaciones sobre el desarrollo del habla expresiva y la inteligibilidad del lenguaje. La familia fue contactada inicialmente a través de la ARSDIP, que coordina los servicios de intervención temprana en la región. La evaluación se llevó a cabo en las oficinas de Terapias Pediátricas Carolina Central, PLLC, donde la evaluadora, Ana Gómez, presta servicios bajo contrato con la ARSDIP.

Historia del nacimiento y la salud: Según el reporte materno, Mateo nació a las 38 semanas de gestación mediante parto vaginal sin complicaciones significativas, con un peso al nacer de 3,100 gramos y una puntuación de Apgar de 8 y 9 al minuto uno y cinco respectivamente. La madre reporta un embarazo sin incidentes mayores, aunque menciona haber tenido presión arterial elevada en el tercer trimestre, controlada sin medicación. Mateo fue dado de alta del hospital Hospital Regional Chatham a los dos días de vida sin complicaciones. No se reportan hospitalizaciones posteriores, cirugías, ni convulsiones. La madre indica que Mateo tuvo varios episodios de otitis media entre los 18 y 30 meses de edad, tratados con antibióticos, y que actualmente no presenta problemas auditivos conocidos. Una prueba de audición realizada en diciembre fue reportada como normal bilateral.

Historia familiar y del lenguaje: En el hogar se habla principalmente español; el padre, Javier, usa inglés de manera más frecuente en el trabajo y ocasionalmente en casa con los niños. La madre, Lucía, trabaja de noche en la Planta de Empaque Avícola Piedmont como supervisora de línea de producción, por lo que la abuela, Rosa, y el padre comparten la mayor parte del cuidado directo de los niños durante las tardes y noches. El padre trabaja como técnico de mantenimiento en una empresa local de manufactura. La familia reporta que Camila habla con fluidez tanto español como inglés y a menudo traduce para Mateo cuando juega con compañeros de habla inglesa. No hay historia familiar reportada de trastornos del habla, lenguaje, audición ni aprendizaje en parientes cercanos, aunque la madre menciona que un tío paterno, Ernesto de la Cruz, tuvo dificultades de lectura en la escuela primaria.

Mateo asiste de lunes a viernes al centro Pequeños Pasos Daycare, donde su maestra principal es la Sra. Gabriela Hernández. Según el reporte de la maestra, Mateo interactúa con sus compañeros de clase, incluyendo a Noah y Valentina Ríos, aunque a veces se frustra cuando no logra hacerse entender y recurre a señalar o a gestos. La familia también reporta que Mateo tiene un perro llamado Max, con quien juega con frecuencia en el patio trasero, y que suele decir "quero jugar" cuando quiere que alguien lo acompañe afuera.

Según el reporte de los padres, las primeras palabras de Mateo aparecieron alrededor de los 16 meses, y comenzó a combinar dos palabras cerca de los 26 meses. Los padres describen su habla actual como difícil de entender para personas fuera del núcleo familiar, especialmente en frases largas. En el hogar, Mateo es descrito como un niño sociable, curioso y motivado para comunicarse, aunque se frustra cuando no es comprendido.

Mateo fue inscrito en el programa de intervención temprana del estado bajo un Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) con fecha de reunión inicial del 2 de octubre de 2025. El objetivo 2 del IFSP actual se centra en el aumento de la inteligibilidad del habla en contextos funcionales. Mateo ha recibido terapia de lenguaje una vez por semana a través de la ARSDIP desde esa fecha, con la terapeuta Marisol Vega, quien ha utilizado principalmente el enfoque Hanen con la familia.

A continuación se presenta el horario actual de las sesiones de terapia domiciliaria y en el centro:

Día | Hora de inicio | Hora de fin | Lugar
Lunes | 9:30 a.m. | 10:15 a.m. | Hogar de la familia, Calle Elm 214
Miércoles | 1:00 p.m. | 1:45 p.m. | Pequeños Pasos Daycare
Viernes | 10:00 a.m. | 10:45 a.m. | Oficina de Terapias Pediátricas Carolina Central, PLLC

Durante la sesión de evaluación, Mateo se mostró cooperativo y participativo durante la mayor parte de la cita, aunque solicitó un descanso breve después de aproximadamente 20 minutos de tareas estructuradas. La evaluación incluyó observación informal del juego, muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, y administración de pruebas estandarizadas en español e inglés, dado el perfil bilingüe de la familia.

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas: Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish, Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), y el subtest de Articulación del Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3). También se obtuvo una muestra de lenguaje espontáneo codificada parcialmente en SALT, incluyendo producciones como "[EW]" marcadas en segmentos ininteligibles.

Resultados de las pruebas:

Prueba | Puntuación estándar | Percentil | Intervalo de confianza
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12 | 76-88
PLS-5 Expressive Communication | 71 | 3 | 65-77
CELF Preschool-3 Core Language Score | 75 | 5 | 69-81
GFTA-3 Standard Score | 68 | 2 | 62-74

En la prueba de articulación, Mateo presentó errores consistentes de simplificación de grupos consonánticos, sustitución de /k/ por [t], y omisión de consonantes finales, tanto en español como en inglés. Por ejemplo, produjo "tasa" para la palabra objetivo "casa" y "apo" para "carro". Durante la muestra espontánea, cuando se le preguntó por su perro, dijo "Max core" en lugar de "Max corre", demostrando el mismo patrón de sustitución en contexto conectado. Con claves de mod cues, logró producir correctamente el sonido /k/ en aislamiento en 7 de 10 intentos, pero no generalizó de manera consistente a nivel de palabra o frase.

En el área de lenguaje receptivo, Mateo mostró un desempeño dentro del rango bajo-promedio, siguiendo instrucciones de dos pasos con apoyo visual en 8/10 ensayos. En el área expresiva, su longitud media de enunciado fue notablemente menor a lo esperado para su edad, y presentó dificultades marcadas con el uso de marcadores morfológicos en ambos idiomas, incluyendo la omisión de artículos y la conjugación verbal inconsistente. La inteligibilidad global fue estimada en aproximadamente 40% para oyentes desconocidos y 70% para oyentes familiares, según el conteo de palabras inteligibles en la muestra de habla conectada.

Durante la observación informal del juego, Mateo demostró habilidades de juego simbólico apropiadas para su edad, incluyendo secuencias de juego de fingir con figuras de acción, y buscó activamente la atención compartida con la evaluadora. No se observaron conductas repetitivas atípicas ni dificultades significativas de atención conjunta. Las habilidades pragmáticas, incluyendo turnos conversacionales y reparación de comunicación, se consideraron relativamente fuertes en comparación con sus habilidades fonológicas y morfosintácticas.

Impresiones: Con base en los resultados de las pruebas estandarizadas, la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, y el reporte de los padres y de la maestra, Mateo presenta un perfil consistente con un trastorno del lenguaje expresivo de moderado a severo, acompañado de un trastorno de sonidos del habla, ambos presentes de manera comparable en español e inglés, lo cual indica un patrón de dificultad en ambos idiomas en lugar de una diferencia típica de desarrollo bilingüe. El código diagnóstico aplicable es F80.1 para trastorno del lenguaje expresivo y F80.0 para trastorno fonológico, según criterios del DSM-5-TR e ICD-10-CM. Las fortalezas relativas en pragmática y juego simbólico son factores positivos para el pronóstico de intervención continuada.

Dado el nivel de inteligibilidad reducida observado, especialmente con oyentes no familiares, y el impacto funcional en la participación de Mateo en el entorno de la guardería, se recomienda un aumento en la frecuencia de los servicios de terapia del habla y lenguaje a dos sesiones por semana, idealmente combinando sesiones en el hogar y en Pequeños Pasos Daycare. Se recomienda continuar usando estrategias del enfoque Hanen con la familia, junto con la incorporación de técnicas de PROMPT para abordar los patrones de simplificación fonológica observados. También se sugiere considerar el enfoque de Cycles para el tratamiento fonológico dada la cantidad de procesos simplificadores presentes.

Se recomienda que la coordinadora de servicios, Diana Castillo, actualice el IFSP para reflejar la frecuencia incrementada de servicios y para añadir un nuevo objetivo relacionado específicamente con la inteligibilidad en el entorno escolar. Se sugiere coordinación continua entre la terapeuta actual, Marisol Vega, la maestra Gabriela Hernández, y la familia para asegurar la generalización de estrategias en múltiples contextos. Se recomienda también una reevaluación de audición de seguimiento dentro de los próximos seis meses dado el historial de otitis media recurrente, y se sugiere que el pediatra, Dr. Patel, sea informado de los resultados de esta evaluación para descartar cualquier contribución auditiva residual.

Finalmente, se recomienda que la familia continúe recibiendo materiales educativos bilingües sobre estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en el hogar, y que se explore la posibilidad de servicios de respiro o apoyo adicional para la abuela, Rosa Martínez, dado el rol central que desempeña en el cuidado diario de Mateo mientras los padres trabajan. Se recomienda una próxima revisión de progreso dentro de tres meses, con fecha tentativa fijada para el 15 de junio de 2026, para evaluar el avance hacia los objetivos actuales del IFSP y determinar si se requieren ajustes adicionales en la frecuencia o el enfoque de los servicios.

Este informe fue preparado por Ana Gómez, patóloga del habla y lenguaje, bajo contrato con la ARSDIP, y refleja el desempeño de Mateo únicamente durante la sesión de evaluación descrita. Cualquier pregunta sobre este informe puede dirigirse a Ana Gómez a través de agomez@carolinacentralpeds.example.com o al teléfono (919) 555-0243.

Estimados Carlos Torres Medina y Lucía Fernández Ramírez:

Espero que se encuentren bien. Les escribo para contarles cómo le fue a María José Fernández Torres en su sesión de terapia del habla y lenguaje el día 9 de octubre de 2026, a las 3:30 p.m., en el Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos.

Trabajamos durante treinta minutos en el salón de la maestra Sra. Pardo, quien nos prestó un rincón tranquilo mientras sus compañeros de clase, Valentina y Santiago, jugaban en el patio. MJ llegó muy contenta hablando de su perrito Max y de su primo Emiliano, quien la visitó el fin de semana pasado y jugó con ella y con Max en el jardín.

Usamos la prueba PLS-5 para revisar su progreso en el área de Comprensión Auditiva. María José obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 82, en el percentil 12, dentro de un intervalo de confianza de 73-91. Esto corresponde a una edad equivalente de 2;9–3;1, comparado con su edad cronológica de 4;2. Seguimos notando dificultad con el sonido /ɾ/; hoy produjo la palabra meta "carro" con claves mínimas, logrando 7 de 10 intentos correctos. También trabajamos el sonido /s/ en posición final; cuando le pedí que dijera "María José tiene dos", ella respondió casi perfecto con claves moderadas.

Seguimos usando el enfoque Hanen para fomentar el lenguaje durante las rutinas diarias en casa, y esta semana comenzamos a probar algunas tarjetas del programa PECS para apoyar su comunicación cuando se frustra o no encuentra la palabra que busca. Les recomiendo seguir narrando en voz alta lo que hacen juntos, en inglés o en español, porque eso ayuda mucho a su desarrollo.

Sé que esta temporada ha sido muy ocupada para toda la familia. Rosa Elena Gómez, quien cuida a MJ por las tardes, me contó que esta semana también trabajó turnos extra en el Servicio de Limpieza Manos Limpias, así que agradezco mucho que ella pudiera traerla hoy. Entiendo también que Lucía tiene turnos largos en la Deep River Family Store y que Carlos sigue en el turno de noche en la Planta de Procesamiento de Pollo Monte Verde. Por eso propongo que hablemos por teléfono la próxima semana en lugar de reunirnos en persona, si les parece bien.

El hermano mayor de María José, Diego Torres Fernández, la ayudó a practicar con las tarjetas durante la cena. La tía Elsa, quien trabaja en el Golden Dragon Restaurant, y el tío Mario, de la Granja El Trigal, estuvieron presentes el domingo y notaron que MJ habló más que de costumbre con su prima Camila. El papá de Camila, el tío Beto, quien trabaja en Blue Ridge Construction Company, también llevó a los niños al parque esa tarde.

Por último, quiero recordarles que nuestra próxima revisión del IFSP con la coordinadora de servicios, Yesenia Ruiz, del Centro de Desarrollo y Servicios para la Infancia del Condado de Durham (CDSICD), está programada para el 18 de noviembre de 2026. El CDSICD ya tiene la información actualizada del caso, con el número de expediente DH-2219847-NC, y el número de Medicaid de María José es 804921758K.

Si tienen preguntas o quieren reprogramar, pueden llamarme al (919) 555-0148 o escribirme a alopez@terapiasunidasnc.com. Represento a Terapias Unidas de Carolina del Norte, PLLC, con oficina en 204 Avenida Roxboro, Durham.

Con cariño y mucho orgullo por el progreso de María José,

Ana López
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje

IFSP REVIEW NOTE

Agency: Western Piedmont CDSA
Service Coordinator: Jennifer Osei, MSW
Interpreter: Carmen Reyes (Spanish/English)
Child: Mateo Vargas del Río (DOB January 14, 2024; age 2;9)
Record #: WP-24-01187
Medicaid #: 987654321A
Address: 412 Juniper Lane, Hickory, NC 28601
Home phone: (828) 555-2847
Mom cell: 828-555-3312
Dad cell: 828.555.7701
Email: delriofamily24@gmail.com
IFSP Review Date: October 9, 2026
Initial IFSP Date: March 3, 2026
Next Review Due: April 9, 2027
Clinician: Maria Fontes, M.S., CCC-SLP, Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Services

S:
Mom, Lucía del Río, and Dad, Ricardo Vargas-Soto, present for review in home; interpreter Carmen Reyes on speakerphone throughout. Both parents report via interpreter that Mateo "habla más en casa, pero todavía mezcla español e inglés" and "a veces grita cuando no lo entendemos" ("talks more at home but still mixes Spanish and English" and "sometimes screams when we don't understand him"). Mom states, "Mateo me dice 'quiero jugo' y 'más' pero no usa frases largas." Family's top priority remains Outcome 1: expressive language production of 2–3 word phrases across settings, so he can "pedir lo que necesita sin llorar."

Daily routine reviewed in detail. Mom works nights at the poultry processing plant Carolina Poultry Processing in Morganton, shift 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.; before that she worked days at the store Tienda La Económica. Dad, Ricardo Vargas-Soto, works day shift for the construction company Soto Construction Company, also called Compañía de Construcción Soto by family at home; he previously worked weekends at the restaurant Restaurante El Fogón. Because both parents' schedules overlap on weeknights, paternal grandmother, Elena Vargas, keeps Mateo and his older sister, Sofía, most evenings until Dad returns around 6:30 p.m. Elena Vargas also cleans houses part-time for the cleaning service Brightway Cleaning Services (Servicios de Limpieza Brightway) on days she is not watching the children. Maternal uncle, Tomás del Río, works the fields at the farm Finca Los Pinos in Valle Nuevo, Honduras, and calls weekly to check in; his number is +504 9988-4521. Maternal grandmother in Mexico can be reached at +52 1 55 5512 3487 for emergencies when Mom is unreachable at the plant.

Family continues to receive nutrition support through Catawba County WIC and is enrolled with Smart Start of Catawba County for playgroup referrals; SC Jennifer Osei coordinates both. Mateo attends Little Steps Daycare three days/week while parents work; his teacher, Ms. Patel, reports he is "starting to request more" during snack and circle time but still points or gestures for most wants, and occasionally pushes peers, including a classmate, Josiah, when toys are taken.

Mom's priorities, in her own words: "Quiero que hable más, que pida lo que necesita sin llorar, y que juegue con otros niños." ("I want him to talk more, to ask for what he needs without crying, and to play with other kids.") Dad adds: "También queremos que entienda las dos lenguas, porque en casa hablamos los dos. No queremos que se le quite el español." ("We also want him to understand both languages, because we speak both at home. We don't want him to lose his Spanish.") Both parents deny new medical concerns; family dog, a terrier mix named Luna, remains a frequent play partner and comfort object per Mom.

O:
Session conducted in home, 4:00 p.m.–4:45 p.m., bilingual Spanish/English, w/ interpreter present. Mateo presents w/ dx of mixed expressive-receptive language delay (ICD-10 F80.2) per initial eval February 20, 2026. CPT 92523 billed for combined artic/language eval at that time; today's update billed under CPT 92507.

Admin'd PLS-5 Spanish subtests for update: Auditory Comprehension standard score 76 (5th %ile), Expressive Communication standard score 71 (3rd %ile), Total Language Score 72, 90% CI 65-79. Compare to initial scores of 68 and 64 respectively, Total Language Score 66 (CI 60-72) — modest gains noted but scores remain >1.5 SD below mean in both languages.

MLU in spontaneous play sample: 1.6 morphemes (English context), 1.4 (Spanish context), up from 1.1 and 1.0 at initial eval. Of 12 sampled utterances, 8/12 were single-word; 4/12 were two-word combinations, including "more jugo," "no mamá," and "Luna come."

During play w/ toy animals, Mateo picked up a small dog figure, patted it, and said, "Luna run," clearly referencing the family dog. Later, shown a family photo, he pointed to a girl in school clothes and said, "Sofía bye-bye," appropriately labeling his sister leaving for school. Both spontaneous combinations coded [EW] per SALT conventions for early word combination.

Articulation screening: substitutions noted on /r/ → [w] (e.g., "wabbit" for "rabbit," "wojo" for "rojo"), broadly consistent w/ 26-month developmental norms; stimulable to min cues in structured imitation. Final consonant deletion present in 3 of 5 trials on CVC targets in both languages. Fronting noted on /k/ → [t] in 2/5 trials. No concerns for oral-motor structure or function; diadochokinetic rates WNL for age.

Social/pragmatic: mod cues needed to sustain turn-taking during ball rolling game; initiated joint attention 6/10 opportunities, up from 3/10 at initial eval. Gestural communication remains a strength; reliably combines point + vocalization to request, and uses a headshake "no" appropriately when offered a disliked snack.

Birth history reviewed per parent report: born at 36 weeks gestation, birth weight 5 lb 8 oz, Apgar 8/9. No NICU stay, no feeding concerns in infancy. Bilingual exposure since birth, w/ Spanish primary at home and increased English exposure at Little Steps Daycare since August 2025. Hearing screening at Catawba Valley Medical Center on February 10, 2026 documented WNL bilaterally.

A:
Mateo continues to meet NC Infant-Toddler Program eligibility criteria for developmental delay in the expressive and receptive language domains, consistent w/ ICD-10 F80.2. Progress is evident since the initial IFSP (March 3, 2026) in early word combinations, MLU, and joint attention, though standard scores remain in the delayed range across both languages assessed. Family's stated priorities align closely w/ continued focus on functional, two-language communication across home, daycare, and community settings. Per current evidence, family should not be counseled to reduce Spanish input; dual-language exposure supports rather than delays this presentation, and this was discussed directly w/ both parents through the interpreter today.

+ Name: Mateo de la Cruz Rodríguez
+ CA: 2;10
+ Context: NC Infant-Toddler Program, Annual IFSP Review

Summary: Mateo is a bilingual (Spanish/English) boy, chronological age 2;10, seen for his annual IFSP review following twelve months of early intervention speech-language services. Mateo presents with a severe expressive and moderate receptive language delay consistent with ICD-10 F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). He attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center part-time in Ms. Lopez's room and continues to receive home-based speech-language therapy twice weekly through Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates. This review was completed with his family, his service coordinator, and his speech-language pathologist present.

Family Information

Mateo lives at 214 Birchwood Lane, Cary, NC 27511, in Wake County, with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez-Paz; his father, Carlos de la Cruz; and his older sister, Valentina de la Cruz Rodríguez, age seven. Lucía works two jobs to support the family: a morning shift stocking produce at Food Lion and an afternoon cafeteria position with WCPSS. Because of this schedule, Mateo's maternal grandmother, Ofelia Paz, provides childcare most weekday afternoons and attends therapy sessions when Lucía cannot. Carlos works full time as a maintenance technician and is present for most evening home visits. The family's home phone is 919-555-2048 and Lucía's email is lucia.rodriguezpaz@gmail.com. Mateo's Medicaid ID is 925374681B, and his CDSA record number is IT-20458.

Mateo's family dog, Rocky, is frequently mentioned in session; Mateo often points to Rocky and says "go" when he wants to take him outside.

Service Coordination

Mateo's service coordinator, Ana Torres, is employed through Coordinación de Servicios Familiares y de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Wake (referred to by the family as CSF de Wake). Ana has coordinated this case since intake in November 2024 and conducted the family interview portion of this review by phone and in person. Ana can be reached at 919-555-7721 or ana.torres@csfwake.org. Ana noted that the family has been consistent with appointments despite Lucía's demanding work schedule, and that Carlos has become increasingly comfortable implementing home strategies independently.

CDSA Office

This IFSP is held through the Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Piedmont, known locally as the CDSA del Piedmont, located in Durham. The intake and eligibility determination were completed at that office on November 18, 2024, and today's annual review was likewise coordinated through the CDSA del Piedmont office. The CDSA case file number CDSA-4471-NC should be referenced for all billing and authorization correspondence.

Family Concerns and Priorities

During the review interview, Lucía shared her primary concern in her own words: "He gets so frustrated when he can't tell me what he wants. He points and grunts, and sometimes he just cries because I don't understand him fast enough, and I feel like I'm failing him between my shifts." Carlos added, "At Little Sprouts, Ms. Lopez says he watches the other kids talk and just goes quiet. We want him to have words before kindergarten, in both English and Spanish, so he's not left behind." The family's stated priorities for the coming year are: (1) increase Mateo's spoken vocabulary in both languages; (2) decrease frustration-related tantrums at home and at Little Sprouts; and (3) support Mateo's participation in group activities with his classmate, Diego Fuentes, whom he follows closely during free play.

Lucía also noted that her mother, Ofelia, sometimes responds to Mateo's gestures too quickly, which may be reducing his motivation to use words; this was discussed as a coaching point for upcoming visits.

Daily Routines

Mateo's typical weekday begins around 7:00 a.m. with breakfast prepared by Carlos before Carlos leaves for work. Ofelia arrives by 8:30 a.m. and takes Mateo to Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, where he stays in Ms. Lopez's room until early afternoon. Ms. Lopez reports that Mateo is affectionate with peers but relies heavily on pulling adults by the hand rather than requesting verbally. After daycare, Ofelia cares for Mateo and his sister, Valentina, until Lucía returns from her second shift around 6:00 p.m.. Dinner, bath, and a bedtime book routine with Carlos close out the evening, with therapy home-practice folded into bath time play, per family report.

On weekends, the family visits Lake Lynn Park in Raleigh, where Mateo enjoys the swings and will occasionally request "up" or "más" (more) when motivated.

Other Agencies

In addition to CDSA services, the family receives nutrition support through WIC and has an open file with Smart Start of Wake County for the childcare subsidy that makes Mateo's placement at Little Sprouts possible. Mateo's developmental pediatrician, Dr. Angela Whitfield, at UNC Children's Developmental Clinic, completed the diagnostic evaluation supporting the F80.2 diagnosis and continues to monitor Mateo at six-month intervals. A referral to the Department of Social Services for emergency childcare backup was discussed but not pursued further, as Ofelia's availability currently meets the family's needs.

Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1: Mateo will use two- to three-word combinations to request preferred items and activities in both English and Spanish across home, Little Sprouts, and community settings.
Strategy: Continue Hanen-based coaching with Lucía and Carlos on expectant waiting and modeling; introduce core vocabulary board for use during meals and bath time; Ms. Lopez to model two-word models during circle time.

Outcome 2: Mateo will reduce frustration-related behaviors (crying, hitting) by substituting a gesture or word for a wanted item in 8 of 10 observed opportunities.
Strategy: Teach a consistent sign for "help" and "more"; coach Ofelia and daycare staff on waiting three seconds before intervening; reinforce any approximation, including vocalization-only attempts.

Outcome 3: Mateo will imitate and spontaneously produce the sounds /m/, /b/, and /w/ in single words with moderate cues, supporting intelligibility for both English and Spanish targets.
Strategy: Use PROMPT-informed tactile cueing during structured play; target words include "mamá", "más", and "bye"; home practice embedded in snack routine.

Outcome 4: Mateo will engage in joint play with a peer for 3 of 5 observed turns, initiating or responding to a play bid with a word, sign, or clear gesture.
Strategy: Structure short parallel-play activities with Diego Fuentes at Little Sprouts; Ms. Lopez to prompt and reinforce shared turn-taking during blocks and sensory bin play.

Evaluation Data and Service Record

Annual reassessment was completed using PLS-5 and REEL-4. On the PLS-5, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 62 (1st percentile), with a confidence interval of 58-68 on the expressive subtest. His overall receptive-expressive age equivalent fell within the range of 1;8–2;0. Articulation probe data showed Mateo correctly producing target consonants in 8/10 trials, approximately 80% accuracy, up from 40% at the prior annual review.

Services this year were billed under CPT 92507 (individual speech-language treatment) and CPT 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression), with the -GN modifier applied for all speech-language pathology claims. Diagnosis code F80.2 remains current and was reconfirmed by Dr. Whitfield on September 9, 2026.

Service Dates

Mateo's initial IFSP was signed on November 25, 2024, with services beginning December 2, 2024. The six-month review occurred on May 14, 2025. This annual review was conducted on October 8, 2026, at the family's home, with the next annual review scheduled for October 2027 and a transition planning conference to be scheduled before Mateo's third birthday, December 15, 2026. Direct therapy will continue twice weekly at 4:00 p.m. on Tuesdays and Thursdays through Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, with Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP continuing as primary clinician and bilingual service provider.

This IFSP review was completed collaboratively by Lucía Rodríguez-Paz, Carlos de la Cruz, Ana Torres of CSF de Wake, and Jennifer Hayes of Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Associates, with input from Ms. Lopez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center incorporated by written report. The family signed consent for continued services on October 8, 2026, and a copy of this review was provided to the family in both English and Spanish per CDSA del Piedmont policy. Follow-up contact information for questions about this review: Ana Torres, 919-555-7721, or Jennifer Hayes at 919-555-3390.

IFSP Review Date: October 6, 2026
Previous IFSP Date: April 2, 2026

2. FAMILY CONCERNS, PRIORITIES, AND RESOURCES

Lucía Rodríguez shared, in her own words: "Queremos que Teo pueda decirnos lo que necesita sin frustrarse y sin pegar a su hermana." She added in English, "He only has maybe ten words, and half of them only Carmen understands."

Jorge Flores reported, "At Rainbow Roots Early Learning Cottage, the teacher says he points and grunts more than he talks. We want him talking before he starts real preschool."

The family's priorities for this review are: (1) increase Teo's spoken vocabulary in both languages; (2) reduce frustration-related aggression toward Camila; (3) coordinate strategies between home, Rainbow Roots Early Learning Cottage, and therapy.

Family resources include a strong extended network: Carmen Rodríguez provides afternoon care, the family attends Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida weekly, and Lucía Rodríguez brings Teo and Camila to the Hickory Public Library's Mother Goose on the Loose toddler program on Tuesdays.

3. PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT

Communication: On the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Teo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 76 (5th percentile) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), yielding age equivalents of 18 months and 16 months respectively (confidence interval 68-84). On the CELF-5 screening items administered informally, Teo followed 2 of 5 two-step directions.

Teo produces single words inconsistently, substituting /t/ for /k/ (e.g., "tat" for "cat") and omitting final consonants, as in "bah" for "ball." During the session, he imitated his sister's name as "Mi-wa" for "Mila." With moderate cues, he combined two words 3 of 10 trials ("more juice," "mama up"). He requires maximal cues for multisyllabic words.

Motor and Adaptive: Gross and fine motor skills are within normal limits per parent report and informal observation. Teo's pediatrician, Dr. Hannah Kim, confirmed no feeding concerns at the 12-month well-child visit.

Social-Emotional: Teo shows frustration-related behaviors (hitting, throwing) when unable to communicate wants, occurring an estimated 4-6 times daily per parent report.

Medical: Diagnosis of expressive-receptive language delay, ICD-10 F80.2, supports continued eligibility. CPT code 92523 was used for the diagnostic speech-language evaluation.

4. FAMILY DAILY ROUTINES

Teo wakes around 6:45 a.m. and eats breakfast with Jorge Flores before Jorge Flores leaves for work. Lucía Rodríguez drops Teo at Rainbow Roots Early Learning Cottage by 8:15 a.m., where his teacher, Ms. Patricia Nguyen, reports he plays near peers but rarely initiates with them, including his favorite playmate, Benji Walsh.

Carmen Rodríguez picks Teo up at 3:30 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays, when Lucía Rodríguez works a later shift at Catawba Valley Linens. Dinner is family-style around 6:00 p.m., followed by bath and a bedtime story, with lights out near 8:30 p.m.. Weekends include the library program and church fellowship meals after the 11:00 a.m. service at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Vida.

5. OTHER AGENCIES, PROGRAMS, AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES

The family receives nutrition support through WIC and was referred by Foothills CDSA to Smart Start of Catawba County for a developmental playgroup. The family is not currently involved with DSS. Teo's case remains open with Foothills CDSA for continued service coordination through Angela Brooks. The family's medical home is Catawba Valley Pediatrics, where Dr. Hannah Kim practices.

6. IFSP OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Teo will use two-word combinations to request and comment across home, Rainbow Roots Early Learning Cottage, and community settings, increasing from 30% to 70% of observed opportunities.
Strategies: Use Hanen-based strategies (OWL: Observe, Wait, Listen) during play; expand utterances in both Spanish and English; use PROMPT tactile cueing to support final consonants.

Outcome 2: Teo will replace hitting with a word, sign, or gesture to express frustration in 4 of 5 observed instances.
Strategies: Model simple signs ("more," "help," "done"); Carmen Rodríguez and Ms. Patricia Nguyen will use identical cue phrases; reinforce attempts immediately.

Outcome 3: Family will report increased confidence supporting language at home, measured by parent-report checklist, improving from 2 of 10 to 8 of 10 items endorsed.
Strategies: Biweekly coaching with Sofía Martínez; bilingual home visuals; shared log between Carmen Rodríguez and Ms. Patricia Nguyen.

7. SERVICE DELIVERY, FREQUENCY, AND DATES

Speech-language therapy: individual sessions, 60 minutes, twice weekly, Tuesdays 9:00 a.m.–10:00 a.m. and Thursdays 1:15 p.m.–2:15 p.m., beginning October 14, 2026 and continuing through the next annual review, April 2, 2027.
Developmental playgroup through Smart Start of Catawba County: weekly, Wednesdays 10:30 a.m.–11:30 a.m., beginning October 21, 2026.
Service coordination check-in: monthly by phone, next scheduled November 9, 2026.

Evaluation and planning dates on record: initial eligibility evaluation February 11, 2026; initial IFSP February 25, 2026; six-month review April 2, 2026; current review October 6, 2026; annual review due April 2, 2027.

8. TEAM PARTICIPANTS AND SIGNATURES

Present at this meeting: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Jorge Flores (father, by phone), Angela Brooks (service coordinator), Sofía Martínez, M.S., CCC-SLP (report author), Ms. Patricia Nguyen (lead teacher, Rainbow Roots Early Learning Cottage).

For program information, visit www.foothillscdsa.nc.gov or www.rainbowrootslearning.com.

Signatures on file. This IFSP review was completed collaboratively and reflects the family's stated concerns, priorities, and resources as of the date above.

Centro de Desarrollo Infantil y Servicios de Apoyo (CDSA) of the Piedmont Region
4420 Harvest Lane, Suite 200, Graylin, NC 27455

October 9, 2026

Dear Marisol Vega and Daniel Vega,

It was wonderful to see Teo again at his IFSP review this week. Thank you both for making time to come to CDSA in the middle of a busy week, and thank you to doña Lupe for driving over to join us too. Below is a summary of what we talked about, in plain language, so you can keep it with your IFSP binder at home.

**Who was there**

We met at 10:00 a.m. in the small conference room. In the room were Teo, you two, doña Lupe (Teo's grandmother), his service coordinator Miss Ana, his early intervention speech-language pathologist Mr. Tom, and me, Carla Fuentes, his bilingual SLP. We also had Sra. Ibarra on the phone as our Spanish interpreter for part of the meeting, since doña Lupe feels most comfortable in Spanish.

**Child and family information**

Teo was born on February 14, 2024 at Graylin Regional Medical Center, at a gestational age of 36 weeks and a birth weight of 5 lbs 8 oz. His Apgar scores were 8 and 9. He is now 2;7 years old. He lives with you at 118 Marigold Court, Graylin, NC 27455, along with his big sister Camila, who is seven. His Medicaid ID is MV4482913K, and his CDSA record number is CDSA-2024-0617.

**What you told us matters most**

In your own words, you shared these concerns and priorities:

"We just want Teo to be able to tell us what he needs instead of screaming and pointing. Right now his sister Camila ends up guessing for him, and that is not fair to her either."

"At Little Sprouts Daycare, Ms. Lopez says he gets frustrated during circle time in Ms. Lopez's room because the other kids can answer questions and he cannot."

"We want him ready for preschool in Ms. Lopez's room next year, and we want to understand what we can do at home, especially since we speak Spanish and English both."

**Daily routines**

Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m. and has breakfast with Camila before Daniel Vega drops him at Little Sprouts Daycare by 8:15 a.m.. He naps from about 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m.. doña Lupe picks him up most afternoons and stays with him until Marisol Vega gets home around 5:30 p.m.. Dinner and bath time are the routines where you say he talks the most, often mixing Spanish and English words.

**Other agencies involved**

Teo also receives WIC support through the Guilford County Department of Social Services, and the family has applied for additional childcare subsidy through Smart Start of Piedmont County. Miss Ana is coordinating with both agencies so paperwork does not get duplicated.

**Evaluation summary**

I completed a bilingual speech-language evaluation on September 22, 2026. Teo was administered the PLS-5 in both English and Spanish with support from Sra. Ibarra. His Auditory Comprehension standard score was 73-83 (combined English/Spanish range), and his Expressive Communication standard score fell in the range of 70-78, both in the range typically described as significantly below average. His overall language age equivalent was 1;8–2;0, compared to his chronological age of 2;7.

On the CELF-5 screening items we attempted, he was stimulable for single words but not yet combining two words reliably; he produced two-word combinations in only 2 of 10 opportunities (20%). His intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at 30-40% to unfamiliar listeners.

Diagnosis: F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder).

**Session notes since the last IFSP**

During a recent session, Teo was working on requesting using PECS. He exchanged a picture for "juice" with min cues in 8/10 trials (80%). When imitating target words, he produced "agua" as [ˈa.wa] with mod cues, approximating the target /ˈa.ɣwa/. He also attempted "more" and produced it as "mo," dropping the final /r/ consonant, which is developmentally appropriate at this age.

We also began light exposure to Hanen strategies with you both, focusing on "OWL" (observe, wait, listen) during play, and doña Lupe has started using the same strategy during afternoon routines, which is wonderful carryover.

**Updated outcomes and strategies**

*Outcome 1:* Teo will use two-word combinations ("want juice," "más agua") to request preferred items across home and daycare settings, increasing from 20% to 60% of opportunities over the next six months.
Strategy: Continue PECS with fading cues; Ms. Lopez will model two-word phrases during snack time in her classroom; family will model bilingual two-word phrases during dinner and bath routines.

*Outcome 2:* Teo will reduce frustration-related tantrum behaviors during group activities at Little Sprouts Daycare by using a picture or gesture to request a break, in 3 of 5 observed opportunities.
Strategy: Ms. Lopez and classroom aide la maestra Carmen will keep a visual "break" card available during circle time; coordinate with Mr. Tom on classroom visits twice monthly.

*Outcome 3:* Teo will improve speech sound intelligibility, particularly producing final consonants in single words, from an estimated 30-40% to 50-60% intelligibility with familiar listeners.
Strategy: Direct therapy targeting final /t/, /k/, and /n/ in structured play using PROMPT touch cues; home practice with simple words during bath time.

**Services and dates**

Speech-language therapy will continue twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, billed under CPT 92523 (evaluation, already completed) and CPT 92507 (individual treatment, ongoing). Sessions will alternate between CDSA and Little Sprouts Daycare, coordinated with Ms. Lopez.

This review covers the period from April 15, 2026 through today, October 9, 2026. The next IFSP review is scheduled for April 9, 2027. Your annual eligibility redetermination is due by February 14, 2027, before Teo's third birthday, when we will also begin transition planning toward preschool services.

**Contacts**

If you have any questions before our next visit, please reach out:

CDSA main office: (336) 555-0148

Thank you again for your partnership and for all the practice you are doing at home. Teo is lucky to have so many people, including doña Lupe and big sister Camila, cheering him on.

BACKGROUND:
Mateo del Río was referred to Western CDSA at 18 months by pediatrician Dr. James Whitfield 2˚ parental concern re: limited expressive vocab (<10 words) and occasional ear infections. Initial IFSP eval (February 10, 2026) confirmed eligibility under dx F80.2 (mixed receptive-expressive language disorder). Family had no prior EI involvement; this is pt's first IFSP. CG reports normal pregnancy, no complications.

REASON FOR REVIEW:
This is a 6-month review of the IFSP initially written February 10, 2026, following Mateo del Río's eligibility determination under dx F80.2 and informal concern re: speech sound intelligibility.

FAMILY CONCERNS & PRIORITIES (family's own words, via bilingual CG, translated/transcribed by SC):
- "Teo gets so frustrated b/c we don't understand him — he points and grunts and then cries."
- "We want him to be able to tell his sister Sofía del Río what he wants w/o a tantrum."

- "My sister Lupe Hernández helps a lot on weekends, but during the week it's just me and Rosa Martínez."
- CG priority: pt communicate basic wants/needs at home and at Little Sprouts Daycare w/ reduced frustration behaviors.

DAILY ROUTINES:
- Wakes approx 6:30 AM, breakfast w/ Ana del Río and Sofía del Río before daycare drop-off

OTHER AGENCIES/SUPPORTS INVOLVED:

PROGRESS SINCE LAST IFSP:
Since initial IFSP, pt's expressive vocab ↑ from <10 words to approx 35-40 words/approximations (per CG log and daycare report). Pt now imitates 2-word phrases w/ mod cues approx 60% of trials, up from near-zero at initial eval. CG reports improved joint attention and turn-taking during play routines. Ms. Carla Jennings notes pt increasingly attempts verbal requests rather than grabbing from classmate Liam Brooks or other peers, though frustration behaviors persist during transitions. Carlos Vega reports high stress re: balancing night shift at Ingles Distribution Center w/ attending sessions; family requests more flexible scheduling where possible.

TRANSITION PLANNING:
B/c pt will turn 3 years old in April 2027, SC Megan Alvarez-Boone has initiated preliminary transition planning discussion w/ family re: potential Part B eligibility / preschool special ed. referral to Buncombe County Schools approx 6 mo prior to 3rd birthday. Family expressed interest in continued bilingual support regardless of setting.

SENSORY/OT CONSULT NOTE:
Grace Thompson, OTR/L, completed informal sensory consult May 28, 2026 2˚ CG report of mealtime texture aversion; recommendations incorporated into daily routine above (spoon use, mod cues, gradual texture exposure).

---

EVALUATION SUMMARY (current review):
Admin June 3, 2026 by this SLP:
- Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale: receptive AE 16-18 months, expressive AE 14-16 months (chronological age 26 months); overall language functioning approx 40-45% below CA
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3: SS 72 (3rd percentile), CI 68-76; multiple phoneme errors incl final consonant deletion, fronting of /k/ → [t], stopping of /s/
- Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-2 (gross motor subtest only, PT collab): SS 78, age equiv 20-22 months
- Bayley-4 (cognitive, SC-administered): composite SS 85, 16th percentile

Oromotor exam WNL. Hearing: passed most recent screen bilaterally. Play skills: pt engages in approx 5 min of functional/pretend play w/ mod cues; limited symbolic play noted.

Sample utterances (spontaneous, English & Spanish mixed, this SLP + interpreter present):
- CG models "más" (more); pt imitates "ma" 8/10 trials (80%)
- Target word "agua" (water); pt produces "ba" 3 of 5 trials w/ min cues
- Pt labels ball spontaneously: "ba" (no /l/, final consonant deletion); w/ mod cues approximates "bah-o" for "balón"
- When shown dog photo, pt says "Rocky run" — referencing family pet Rocky

---

IFSP OUTCOMES (updated June 10, 2026):

Outcome 1: Mateo del Río will use 2-word combinations in Spanish and/or English to request desired items at home and daycare, as measured by CG/teacher report and direct observation, achieving 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive data collection pts.
Strategies: Hanen-based CG coaching ("It Takes Two to Talk" framework); modeling + expansion of pt's single-word utterances; use of core vocabulary board at daycare and home; CG to model bilingual input consistently, following child's lead.

Outcome 2: Mateo del Río will reduce frustration-related behaviors (crying, hitting) during communication breakdowns from current baseline of approx 6-8 episodes/day to 2-3 episodes/day, per CG daily log.
Strategies: Teach CG + Rosa Martínez + Carla Jennings a consistent set of 3-5 core signs/gestures paired w/ verbal models; visual schedule for daycare transitions; Megan Alvarez-Boone to coordinate w/ Little Sprouts Daycare re: carryover.

Outcome 3: Mateo del Río will imitate/produce target CV and CVC words w/ improved phonetic inventory (incl. final consonants), moving from current 8/10 deletion rate to 50% accurate production of final consonants across 10 trials.
Strategies: Cycles phonological approach targeting final consonant deletion and stopping patterns; home practice sheets in Spanish/English; PROMPT-informed tactile cueing during tx sessions as needed.

Outcome 4 (new, added at this review): Family will access Early Intervention supports consistently w/o transportation barriers, as evidenced by 90% session attendance over next 6 mo.
