text:
Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC
d/b/a Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Speech ("CBPST")
118 Mill Pond Road, Suite 4, Brookhaven, NC 28455
Office: (910) 555-7700 | Fax: (910) 555-7701

SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT
(Bilingual English/Spanish Assessment)

CLIENT INFORMATION

Client Name: Mateo Alejandro Reyes Castillo, called "Teo" at home
Date of Birth: April 3, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 5;5
Gender: Male
Home Languages: Spanish (primary) and English (secondary, acquired through daycare and television)
Mother: Lucía Rodríguez Reyes
Father: Jesús Reyes Delgado, known to the family and to Teo's teachers as "Chuy"
Address: 482 Willow Creek Lane, Brookhaven, NC 28455, Harnwood County
Home Phone: (910) 555-2847
Mother's Cell: 910.555.9931
Father's Cell: 910-555-4412
Email: lucia.reyes82@mailbox.com
Medicaid ID: NC8847291X
CDSA Case Number: CDSA-2026-01837
Evaluation Dates: September 18, 2026 and September 25, 2026
Report Date: October 2, 2026
Evaluator: Isabel Marquez, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist, Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Speech
Referral Source: Dr. James Patterson, pediatrician, and Linda Chen, Service Coordinator, Harnwood County CDSA

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo was referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by Dr. James Patterson following his four-year well-child visit, at which Lucía Rodríguez Reyes voiced ongoing concern about her son's speech intelligibility in both Spanish and English. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes reported that familiar listeners understand roughly 60% of Mateo's speech, while unfamiliar listeners, including his daycare teacher, understand far less. Linda Chen at Harnwood County CDSA coordinated the referral and confirmed Medicaid authorization prior to scheduling. This evaluation was requested to determine Mateo's current speech and language skills in both languages, to establish eligibility for ongoing services, and to guide treatment planning before his transition into kindergarten.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Lucía Rodríguez Reyes reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care. Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation at Piedmont Valley Medical Center via spontaneous vaginal delivery. Birth weight was 3,118 grams (6 lbs 14 oz), and Apgar scores were 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes. No NICU stay was required. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes reported a history of recurrent bilateral ear infections beginning around 14 months, treated with multiple courses of antibiotics. Mateo underwent bilateral myringotomy with tube placement (CPT 69436) at 22 months, performed by Dr. Angela Ruiz at Piedmont Valley Medical Center. A follow-up audiogram at 3;1 showed hearing within normal limits bilaterally. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes stated that frequent ear infections overlapped with the period when Mateo was expected to begin combining words, and she wonders whether this contributed to his current difficulties. No history of seizures, head injury, or hospitalization beyond the tube placement was reported. Mateo is not currently on any medications. Vision was last screened at his five-year well-child visit with Dr. James Patterson and was reported as within normal limits.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo lives with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Reyes and Jesús Reyes Delgado ("Chuy"), his older sister Guadalupe Reyes, age 8, called "Lupita" by the family, and his younger brother José Reyes, age 2, called "Pepe." The family also has a dog named "Rocky," whom Mateo mentioned repeatedly during both sessions. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes was born in Veracruz, Mexico, and Jesús Reyes Delgado was born in Comayagua, Honduras; both immigrated to Harnwood County before Guadalupe Reyes was born. Spanish is the dominant language spoken in the home among all family members; Jesús Reyes Delgado reported speaking almost exclusively Spanish with the children, while Lucía Rodríguez Reyes code-switches more frequently, particularly when helping Guadalupe Reyes with schoolwork. Mateo's maternal grandmother, who lives in Mexico, calls the family several times a week; her number is +52 229 123 4567, and Lucía Rodríguez Reyes noted that Mateo enjoys talking to her on video calls, though she often asks Lucía Rodríguez Reyes to "translate what he's trying to say."

Mateo's cousin, Juan Hernández, called "Juanito" by the family, is approximately the same age and visits most weekends; Lucía Rodríguez Reyes reported that the two boys play well together but that Mateo often lets Juanito speak for him when adults ask questions. A family friend, Rosa Hernández, babysits Mateo and his siblings two evenings a week while Lucía Rodríguez Reyes works a late shift; Rosa Hernández speaks only Spanish with the children. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes works at Riverside Poultry Processing, and Jesús Reyes Delgado operates a small landscaping business, Reyes Landscaping & Lawn Care. Both parents described long work hours, which Lucía Rodríguez Reyes feels limits the time she has to work directly on speech sounds at home, though she reported trying to repeat words back to Mateo "the right way" when she can.

Mateo has attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Center since he was 2;6, initially in a Spanish-dominant toddler room and more recently in a mixed-language pre-kindergarten classroom. His current teacher, Sarah Lopez, and assistant teacher, Monica Alvarez, both report that Mateo is social and eager to participate but is frequently misunderstood by peers. His classmates Ava Thompson, Diego Martínez, and Ethan Brooks were named by Sarah Lopez as children Mateo plays with most often; Sarah Lopez noted that Diego Martínez, who is also bilingual, sometimes repeats Mateo's requests to other children "so they understand him."

DEVELOPMENTAL AND EDUCATIONAL HISTORY

Lucía Rodríguez Reyes reported that Mateo sat independently at 6 months, walked at 13 months, and said his first words, "mamá" and "papá," around 12 months, consistent with typical milestones. She reported that word combinations in Spanish did not emerge until closer to 30 months, and that English words began appearing only after Mateo started the mixed-language classroom at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center around age 4. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes and Jesús Reyes Delgado both agreed that Mateo's speech intelligibility has always lagged behind that of Guadalupe Reyes at the same age, and that family members, including Rosa Hernández and the maternal grandmother, have commented on this difference for some time.

Mateo is enrolled to begin kindergarten at Brookhaven Elementary School in August 2027. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes expressed concern about how Mateo's speech will be understood by a new teacher and classmates who may not share his home language, and this concern was a significant motivation for pursuing this evaluation now, ahead of the transition.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with the examiner across both sessions, which were conducted primarily in Spanish with English probes interspersed as appropriate for each measure. He demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks lasting 15–20 minutes before requiring a brief break. Mateo was cooperative and motivated by praise and a sticker chart. His speech was markedly less intelligible to the examiner during the first session than reported by Lucía Rodríguez Reyes for familiar listeners, which is consistent with typical patterns in which children are better understood by caregivers than by unfamiliar adults. No concerns regarding voice quality, resonance, or fluency were noted; Mateo did not exhibit dysfluencies, struggle behaviors, or secondary characteristics during either session.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES

The following standardized and informal measures were administered across both sessions, with Spanish-language forms used where available and English probes added for cross-linguistic comparison:

- Parent interview and case history review
- Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), Spanish-English Bilingual Edition
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), administered in English with Spanish phonological analysis supplement
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Phonology and Morphosyntax subtests
- Spontaneous language sample analysis, Spanish and English, with SALT coding
- Oral-motor examination and hearing screening
- Classroom and play-based observation

TEST RESULTS

On the PLS-5 Bilingual Edition, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 78 (7th percentile), with a 90% confidence interval of 73–83, and an Expressive Communication standard score of 71 (3rd percentile), with a confidence interval of 65–77. His Total Language Score was 73 (4th percentile), confidence interval 68-78. On the BESA Morphosyntax subtest, administered in both languages, Mateo scored at the 9th percentile in Spanish and the 5th percentile in English, both below the clinical cutoff, suggesting a language impairment present across both languages rather than a difference attributable to typical bilingual development alone.

Summary Score Table

Measure | Language | Standard Score | Percentile | 90% CI | Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | Bilingual | 78 | 7 | 73–83 | 3;6–4;0
PLS-5 Expressive Communication | Bilingual | 71 | 3 | 65–77 | 2;6–3;0
PLS-5 Total Language Score | Bilingual | 73 | 4 | 68-78 | 3;0–3;6
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | English | 64 | 1 | 58–70 | 3;0–3;6
BESA Phonology | Spanish | 70 | 2 | 64–76 | 2;9–3;3

Mateo's profile across these measures is consistent with a moderate-to-severe mixed receptive-expressive language disorder occurring in both of his languages, accompanied by a moderate speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility.

ARTICULATION AND PHONOLOGY

On the GFTA-3, Mateo demonstrated a pattern of final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and fronting of velars. He produced the word "car" as "tar" and "cup" as "tup", substituting /t/ for /k/ in word-initial position. He produced "dog" as "dod", and when prompted to name the family dog, said "mi perrito Rocky 'ta aquí," omitting the final /s/ expected in a fully developed utterance. In Spanish, Mateo produced "taza" as "tata", substituting /t/ for the medial /s/, and produced "árbol" as "ábo", omitting the liquid cluster and the tapped /ɾ/. He consistently simplified the trilled /r/ and tapped /ɾ/ to [w] or omitted them entirely, for example producing "ratón" as "watón". Stimulability testing showed that Mateo could approximate /k/ in isolation and in syllables with moderate cues, but could not yet produce it reliably in connected speech. He produced 3 of 10 target consonant clusters correctly with maximal cues across the session.

Connected speech intelligibility was estimated at approximately 50% for unfamiliar listeners and 70% for familiar listeners, based on examiner judgment and parent report, consistent with the concerns that prompted referral.

LANGUAGE SAMPLE AND PRAGMATICS

A spontaneous language sample was collected during play with toy animals and a classroom-themed dollhouse. Mateo's mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was 3.1 in Spanish and 2.6 in English, both below age expectations. SALT coding identified frequent omission of grammatical morphemes, including the Spanish plural marker and verb tense agreement, coded as [EW] errors in 6 of 20 utterances. Mateo used primarily subject-verb-object word order with limited use of connectives or embedded clauses. He initiated communication appropriately with the examiner and showed adequate eye contact and turn-taking, but relied heavily on gesture and single-word utterances when a listener did not understand him on the first attempt, rather than attempting to repair or rephrase.

During a brief observation at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Sarah Lopez reported that Mateo often defers to Diego Martínez in group activities and becomes quiet when asked direct questions by unfamiliar adults, which Sarah Lopez attributes in part to frustration over not being understood. Lucía Rodríguez Reyes confirmed that Mateo behaves similarly at home when his nickname "Teo" does not get a response quickly enough, sometimes resorting to pulling on a sleeve or pointing rather than repeating himself.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) affecting both Spanish and English, along with a moderate speech sound disorder (ICD-10 F80.0) characterized by final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, velar fronting, and liquid simplification. These findings are consistent across both of Mateo's languages, which supports a true bilingual language impairment rather than a language difference secondary to typical second-language acquisition. The recurrent otitis media history and bilateral tube placement reported by Lucía Rodríguez Reyes and documented by Dr. Angela Ruiz may have contributed to early delays, though normal hearing on the most recent audiogram suggests hearing is not currently a limiting factor. Mateo's strengths include social engagement, imitation skills, and stimulability for several error sounds with cueing, all of which are favorable prognostic indicators for therapy.

Given the upcoming transition to Brookhaven Elementary School, early and intensive intervention is strongly recommended to improve Mateo's intelligibility and language skills before he enters a classroom environment with less bilingual support than Little Sprouts Early Learning Center currently provides.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo qualifies for and should begin bilingual speech-language therapy services twice weekly, 30-minute individual sessions (CPT 92507), targeting both articulation and expressive/receptive language goals, provided through CBPST under his existing Medicaid authorization.
2. Therapy should address the phonological patterns identified above using a Cycles phonological approach, targeting /k, g/ fronting, final consonant deletion, and cluster reduction, with generalization probes in both Spanish and English.
3. A trial of PROMPT tactile-kinesthetic cueing is recommended to support placement for the tapped /ɾ/ and trilled /r/ in Spanish, given Mateo's stimulability with cueing.
4. Parent coaching using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies is recommended to help Lucía Rodríguez Reyes and Jesús Reyes Delgado support language expansion during daily routines at home, given the family's reported time constraints.
5. Continued collaboration with Sarah Lopez and Monica Alvarez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center is recommended, including a brief classroom consultation prior to the August 2027 kindergarten transition.
6. A referral to Harnwood County CDSA for transition planning with Linda Chen is recommended to ensure continuity of services as Mateo moves from daycare into the public school system.
7. Re-evaluation of hearing is recommended if any recurrence of ear infections occurs, given Mateo's prior history; families may also contact Smart Start of Harnwood County for additional community-based language enrichment resources.
8. Progress should be re-assessed in approximately 6 months to determine continued medical necessity and update goals as needed.

This report and its recommendations were discussed with Lucía Rodríguez Reyes by phone at 4:30 p.m. on October 2, 2026, and a written copy will be provided in Spanish upon request. Please contact our office at (910) 555-7700 with any questions.

Respectfully submitted,

Isabel Marquez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Pediatric Speech & Language Therapy, PLLC

text:
**Individualized Family Service Plan — Initial IFSP and Six-Month Review**

This Individualized Family Service Plan was developed for Mateo Alejandro Cruz Ramírez, known to his family as Teo, born April 14, 2024, and reviewed on September 22, 2026 at the CDSA of the Triangle office located at 4108 Falls of Neuse Road, Suite 210 in Raleigh. The family lives at 214 Birchwood Lane in Garner, Wake County, ZIP 27529. Mateo's Medicaid number is 8827193645A and his CDSA case number is CDSA-2026-00417. This plan was written by Hannah Reyes, CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist with Carolina Early Steps Therapy, PLLC, who can be reached at (919) 555-0148 or hreyes@carolinaearlysteps.org. The family's service coordinator is Denise Walters of the CDSA of the Triangle.

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez, his father, Hernán Cruz, and his older sister, Camila Cruz Ramírez, who is six years old and attends first grade. His grandmother, Alicia Ramírez, lives nearby and helps with child care several afternoons a week, and the family's regular babysitter, Daniela Soto, watches Mateo on Lucía's overnight shifts. Lucía told this writer, in Spanish, "él entiende mucho más de lo que dice, y eso me preocupa" ("he understands much more than he says, and that worries me"). Hernán added, in English, "we just want him to be able to tell us what he needs before he gets so frustrated he starts screaming."

Mateo was born at 35 weeks gestation at Pinecrest Women's Hospital, with a birth weight of 4 lbs 11 oz and Apgar scores of 6 and 8. He spent eleven days in the NICU at Pinecrest Women's Hospital under the care of Dr. Samuel Okafor, neonatologist, for feeding and respiratory support. His pediatrician, Dr. Priya Patel, referred the family to the CDSA after Mateo's 18-month well visit showed fewer than ten words and limited babbling variety. Medical history is otherwise unremarkable; hearing was screened as within normal limits at birth and again at 24 months of age.

The family's primary concerns, in their own words, center on communication and frustration tolerance. Lucía said, "en la guardería las otras mamás me dicen que sus hijos ya hablan en oraciones, y Teo todavía señala y gruñe" ("at daycare the other moms tell me their children already speak in sentences, and Teo still points and grunts"). Hernán shared that he worries Mateo will fall behind once he starts preschool, and that family gatherings are hard because Mateo's cousins, Ximena Torres and Joaquín Torres, play together easily in both languages while Mateo often wanders off alone or gets upset when he cannot make himself understood. The family's priorities for this IFSP are: increasing Mateo's expressive vocabulary in both English and Spanish, reducing tantrum behavior linked to communication breakdown, and helping Mateo participate more successfully in group activities at daycare.

Mateo attends Little Sprouts Daycare on weekday mornings while Lucía sleeps after her overnight shift. Mom works nights at Harrison Foods Distribution Center, typically from 11:00 p.m. to 7:30 a.m., and Dad works days as a machine operator, which means Alicia Ramírez and Daniela Soto share drop-off and pickup duties during the week. At daycare, his teacher, Ms. Deborah Patterson, reports that Mateo enjoys circle time with classmates Ayden and Nilda but tends to watch rather than join in during songs. The assistant teacher, Ms. Karen Liu, noted that Mateo will point to a snack and grunt rather than attempt the word, and that he has started biting his own hand when he becomes frustrated during transitions.

At home, the family's typical morning routine runs from about 6:45 a.m. to 8:00 a.m.: Mateo wakes, eats breakfast at the kitchen table with Camila, and gets dressed with help from Alicia before daycare drop-off. He loves playing in the backyard with the family dog, Rocky, a terrier mix who tolerates being chased and hugged with great patience. Bath time around 7:00 p.m. is a high-motivation routine; Mateo will reach for the water and say what sounds like "/wabo/" for "water," which the family has started modeling back as a full word in both languages. Bedtime stories are read in Spanish by Lucía and in English by Hernán on alternating nights, giving Mateo regular exposure to both languages at home.

The family also receives support from several other agencies. They are enrolled with WIC for nutrition support and attend playgroups through Wake County Smart Start roughly once a month. The family was also referred to Wake County DSS earlier this year for help with childcare subsidy paperwork, which Denise Walters is assisting them to complete. Lucía reports that the Smart Start playgroup has been a good place for Mateo to be around other toddlers outside of daycare, though she notes he still prefers to play near her rather than with the other children.

Formal assessment was completed using the Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), administered in both English and Spanish, along with informal observation and the REEL-4 parent interview. Results are summarized below.

| Date | Subtest | Standard Score | Confidence Interval | Percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| March 3, 2026 | Auditory Comprehension | 73 | 68-78 | 4th |
| March 3, 2026 | Expressive Communication | 70 | 65-75 | 2nd |
| March 3, 2026 | Total Language Score | 71 | 67-76 | 3rd |
| September 2, 2026 | Auditory Comprehension | 79 | 74-84 | 8th |
| September 2, 2026 | Expressive Communication | 76 | 71-81 | 5th |

Mateo's age-equivalent scores on the Expressive Communication subtest rose from 14-16 months at the initial evaluation to 19-21 months at the six-month review, placing him within the 18 months to 22 months range overall, with receptive skills estimated at 2;0–2;3 and expressive skills estimated at 1;7–1;9. This represents a gap of approximately six months between receptive and expressive development, consistent with his pattern of understanding more than he produces.

During direct observation, Mateo used a total expressive vocabulary estimated at 35 words across both languages, with roughly 20 English words and 15 Spanish words, and no two-word combinations observed. He imitated the target word "more" with moderate cues 3 of 5 trials, and produced "up" approximated as "[ʌp]" independently in 8/10 opportunities when reaching to be picked up. When this writer modeled the Spanish word "pelota" (ball), Mateo responded with an approximation close to "[eota]" after minimal cues. His play skills are emerging appropriately for his age, including functional play with cause-and-effect toys and brief pretend sequences such as feeding a stuffed animal.

Based on these findings, the IFSP team, including Lucía Rodríguez, Hernán Cruz, Denise Walters, and this writer, developed the following outcomes.

Outcome 1 (IFSP Outcome 1): Mateo will use at least 50 single words across English and Spanish to request and comment during daily routines, as measured by parent report and direct observation, within six months. Strategies include modeling target words during bath time and backyard play with Rocky, using a core vocabulary board at daycare and at home, and having Alicia Ramírez and Daniela Soto narrate routines aloud in whichever language they are most comfortable using, since both languages support overall language growth.

Outcome 2 (IFSP Outcome 2): Mateo will combine two words together (for example "more water" or "más agua") in 3 of 5 observed opportunities within six months. Strategies include expansion of his single-word utterances by caregivers, use of the Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" approach during play, and brief weekly coaching sessions with Lucía and Hernán on expansion techniques they can use during bedtime stories and car rides.

Outcome 3 (IFSP Outcome 3): Mateo will use a word, approximation, or gesture paired with a word to communicate a need instead of grunting or self-biting, in 4 of 5 observed frustration episodes, within six months. Strategies include teaching Ms. Deborah Patterson and Ms. Karen Liu to prompt for a word before responding to a grunt, visual supports at daycare showing choices such as snack or outside, and consistent response from family members at home, including Alicia Ramírez, to wait for a communicative attempt before intervening.

Services under this plan include direct speech-language therapy twice weekly for thirty minutes, delivered in the home and at daycare in both English and Spanish by Hannah Reyes, beginning March 10, 2026 and continuing through this review date. Developmental therapy consultation is provided monthly by Marcus Webb, occupational therapist, to address sensory regulation strategies related to Mateo's frustration behaviors. Service coordination continues monthly with Denise Walters. The family has consented to continued services and requested that sessions remain scheduled around Lucía's sleep schedule when possible, given her overnight work hours.

At this six-month review, the team notes meaningful progress. Mateo's total language score rose from 71 to an estimated 78, within the 73-83 range reported above, and his self-biting behavior has decreased from several times daily to roughly twice weekly, according to both Lucía and Ms. Deborah Patterson. Mateo has begun approximating the names of his cousins, Ximena Torres and Joaquín Torres, during family visits, and recently called for Rocky by name across the backyard, which Hernán described as "the best thing I've heard all year." The family continues to prioritize bilingual language exposure and has asked that future sessions include more strategies for supporting Mateo's participation in group settings like the Wake County Smart Start playgroup and at Little Sprouts Daycare.

The team agreed to continue the current outcomes with revised criteria reflecting progress, to add a fourth outcome addressing group participation, and to reconvene for the next six-month review on March 16, 2027. All team members present, including Lucía Rodríguez, Hernán Cruz, Denise Walters, and Hannah Reyes, signed this plan on September 22, 2026, indicating agreement with the outcomes, strategies, and services described above. A copy of this plan was provided to the family in both English and Spanish, consistent with CDSA policy for families whose preferred language is Spanish.

Individualized Family Service Plan – Six-Month Review / Revisión del IFSP

This review was completed by Jennifer Lin, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC, in coordination with service coordinator Patricia Gómez-Reyes of the CDSA of Holly County. The meeting took place on September 22, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. in the home of the family.

Child: Mateo de la Cruz, called "Teo" at home, date of birth June 2, 2023, born at Holly County Regional Hospital at 38 weeks gestation, birth weight 3,100 grams, Apgar 8 and 9. Medicaid ID 987654321A; CDSA record number IFSP-2026-0442. The family resides at 482 Laurel Oak Lane, Pinebrook, Holly County, NC 27559. Parents are Lucía Vásquez-Ortiz (madre) and Andrés de la Cruz (padre). Andrés works at Pinebrook Poultry Processing, and the family can be reached at (910) 555-0148.

Preocupaciones y Prioridades de la Familia / Family Concerns: During the home visit, Lucía shared her concerns in her own words: "Yo quiero que Teo pueda decirme qué necesita sin frustrarse tanto — a veces llora porque no lo entendemos." She noted that his cousins at Early Head Start already speak in full sentences, and the comparison worries her. Andrés added, in English, "I just want him to be able to tell his teacher when something's wrong, en inglés o en español, no importa cuál." Both parents agreed that their top priority is functional communication at home and at daycare, followed by reducing Mateo's frustration-related tantrums, which Lucía described as "casi todos los días, cuando no me entiende lo que quiere."

Rutinas diarias: Mateo attends Sunbeam Bilingual Daycare four days a week, where Miss Ana leads his toddler classroom in the mornings and la maestra Carmen covers the afternoon shift. On Fridays he stays home with the family's neighbor, doña Lupe, whom the family describes as "como una abuela" for him. His older brother, Leo, age 4;2, attends the same daycare and often translates for Mateo with peers, telling his friends, "él quiere jugar también." The family also receives support from WIC and was recently connected to Smart Start for a parenting group. Mateo's evening routine includes bath, cuento, and a visit from the family dog before bed.

Standardized testing was completed on March 14, 2026 and repeated at this review on September 22, 2026:

PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension: Standard Score 73 (68-78, 95% CI), administered 03/14/2026.
PLS-5 Expressive Communication: Standard Score 70 (65-75, 95% CI), administered 03/14/2026.
CELF-5 Core Language Score: Standard Score 76 (71-81, 95% CI), re-administered 09/22/2026 at six-month review, showing growth from the 03/14/2026 baseline of 65 (60-70).

Speech-language services are billed under CPT 92523 and ICD-10 F80.2. Current services are 30-minute sessions, 2x/week, provided in the home and at Sunbeam Bilingual Daycare, beginning April 1, 2026 and continuing through this review.

During the language sample, Mateo produced several spontaneous utterances illustrating his current phonology and syntax. Shown a family photo, he pointed and said, "Rocky no aquí," reducing the final consonant cluster and omitting the copula; his target was "Rocky no está aquí." Later, looking at a drawing, he said, "Leo bike go," a three-word utterance lacking the article and verb inflection, coded [EW] for the omitted auxiliary. He also produced /k/ as [t] in "taza" for "casa," and substituted [w] for /r/ in several words, consistent with a phonological process affecting liquids. Spontaneous production accuracy for target consonants was 8/10 with mod cues, and he combined two words correctly in 3 of 5 opportunities.

Other agencies involved include DSS, which conducted a home visit on July 8, 2026 regarding the family's housing application, and Pinebrook Pediatric Clinic, where his primary care physician Dr. Omar Santos monitors his hearing screenings. His most recent audiological screening, conducted by audiologist Grace Ferreira-Lima, was within normal limits bilaterally. The family also sees occupational therapist Mr. Tom for sensory-related feeding concerns twice monthly.

Outcome 1: Mateo will use two- to three-word combinations to request and comment across home and daycare settings. Strategy: parents and Miss Ana will model expansion using Hanen "More Than Words" strategies during play and mealtime routines; Jennifer Lin will coach Lucía and Andrés in bilingual input strategies during home sessions, alternating target language by day to support both English and Spanish development without mixing cues within the same utterance.

Outcome 2: Mateo will reduce frustration-related behaviors by using a gesture or single word to request a break, in 4 of 5 observed opportunities. Strategy: implement a modified PECS exchange at daycare and home, introduced by Jennifer Lin and reinforced by la maestra Carmen during transitions; PROMPT tactile cueing will support jaw and lip placement for emerging bilabial sounds during structured snack time.

Outcome 3: Mateo will produce age-appropriate consonant clusters in single words with min cues, targeting /s/ clusters and final consonants. Strategy: weekly Cycles phonological approach sessions alternating target sound patterns, with home practice sheets sent in both languages so Lucía and Andrés can reinforce targets during bath and bedtime routines; doña Lupe will be given simplified cue cards for Friday practice.

Next steps include a referral evaluation for preschool special education services as Mateo approaches 36 months, with the transition conference tentatively scheduled for February 10, 2027. Patricia Gómez-Reyes will coordinate paperwork with CDSA of Holly County and notify the family's local school district contact once a placement team is assigned. The family's authorization for continued services runs through March 31, 2027, and the next IFSP review is scheduled for March 15, 2027 at 2:30 p.m.

The family expressed satisfaction with progress so far. Lucía remarked, "Ya veo que me entiende más, y eso me ayuda a no frustrarme yo tampoco." Andrés added that he has started narrating his routine at work in simple phrases over video calls so Mateo hears consistent modeling even when he is away. Mateo's brother, Leo, has also begun modeling slower, simplified sentences at Miss Ana's suggestion, which the family reports has reduced sibling conflict during play.

For questions regarding this report, contact Jennifer Lin at jlin@carolinabilingualtherapy.com or visit www.carolinabilingualtherapy.com for intake forms and bilingual resource handouts. The CDSA of Holly County can also be reached regarding service coordination questions at the number on file with the family.

This review reflects input gathered during the home visit, daycare observation, and parent interview, and was reviewed with the family in both English and Spanish before signatures were obtained. Copies were provided to the family, CDSA of Holly County, and Sunbeam Bilingual Daycare for the child's file.

Mateo continúa mostrando progreso lento pero constante en vocabulario expresivo y articulación de sonidos tempranos. Plan:
Continuar sesiones semanales de 45 minutos. Se recomienda seguimiento con la pediatra, Dra. Teresa Villanueva, para evaluación auditiva antes de la próxima revisión del IFSP, programada para el 12 de diciembre de 2026. Se enviará resumen a Lucía Hernández por correo electrónico y se coordinará con CDSA del Triángulo.

CAROLINA PEDIATRIC SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC
1420 Fairgrove Church Road, Hickory, NC 28601

COMPREHENSIVE SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION
Evaluación Integral del Habla y el Lenguaje

Client / Cliente: María José Hernández Soto ("Majo")
Date of Birth: April 2, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 3;9
Evaluation Dates: January 12, 2026 and January 14, 2026
Report Date: January 20, 2026
Record ID: CPSL-2026-0419
Medicaid ID: 882746100B
Referral Source: Monica Díaz, Service Coordinator, Catawba County Partnership for Children
Primary Caregivers: Carmen Soto Luna (madre/mother) and Javier Hernández Ramírez (padre/father)
Home Address: 212 Willow Bend Court, Claremont, NC 28610, Catawba County
Contact Phone: (828) 555-0932
Contact Email: csotoluna22@gmail.com
Primary Home Language: Spanish; secondary exposure: English
Evaluator: Rebecca Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP (bilingual Spanish/English clinician; no interpreter required)

RAZÓN PARA LA REMISIÓN / REASON FOR REFERRAL

Majo is a 3;9-year-old girl referred by Monica Díaz at the Catawba County Partnership for Children after her pediatrician, Dr. Patel at Catawba Valley Medical Center, raised concerns during her 3-year well-child visit about limited intelligibility in both of Majo's languages. Her mother, Carmen Soto Luna, reported, "no le entiendo casi nada cuando está cansada" (I barely understand her when she's tired), and her father, Javier Hernández Ramírez, added that teachers at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center have asked the family to "repeat everything she says" during drop-off. The family was also connected to this evaluation through Catawba County DSS, which referred them for WIC services last year and flagged the speech concern on a developmental screener.

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y MÉDICA / BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Majo was born at Catawba Valley Medical Center on April 2, 2022 at 38 weeks gestation via uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at one and five minutes, and birth weight was 6 lbs, 10 oz. Carmen reported no prenatal complications other than mild gestational hypertension managed with monitoring. Majo passed her newborn hearing screening and has had no recurrent ear infections, though she was diagnosed with two episodes of otitis media at age 18 months, treated with amoxicillin and resolved without tubes. A tympanogram completed by Dr. Patel's office on November 4, 2025 showed normal middle ear function bilaterally. No history of seizures, feeding difficulties, or significant illness. Majo's older brother, Mateo Hernández Soto ("Teo"), age 7, has a history of articulation therapy through his elementary school, which the family noted when asked about family history of speech-language concerns. There is no other reported family history of speech, language, hearing, or developmental disorders.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Majo lives at home with her parents, Carmen Soto Luna and Javier Hernández Ramírez, and her brother Teo. Her maternal grandmother, Rosa Soto Luna, lives nearby in Claremont and cares for Majo two afternoons a week when her parents work. The family's regular babysitter, Yolanda Martínez, also picks Majo up from daycare on Fridays. Majo is close with her cousins Juanito and Pepe, who visit most weekends, and the family's dog, Canela, who Carmen says "la sigue a todos lados" (follows her everywhere).

Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home; Javier reported, "en casa hablamos puro español, pero ella ya mezcla mucho inglés." Carmen works part-time at Valle Fresh Produce Distributors, and Javier is employed at Piedmont Steel Fabrication; both report using mostly Spanish with Majo and some English vocabulary learned from Teo's homework. Majo has attended Little Sprouts Early Learning Center in Hickory since age 2, where instruction is primarily in English. Her teacher, Ms. Davis, and the classroom aide, Srta. Pérez, both describe Majo as social and eager to communicate but difficult to understand, especially in multi-word utterances. Classmates Ashley and Kevin reportedly ask Majo to repeat herself frequently during play, and Carmen noted that Majo has started to say "no importa" and walk away rather than repeat unclear utterances.

Developmental milestones were reported as age-appropriate: Majo walked independently at 13 months, used her first words around 14 months, and began combining words around 26 months. Parents report she currently uses 3–4 word utterances in Spanish but struggles with grammatical markers and word-final consonants in both languages.

SESSION SCHEDULE / HORARIO DE SESIONES

Weekly direct therapy sessions were scheduled across two settings to accommodate the family's work hours and Majo's daycare schedule:

Day | Start Time | Stop Time | Location
Tuesday | 9:00 AM | 9:45 AM | 212 Willow Bend Court, Claremont (home)
Thursday | 1:30 PM | 2:15 PM | Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, Hickory
Saturday (biweekly) | 10:15 AM | 11:00 AM | Carolina Pediatric Speech & Language Services, PLLC clinic, Hickory

ASSESSMENT TOOLS ADMINISTERED

Standardized and informal measures were administered in both Spanish and English where appropriate, with order counterbalanced across sessions to reduce fatigue effects.

- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish and English editions
- Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool, Second Edition (CELF Preschool-2)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3)
- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA)
- Spontaneous language sample (SALT-coded), 50 utterances in Spanish and 30 in English
- Oral-motor and hearing screening

RESULTADOS / RESULTS

RECEPTIVE AND EXPRESSIVE LANGUAGE

On the PLS-5 Spanish edition, Majo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 82 (12th percentile; 95% confidence interval 76–88) and an Expressive Communication standard score of 79 (8th percentile; 95% confidence interval 73–85). Age equivalents were 2;11–3;2 for Auditory Comprehension and 2;8–2;11 for Expressive Communication. On the English edition, scores were lower, consistent with reduced exposure: Auditory Comprehension standard score 68 (2nd percentile), Expressive Communication standard score 65 (1st percentile).

Standard Score Table

Measure | Standard Score | Percentile | 95% CI | Age Equivalent
PLS-5 Spanish Auditory Comprehension | 82 | 12th | 76–88 | 2;11–3;2
PLS-5 Spanish Expressive Communication | 79 | 8th | 73–85 | 2;8–2;11
CELF Preschool-2 Core Language | 77 | 6th | 71–83 | 2;9–3;0
GFTA-3 Sounds-in-Words | 71 | 3rd | 65–77 | 2;6–2;10
BESA Semantics (Spanish-dominant) | 85 | 16th | 79–91 | 3;0–3;4

On the BESA, Majo demonstrated stronger performance in Spanish morphosyntax than English, correctly producing Spanish plural and gender agreement markers 8 of 10 trials but omitting English third-person singular -s in 9 of 10 opportunities. This pattern is consistent with typical bilingual acquisition rather than a primary language disorder, though both languages show delay relative to same-age peers.

SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION

On the GFTA-3, Majo scored at the 3rd percentile overall, with error patterns consistent across both languages: final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, and substitution of /ɾ/ for trilled /r/. During the language sample, Majo produced "peyo" for target "perro" (dog) and "ka" for target "casa" (house), omitting the final /s/. In English, she produced "do" for target "dog" and "ka" for target "cat", showing the same final-consonant deletion pattern cross-linguistically, which supports a true phonological disorder rather than typical second-language interference alone.

Interestingly, Majo referred to the family dog by name during the sample, saying "Canela vino" (Canela came) with the final /n/ intact, suggesting some variability by word familiarity and frequency.

Stimulability testing showed Majo could produce final consonants with moderate cues (verbal model plus visual cue) in 6 of 10 trials, and could approximate /r/ with maximal cues in 3 of 10 trials. She was stimulable for syllable-final /s/ with minimal cues in single words but not in connected speech.

ORAL-MOTOR AND HEARING

Oral-motor examination was within normal limits for structure and function. Majo passed a pure-tone hearing screening bilaterally at 20 dB across 500–4000 Hz.

PRAGMATICS AND SOCIAL COMMUNICATION

Majo initiated communication frequently and used eye contact, gesture, and joint attention appropriately. She showed frustration when unable to be understood, consistent with parent and teacher report, but no concerns were noted regarding social reciprocity or restricted/repetitive behavior.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Majo presents with a bilingual speech sound disorder and language delay affecting both Spanish and English, with error patterns and standard scores below expectations in both languages. Because deficits are present across both of her languages rather than limited to the less-dominant one, this pattern is consistent with a true communication disorder rather than a difference attributable solely to second-language acquisition or dialectal variation. Majo meets criteria for speech and language services under ICD-10 codes F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder).

Given Majo's young age, bilingual environment, and the family's strong use of Spanish at home, intervention should be delivered in both languages, with primary emphasis on Spanish given its role as the dominant home language and the language in which Majo's grandmother, Rosa, and babysitter, Yolanda, primarily interact with her.

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Individual speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, targeting phonological processes (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction) and expressive morphosyntax in both Spanish and English, billed under CPT 92507.
2. Initial evaluation billed under CPT 92523 (speech sound production and language evaluation).
3. A Cycles phonological approach is recommended given the number and consistency of error patterns identified.
4. Continued coordination with Monica Díaz at the Catawba County Partnership for Children regarding Early Intervention eligibility and IFSP Outcome 2 (communication) development.
5. Classroom-based strategies for Ms. Davis and Srta. Pérez at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, including modeling full-word productions and allowing extra response time.
6. Home strategies for Carmen and Javier, including modeling target sounds in context rather than correcting Majo directly, and encouraging extended family members such as Rosa and Yolanda to maintain rich Spanish language input.
7. Re-evaluation in 6 months to monitor progress across both languages.
8. Referral to Catawba County DSS and WIC services, which the family is already connected with, to ensure continuity of support services.

This evaluation was conducted in accordance with best practices for bilingual assessment, using normed tools in both of Majo's languages and considering her full linguistic repertoire rather than evaluating English proficiency alone.

Respectfully submitted,

Rebecca Ortiz, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

This Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) review was completed for José Luis Hernández Martínez, known at home as "Pepe," who was born on April 9, 2024 and is currently 2;6. Pepe lives with his parents, Lucía Martínez Reyes and Hernán Hernández Ruiz, and his older sister, Guadalupe Hernández Martínez, called "Lupita," at 412 Willow Creek Lane in Mebane, Alamance County, NC 27302. The family's Medicaid ID for Pepe is 987654321B, and this review corresponds to IFSP record IFSP-00417-2026. The review meeting took place on September 22, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. in the family's living room, with service coordinator Diana López of Agencia de Coordinación Familiar Esperanza y Vida (short form ACFEV), operating under contract with the Piedmont CDSA office, present for the full hour.

Pepe's day begins around 6:45 a.m., when his mother wakes him and his sister for breakfast, usually eggs and tortillas at the kitchen table by 7:15 a.m.. His grandmother, Rosa Reyes, who lives two streets over, comes by most mornings to help get Lupita ready for school and to watch Pepe while Lucía drives her to the bus stop. Hernán leaves for his shift at Sunrise Poultry Processing by 6:30 a.m. and is usually home again by 4:00 p.m.. On weekday mornings Pepe attends Little Scholars Bilingual Daycare from 8:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., where his teacher, Ana Pérez, reports that he plays well alongside classmates Juanito Pérez and Teo Flores but rarely initiates words during group time, often watching from the edge of the rug instead of joining in. The family's dog, Canela, sleeps in Pepe's room and is, according to Lucía, "the only one who gets him to point and babble without being asked." Pepe naps most days from about 1:30 p.m. to 3:00 p.m., has a bath around 5:30 p.m., and the family eats dinner together near 6:30 p.m. before bedtime routines start close to 8:00 p.m.

During the review, Lucía shared her priorities in her own words: "Yo quiero que Pepe me pueda decir lo que necesita sin llorar tanto. A veces no sé si tiene hambre o si le duele algo." Hernán added, "Para mí lo más importante es que aprenda a jugar con otros niños, porque en la guardería se queda solo." Both parents agreed that their top priority remains helping Pepe communicate basic wants and needs at home and at daycare without resorting to crying or hitting his head against the couch, followed by increasing his play interactions with peers, and continuing to build his skills in both Spanish and English since the household is primarily Spanish-speaking and the parents want him equally comfortable in both languages before he starts preschool.

The family remains connected to several community supports. They attend Sunday services at Iglesia Bautista Nueva Esperanza, where Pepe's grandmother sometimes brings him to the nursery room while the rest of the family is in service. The family also participates in the bilingual story-time program at Cedar Grove Public Library on Tuesday afternoons, and Lucía recently enrolled in a parenting class through Centro Comunitario Nueva Vida, a nonprofit that also connected the family to WIC services and a Smart Start home-visiting program. Carmen Martínez, Lucía's sister, occasionally babysits on weekends and has learned several of Pepe's signs so she can communicate with him when the parents are out.

Developmentally, Pepe's most recent assessment used the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5) Spanish-English bilingual protocol, administered August 14, 2026. He obtained a standard score of 68 on Auditory Comprehension (percentile 2nd) and a standard score of 65 on Expressive Communication (percentile 1st), yielding an age equivalent range of 11-14 months against his chronological age. His gestational age at birth was 38 weeks, birth weight 6 lbs 4 oz, with an Apgar score of 8 and 9. Pepe currently uses approximately 12 single words consistently across both languages, including "mamá," "más," and "up," and produces the sounds /m/ and /p/ in isolation but omits most final consonants, as in "ba" for "bath." He responds to simple one-step directions with moderate cues about 3 of 5 trials, and a caregiver questionnaire of social communication skills placed him in the 5th percentile for his age.

Three outcomes were reviewed and continued with updated strategies. Outcome 1: Pepe will use two-word combinations to request preferred items and activities at home and daycare. Strategies include modeling two-word phrases during snack and play routines, using a core vocabulary board in both languages, and prompting with min to mod cues during structured play. Outcome 2: Pepe will increase joint attention and turn-taking with peers during a shared activity for at least 3 consecutive turns. Strategies include Hanen-based coaching for Lucía and Hernán during home visits, modeling parallel play narration in the home, and a visual turn-taking cue at daycare supported by Ana Pérez during centers time. Outcome 3: Pepe will imitate final consonants in single words with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive sessions, supported by articulation drills using PROMPT tactile cueing, bath-time sound play, and weekly home practice sheets sent in Spanish so both parents can carry over the targets consistently.

Speech-language services continue at a frequency of one 45-minute home visit per week, typically scheduled from 3:30 p.m. to 4:15 p.m. on Wednesdays, delivered jointly in Spanish and English depending on the family's preference that day. Pepe's pediatrician, Dr. Samuel Ortiz, was consulted by phone prior to this review regarding a recent ear infection, and no additional medical barriers to therapy were identified at this time. Service coordinator Diana López can be reached at (336) 555-0148 or dlopez@acfev-nc.org for scheduling questions, and families can review program information at www.piedmontcdsa.nc.gov. The next IFSP review is scheduled for March 20, 2027, six months from this meeting, unless concerns warrant an earlier visit.

This review was completed and documented by Maritza Gómez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC, contracted through the Piedmont CDSA office to provide early intervention services to the family. All strategies above were reviewed with the family in Spanish, and both parents confirmed understanding through return demonstration before the end of the visit on September 22, 2026.

North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program — Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) Review
Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia — Revisión Semestral

Child / Niño: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Rodríguez ("Teo")
Date of Birth / Fecha de nacimiento: January 14, 2024
Age at review / Edad en la revisión: 2;8
Medicaid ID: 7284910335J
Case ID: CDSA-21847
CDSA Office / Oficina de CDSA: Centro de Desarrollo y Servicios para Niños del Área de Piedmont Central (CDSA Piedmont Central)
Service Coordinator / Coordinadora de Servicios: Maria Elena Gutiérrez, Coordinación de Servicios Familiares del Condado de Durham (CSF Durham)
IFSP Review Meeting Date / Fecha de la reunión: September 9, 2026
Report Written By / Informe escrito por: Ana Torres, M.S., CCC-SLP, Pequeños Pasos Pediatric Therapy Services
Home Address / Dirección: 412 Larkspur Lane, Durham, NC 27705
Mother / Madre: Lucía Rodríguez Peña
Father / Padre: Héctor Cruz Martínez

Contact table / Tabla de contactos:
Name	Role	Phone	Email
Lucía Rodríguez Peña	Mother/Madre	(919) 555-0148	lucia.rodriguezpena@mailnest.com
Héctor Cruz Martínez	Father/Padre	(919) 555-0162	hcruzmartinez@workmail.com
Maria Elena Gutiérrez	Service Coordinator/Coordinadora	(919) 555-0120	mgutierrez@csfdurham.org
Ana Torres	SLP/Patóloga del Habla	(919) 555-0199	atorres@pequenospasos.org
Dr. James Okafor	Pediatrician/Pediatra	(919) 555-0177	jokafor@durhampeds.com

Family Information / Información de la Familia

Teo lives at home with his parents, Lucía and Héctor, his older sister Sol (5 years old), and the family's dog, Rocky. The family is bilingual, and Lucía reports that the home language mix is "mitad y mitad, pero más español con los abuelos." Lucía works part-time at Triangle Linen Services, and Héctor is employed at Carrboro Millwork. Sol attends kindergarten at Hope Valley Elementary, and Teo attends three mornings a week at Centro de Cuidado Infantil Little Sprouts.

Family Concerns and Priorities / Preocupaciones y Prioridades Familiares

During the review, Lucía shared, "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no pide las cosas con palabras — señala, o nos lleva de la mano. Solo dice unas pocas palabras, como 'mamá' y 'agua.'" She added, "Él entiende mucho más de lo que dice, en los dos idiomas." Héctor noted, "I want him to be able to tell his teacher at daycare what he needs, in English or in Spanish, doesn't matter, just so he's not frustrated." Lucía also said, "Su hermana Sol lo entiende perfecto, pero con los demás es difícil." The family's top priority remains functional communication at home and at daycare, followed by continued fine and gross motor progress.

Daily Routines / Rutinas Diarias

Teo wakes around 7:00 a.m. and eats breakfast with Sol before she leaves for school. He attends Little Sprouts from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Afternoons are spent at home with Lucía, who reports that bath time and playing with Rocky in the backyard are Teo's favorite routines. Lucía shared, "Cuando saca la pelota para Rocky, Teo se emociona mucho y grita." Dinner is a shared family routine at 6:00 p.m., and Héctor reads bedtime stories in English while Lucía sings lullabies in Spanish.

Evaluation Summary / Resumen de la Evaluación

Teo was assessed using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4 (Bayley-4), the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), and the Peabody Developmental Motor Scales-2 (PDMS-2). Testing was conducted in both English and Spanish, with items presented bilingually per Lucía's report of home language exposure.

Score table / Tabla de puntajes:
Measure	Domain	Standard Score	Percentile	Age Equivalent
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale	Receptive Language	--	9th	18-20 months
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale	Expressive Language	--	3rd	14-16 months
Bayley-4	Cognitive	91	27th	--
Bayley-4	Fine Motor	88	21st	--
GFTA-3	Sounds-in-Words	79	8th	--
PDMS-2	Gross Motor Quotient	94	34th	--

On the GFTA-3, Teo produced several early sounds with moderate cues. He imitated the target word "sol" (sun) during the picture-naming task, reducing the final consonant cluster and producing [so]. Of note, during spontaneous play with Rocky's ball, Teo separately said, "Sol pelota," referring to his sister rather than the test item — the clinician flagged this distinction in session notes, since the target word and the sibling's name are homophones. He also said, "Rocky afuera," reaching toward the back door. Expressively, Teo produces 8-10 single words and no two-word combinations; receptively, he follows 2 of 5 two-step directions and identifies 9 of 10 body parts when named in Spanish.

Other Agencies Involved / Otras Agencias Involucradas

The family also receives support from WIC for nutrition services and participates in a Smart Start parenting group. Lucía reported an open case with Durham County DSS related to a prior housing assistance application, unrelated to Teo's services. The family's pediatrician, Dr. James Okafor of Durham Pediatric Associates, continues to monitor Teo's growth and hearing status; his most recent audiological screening at UNC Children's Hospital on August 3, 2026 showed results within normal limits bilaterally.

Outcomes and Strategies / Resultados y Estrategias

Outcome 1: Teo will use 2-3 word combinations to request preferred items and activities in English or Spanish across home and daycare settings.
Strategies: Ana Torres will model expansion using Hanen "It Takes Two to Talk" strategies during biweekly home visits. Lucía and Héctor will practice following Teo's lead and pausing expectantly before offering preferred items, both in Spanish and English, including during play with Rocky and with Sol.

Outcome 2: Teo will increase intelligibility of early-developing consonants (/m/, /b/, /p/, /s/) in single words across 3 of 5 opportunities with minimal cues.
Strategies: Ana Torres will use a modified Cycles approach targeting final consonants in both languages. Home practice will embed target sounds in daily routines; Lucía noted, "Podemos practicar con las palabras de la rutina, como 'más' y 'pan.'"

Outcome 3: Teo will demonstrate improved fine motor coordination for self-feeding and simple manipulatives during meals and play.
Strategies: Occupational therapy consultation will continue monthly; Héctor will incorporate utensil practice during dinner routines.

Outcome 4: The family will access respite or childcare support resources to reduce caregiver stress, per Lucía's report, "A veces necesitamos un descanso, especialmente cuando Sol también necesita atención."
Strategies: Maria Elena Gutiérrez will provide a referral list for respite care through CDSA Piedmont Central and connect the family with the Smart Start parenting group coordinator.

Service Schedule / Horario de Servicios

Service	Provider	Frequency	Location	Start Date
Speech-Language Therapy	Ana Torres	60 min, biweekly	Home	October 1, 2026
Occupational Therapy	Rachel Simms	45 min, monthly	Home	October 15, 2026
Developmental Service Coordination	Maria Elena Gutiérrez	Quarterly	Home/CDSA Piedmont Central	January 14, 2026
Audiology Follow-up	UNC Children's Hospital	Annual	Clinic	August 3, 2027

Transition Planning / Planificación de Transición

As Teo approaches his third birthday, the team discussed transition planning. Lucía stated, "Queremos que siga con apoyo cuando empiece preescolar, porque Sol tuvo mucha ayuda al principio y le fue muy bien." A transition conference will be scheduled no later than 90 days prior to Teo's third birthday, per North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program requirements, to coordinate with Durham Public Schools Exceptional Children's Services for a preschool eligibility determination.

PLAN DE SERVICIOS FAMILIARES INDIVIDUALIZADO (IFSP) — INFORME DE REVISIÓN
Programa de Intervención Temprana del Infante y Niño Pequeño de Carolina del Norte

Preparado por: Terapias Pediátricas Esperanza, PLLC
Patóloga del habla y lenguaje: Lic. Fernanda Ortiz, CCC-SLP

1. INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN DEL NIÑO Y LA FAMILIA

Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro del Río Castillo
Apodo usado en casa: Teo
Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de enero de 2023
Número de expediente del CDSA: CDSA-48213-NC
Número de Medicaid: 9284716203A
Dirección de la familia: 412 Calle Hortensia, Mebane, condado de Alamance, Carolina del Norte, 27302
Teléfono de contacto principal: (336) 555-0148
Correo electrónico de la familia: familiadelrio23@correoweb.com

Oficina del CDSA que coordina el caso: CDSA del Triángulo Central
Coordinadora de servicios: Karen Suárez
Fecha de esta revisión del IFSP: 2 de octubre de 2026
Fecha del IFSP inicial: 15 de marzo de 2025
Fecha de la revisión anterior: 20 de abril de 2026
Próxima revisión programada: 2 de abril de 2027

2. INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR

Mateo vive en el domicilio familiar con su madre, Daniela Castillo-Mendoza, y su padre, Joaquín del Río. Su hermana mayor, Camila del Río, tiene seis años y asiste a la escuela primaria del vecindario. La familia también cuenta con el apoyo frecuente de la abuela materna de Mateo, Rosa Martínez, quien lo cuida dos tardes por semana mientras sus padres trabajan. Un primo adolescente, Esteban Castillo, a veces ayuda a llevar a Mateo a sus citas cuando Daniela no puede salir del trabajo.

Daniela trabaja como supervisora de turno en Procesadora de Alimentos Monte Verde, y Joaquín trabaja como capataz en Construcciones Hermanos Paredes. Ambos padres hablan español en casa como idioma principal; Joaquín también habla inglés de manera limitada. Camila es bilingüe y a menudo traduce para Mateo cuando juegan con vecinos de habla inglesa.

3. ANTECEDENTES DEL DESARROLLO Y MÉDICOS

Mateo nació en Hospital Comunitario de Alamance a las 37 semanas de gestación, con un peso al nacer de 2,890 gramos y puntuaciones de Apgar de 8 y 9. Permaneció 3 días en observación neonatal por dificultad leve para alimentarse, sin complicaciones posteriores reportadas.

El pediatra de Mateo, Dr. Benjamín Alvarado, remitió a la familia al CDSA después de notar, durante la revisión de los 18 meses, que Mateo tenía un vocabulario expresivo muy limitado. En ese momento, a la edad de 18 meses, Mateo producía menos de 5 palabras inteligibles. A los 34 meses, edad actual, su madre reporta un vocabulario expresivo de aproximadamente 40 a 50 palabras, principalmente en español.

Mateo fue diagnosticado con un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo y expresivo, código F80.2, por Dr. Alvarado en coordinación con el equipo de intervención temprana. No se reportan antecedentes de convulsiones, pérdida auditiva confirmada ni hospitalizaciones adicionales. Una prueba de audición realizada el 9 de febrero de 2025 resultó dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos.

4. PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en palabras de la familia)

Durante la entrevista de revisión, Daniela expresó: "Nos preocupa que Mateo se frustre mucho cuando no lo entendemos. Grita o jala nuestra ropa en vez de usar palabras, y a veces llora por minutos enteros porque no sabemos qué quiere."

Joaquín añadió: "Queremos que pueda ir al kínder normal cuando le toque. Nos preocupa que, si sigue atrasado con el habla, los demás niños no lo entiendan y se quede atrás en todo lo demás también."

La prioridad principal de la familia es que Mateo desarrolle suficiente lenguaje funcional para comunicarse con la familia, los compañeros en su centro preescolar y el personal médico. La familia también solicitó estrategias bilingües específicas, ya que el hogar es predominantemente hispanohablante, pero el entorno preescolar de Mateo es mayormente de habla inglesa.

5. RUTINAS DIARIAS Y CONTEXTOS NATURALES

Mateo asiste de lunes a viernes, de 7:30 a.m. a 4:00 p.m., al centro preescolar Los Caracoles Felices, ubicado cerca del domicilio familiar. Su maestra principal es la Sra. Vásquez, quien reporta que Mateo interactúa poco verbalmente con sus compañeros de clase, entre ellos Emma y Lucas, aunque disfruta del juego físico y de las actividades musicales en grupo.

En casa, la rutina matutina incluye el desayuno a las 6:45 a.m., seguido de la preparación para salir al centro preescolar. Rosa Martínez recoge a Mateo los martes y jueves alrededor de las 4:15 p.m. y lo cuida hasta que Daniela o Joaquín regresan del trabajo, usualmente antes de las 6:30 p.m..

Durante las comidas familiares, Mateo se sienta con Camila y a menudo imita sus gestos y sonidos. La madre reporta un momento reciente en que, al jugar con su amigo en el parque, Mateo repitió el nombre de su compañero y dijo "Lucas, ven" con articulación clara, lo cual la familia consideró un avance notable.

6. OTRAS AGENCIAS Y PROGRAMAS COMUNITARIOS INVOLUCRADOS

Además del CDSA, la familia recibe apoyo de WIC para asistencia nutricional y de Smart Start del condado de Alamance para subsidio parcial de la matrícula preescolar de Mateo. La familia también fue conectada recientemente con la Alianza Comunitaria para el Desarrollo Infantil Temprano (ACDIT), una organización sin fines de lucro que ofrece grupos de apoyo en español para padres de niños con retrasos en el desarrollo. La coordinadora de servicios, Karen Suárez, refirió a la familia a la ACDIT después de que Daniela mencionara sentirse aislada de otras familias en situaciones similares.

El Departamento de Servicios Sociales (DSS) del condado también mantiene contacto breve con la familia debido a una solicitud previa de asistencia con vivienda, aunque esa gestión no está directamente relacionada con los servicios de intervención temprana de Mateo.

7. EVALUACIONES FORMALES Y RESULTADOS

Para esta revisión se administraron las siguientes evaluaciones estandarizadas en español e inglés según corresponda:

a) Escala Rossetti de Lenguaje Infantil (Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale): Mateo obtuvo un desempeño equivalente a una edad de 18-20 meses en el área receptiva y de 14-16 meses en el área expresiva, en comparación con su edad cronológica actual de 34 meses. Esto representa una discrepancia significativa entre su edad cronológica y su desempeño lingüístico.

b) Prueba Goldman-Fristoe de Articulación-3 (Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3): puntuación estándar de 76, lo cual lo ubica en el percentil 6. Los errores incluyeron sustituciones consistentes del sonido /k/ por [t] y omisión de consonantes finales, como en la producción ""pato"" por ""plato"".

c) Escalas Bayley de Desarrollo Infantil-4 (Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4), subprueba de comunicación: puntuación compuesta de 79 (IC 73-85), percentil 8, clasificada como rango bajo.

d) Prueba Peabody de Vocabulario en Imágenes (Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test), versión en español: puntuación estándar de 80, edad equivalente de 2;4.

En tareas informales de seguimiento de instrucciones de dos pasos en español, Mateo respondió correctamente en 8/10 ensayos (80%), lo cual representa una mejora comparado con 4/10 ensayos en la evaluación inicial. En producción de palabras funcionales de uso diario, logró imitar correctamente 6 de 10 palabras objetivo con claves verbales mínimas.

Las sesiones de evaluación y tratamiento se documentaron bajo los códigos de procedimiento 92523 (evaluación de habla y lenguaje) y 92507 (tratamiento individual de habla y lenguaje), con el modificador GN correspondiente a servicios proporcionados por patología del habla-lenguaje.

8. RESULTADOS (OUTCOMES) DEL IFSP Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Mateo usará de 30 a 50 palabras funcionales de manera espontánea en el hogar y en el centro preescolar para pedir objetos, rechazar actividades y comentar sobre su entorno, medido mediante registro de vocabulario de los padres y observación directa.

Estrategias: Se implementará el enfoque Hanen con los padres para fomentar la expansión del lenguaje durante las rutinas naturales. Daniela y Joaquín recibirán entrenamiento mensual en técnicas de estimulación del lenguaje durante las comidas y el juego. Lic. Fernanda Ortiz coordinará con la Sra. Vásquez para reforzar el mismo vocabulario objetivo en el centro preescolar Los Caracoles Felices.

Resultado 2: Mateo producirá los sonidos /k/, /g/ y consonantes finales con 80% de precisión en palabras de una y dos sílabas, medido mediante muestras de habla grabadas y análisis de producción.

Estrategias: Se utilizará un enfoque de Ciclos (Cycles) con énfasis en estructura de sílaba y patrones fonológicos, con sesiones semanales individuales de 30 minutos conducidas en español por Lic. Fernanda Ortiz. Se incorporarán símbolos visuales del sistema PECS como apoyo complementario durante momentos de alta frustración comunicativa.

Resultado 3: La familia identificará y usará al menos tres estrategias de comunicación aumentativa (gestos, señalar, imágenes) durante momentos de frustración en el hogar, reduciendo los episodios de llanto prolongado reportados por los padres.

Estrategias: Lic. Fernanda Ortiz proporcionará modelado directo durante visitas domiciliarias y revisará el progreso con Karen Suárez en cada contacto de coordinación de servicios. La fisioterapeuta del equipo, Lic. Patricia Núñez, también observará las transiciones motoras gruesas durante el juego, ya que estas a veces preceden los episodios de frustración comunicativa.

9. RESUMEN DE SERVICIOS Y FECHAS

Terapia de habla y lenguaje individual: dos sesiones semanales de 30 minutos cada una, en el hogar de la familia, conducidas en español por Lic. Fernanda Ortiz, bajo el código 92507. Fecha de inicio de este ciclo de servicio: 10 de octubre de 2026. Fecha de finalización proyectada: 9 de abril de 2027.

Visita de coordinación de servicios: una visita mensual realizada por Karen Suárez, con la próxima visita programada para el 6 de noviembre de 2026 a las 10:00 a.m. en el domicilio familiar.

Consulta de fisioterapia: una sesión mensual de 45 minutos con Lic. Patricia Núñez, iniciando el 15 de octubre de 2026.

Consulta médica de seguimiento: cita programada con Dr. Benjamín Alvarado el 3 de diciembre de 2026 a las 2:30 p.m. para revisar el progreso general del desarrollo.

10. PARTICIPANTES EN ESTA REVISIÓN DEL IFSP

Los siguientes participaron en la reunión de revisión celebrada el 2 de octubre de 2026 en las oficinas del CDSA del Triángulo Central:

- Daniela Castillo-Mendoza, madre
- Joaquín del Río, padre
- Karen Suárez, coordinadora de servicios
- Lic. Fernanda Ortiz, patóloga del habla y lenguaje, Terapias Pediátricas Esperanza, PLLC
- Lic. Patricia Núñez, fisioterapeuta pediátrica

11. ACUERDO Y FIRMAS

La familia de Mateo Alejandro del Río Castillo acepta los resultados y estrategias descritos en este documento y confirma su participación continua en el proceso de intervención temprana.

Este informe se archivará en el expediente del CDSA bajo el número CDSA-48213-NC y en el sistema de registros del Medicaid de Carolina del Norte bajo el número 9284716203A. Cualquier pregunta sobre este plan puede dirigirse a la coordinadora de servicios, Karen Suárez, al (336) 555-0291 o por correo a ksuarez@cdsatriangulocentral.org.

+ Name: Mateo Alejandro Ríos
+ CA: 3;10
+ Context: Sesión individual de terapia del habla y lenguaje en el hogar, con la madre presente.

Resumen:

Mateo llegó alerta y cooperador. Su mamá, Carmen Ríos, comentó que esta semana fue difícil porque ella trabaja el turno de noche en UPS y además limpia casas los fines de semana, así que Mateo estuvo al cuidado de su abuela, Dolores Ríos, y de su hermana mayor, Luz, quien lo ayuda con la tarea y lo lleva al parque.

S: La mamá reporta que Mateo dijo espontáneamente "quiero agua" y que su producción del fonema /r/ mejoró en casa. También mencionó que la cita de seguimiento con audiología en Novant Health Pediatric ENT & Audiology, Campus Huntersville quedó para el 12 de noviembre de 2026 a las 2:30 p.m.

O: Trabajamos vocabulario funcional usando el enfoque de Hanen. En 8/10 ensayos, Mateo combinó dos palabras con claves moderadas. Produjo el fonema /k/ en posición inicial en 7 de 10 intentos, mejor que el 40% documentado el 3 de octubre de 2026. Revisamos la meta IFSP #2 de comunicación expresiva. También practicó el objetivo "más jugo" con apoyo visual.
